15.he: הַנְּעָרוֹת בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁגּוֹדְלוֹת רֹאשָׁן מוֹשִׁיבוֹת אוֹתָן בְּתוֹךְ יַם נָפָה, לְקַבֵּל שָׁם מַה שֶּׁיִּפֹּל מֵרֹאשָׁן מִן הָעַפְרוּרִית וְעִרְבּוּבִיתָא דְרֵישָׁא. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
15.en: the young women who have their heads dressed they place them within the receiver of flour at sifting or in the mill, to receive what might fall from their heads from the sandy matter in grain and the tangles and scabs of the head formed through uncleanliness. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yehuda.

15.he: הָעֲשׂוּיִין לַכְּלִי לִתְלוֹתוֹ בּוֹ:
15.en: that are made for a utensil/vessel to hang upon it. כברת גרנות

15.he: דַּהֲווּ חִבּוּר לַכְּלִי:
15.en: because they are an attachment to the vessel.

15.he: עֲשׂוּיָה לְהוֹצִיא הַחִטִּים וְלִקְלֹט הַמֹּץ, וּמַנִּיחִים הַכְּבָרָה עַל שְׁנֵי עֵצִים וּמְנַהֲלִין, וּכְשֶׁהֵן יְגֵעִים מַכְנִיסִים יְדֵיהֶן בַּתְּלוֹי שֶׁלָּהּ וּמְנַהֲלִין, וְהַיְנוּ דְקָתָנֵי דִמְסַיְּעִין בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה:
15.en: that is made to remove the wheat and to retain the chaff, and they place the sieve on two pieces of wood and sift it, and when they are tired, they put their hands on its hanger and sift, which is what it teaches [in the Mishnah] that they assist at the time of work.

15.he: הַמְחַפְּשִׂין בְּתוֹךְ הַכֵּלִים לִרְאוֹת אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ דָבָר שֶׁרָאוּי לִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ מֶכֶס לַמֶּלֶךְ. תַּרְגּוּם וַיְחַפֵּשׂ, וּבְלַשׁ:
15.en: that he searches within the vessels to see if there is something appropriate to give from it as a taxes to the king. The Aramaic translation of “and he searches” is ובלש/and he searches, examines [for concealed goods].

15.he: מַכְנִיסִין יְדֵיהֶם בַּתְּלוֹי כְּשֶׁרוֹצִים לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בַּכְּלִי, וּמִסְתַּיְּעִים בּוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתָּן. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:
15.en: they bring their hands in on something hanging when they want to use a vessel, and they support with it to perform their work. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.

15.he: שֶׁזּוֹרִים בָּהּ תְּבוּאָה וְקִטְנִיּוֹת. בַּעֲרָבִי אלרח"ה, וּבְלַעַ"ז פאל"א:
15.en: that they winnow the grain and beans with. In Arabic it is ALRAKHA, and in the foreign tongue PALA.

15.he: הָעוֹשִׂים גְּרִיסִים שֶׁל פּוֹל:
15.en: that make pounded beans.

15.he: לְפִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל וַעֲשׂוּיָה לְהַכְנִיס בָּהּ לָרֵחַיִם:
15.en: because it has a receptacle and is made to be entered into millstone.

15.he: עֲשׂוּיָה לִלְקֹט בָּהּ הַחִטָּה שֶׁהִיא מִן הַצְּדָדִים מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן. וּלְנַקּוֹתָהּ שֶׁתִּתְיַשֵּׁב בָּאוֹצָר:
15.en: made to collect in it the wheat which is from the sides from here and there, and to cleanse it when it settles in the storeroom.

15.he: לְהַשְׁלִיךְ הַחַרְצַנִּים וְהַזָּגִין חוּץ מִן הַגַּת:
15.en: to cast off the shells of grapes and the pomace of grapes outside of the winepress.

15.he: מִמְּקוֹם פְּזוּרָן, אֲבָל לֹא לְקַבֵּל בְּתוֹכוֹ:
15.en: from the place of their scattering, but not to receive into it.

15.he: נְבָלִים שֶׁמְּשׁוֹרְרִים בָּהֶם. לְשׁוֹן נֵבֶל וְכִנּוֹר:
15.en: harps that they sing with them. The language of lyre and harp (i.e., secular music).

15.he: שֶׁהַנְּבָלִים וְהַכִּנּוֹרוֹת חֲלוּלִים הֵם וּמְנֻקָּבִים לְצַד הַנִּימִין לְהַשְׁמִיעַ קוֹל הַנִּגּוּן, וְדֶרֶךְ הַמְנַגְּנִים לְהַנִּיחַ בְּתוֹכָן הַמָּעוֹת שֶׁמְּקַבְּצִין מִבְּנֵי אָדָם הַבָּאִים לִשְׁמֹעַ, וְהָוֵי לֵיהּ מִטַּלְטֵל מָלֵא וְרֵיקָן:
15.en: that the lyres and harps are profane and are perforated to the side of the strings in order to produce the sound of the melody. And it is the manner of those of play to leave within them the money that they collect from people who come to listen. And it is carried both full and empty.

15.he: הַמְּנַגְּנִים עַל הַדּוּכָן:
15.en: who play on the platform [of the Temple].

15.he: שֶׁאֵינָן עֲשׂוּיִין לָתֵת בְּתוֹכָן מָעוֹת, וְאֵין עֲשׂוּיִין לְקַבֵּל:
15.en: they are not made to place money in them, and they are not made to receive anything.

15.he: כָּל אֶחָד מִשִּׁבְעָה מַשְׁקִין, שֶׁהֵן, מַיִם יַיִן שֶׁמֶן דְּבַשׁ חָלָב דַּם טַל, מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה, וּמַכְשִׁירִין הַזְּרָעִים לְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה:
15.en: each one of the seven liquids which are water, wine, oil, honey, milk, blood [and] dew, are susceptible to receive ritual defilement, and make fit the seeds to receive ritual defilement.

15.he: הַמַּיִם וְהַדָּם שֶׁבְּבֵית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִם שֶׁבָּעֲזָרָה:
15.en: the water and the blood that are in the slaughterhouse that is in the Temple courtyard.

15.he: שֶׁהֵם אֵינָם מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה, וְלֹא מַכְשִׁירִין הָאֳכָלִים לְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה:

לְפִי שֶׁבִּתְחִלָּה הָיוּ מַצְנִיעִים אֳכָלִים שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה אֵצֶל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה, דְּאָמְרֵי הַאי קֹדֶשׁ וְהַאי קֹדֶשׁ, כֵּיוָן דְּחָזוּ דְקָאָתוּ סְפָרִים לִידֵי פְסֵידָא, שֶׁהָעַכְבָּרִים שֶׁהָיוּ מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל הָאֳכָלִים הָיוּ מַפְסִידִים אוֹתָן, גָּזְרוּ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַסְּפָרִים כָּל כִּתְבֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ פּוֹסְלִים אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה בְמַגָּעָן, וְגָזְרוּ עוֹד שֶׁהַיָּדַיִם הַנּוֹגְעוֹת בַּסְּפָרִים יִהְיוּ שְׁנִיּוֹת לַטֻּמְאָה וּפוֹסְלוֹת אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה:
15.en: because at the outset, they would hide the food of the heave-offering with the Torah scrolls, for they said: “this is holy, and that is holy,” since they saw that these Scrolls came to a loss, that the mice that would be found near the foods would cause loss to them, they (i.e., the Sages) decreed that all Scrolls of all Holy Writings defile the heave-offering through their contact, they decreed further that the hands that touch the Scrolls would be second-level of ritual defilement and would invalidate the heave-offering [for the Kohanim].

15.he: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל קוֹרֵא בוֹ בְּעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים. דְּלֵיכָּא לְמֵיחַשׁ שֶׁמָּא יָשִׂימוּ אֳכָלִים שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה אֶצְלוֹ, מִפְּנֵי מוֹרָאוֹ וַחֲשִׁיבוּתוֹ:
15.en: The Torah scroll that the High Priest reads from in the Women’s Court on Yom Kippur, for one should not be concerned lest they place food-stuffs of heave-offering near it, because of his fear and its importance.

15.he: סוּס שֶׁל עֵץ שֶׁעוֹשִׂים הַלֵּיצָנִים לִרְכֹּב עָלָיו לְצַחֵק בּוֹ:
15.en: a wooden horse that the jesters/scoffers make to ride upon to make fun of.

15.he: כְּלִי נִגּוּן גָּדוֹל, שֶׁהַמְנַגֵּן בּוֹ סוֹמְכוֹ עַל בִּטְנוֹ. וְקוֹרִים לוֹ בְּלַעַ"ז ציטר"א:
15.en: a large musical instrument, that the player rests on his stomach. And they call it TZITRA in the foreign language.

15.he: מִין כְּלִי שֶׁל נִגּוּן עָשׂוּי בְּצוּרַת רֶגֶל שֶׁל עֵץ שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה מִי שֶׁנֶּחְתְּכָה רַגְלוֹ:
15.en: a kind of musical instrument made in the form of a leg of wood that a person makes whose leg was cut/severed.

15.he: עָשׂוּי כְּמִין נָפָה שֶׁדָּפְנוֹתֶיהָ עֲגֻלּוֹת וְשׁוֹטְחִין עַל פִּיו עוֹר דַּק, וּמַכִּין עָלָיו בְּמַקֵּל וּמוֹצִיא קוֹל צָלוּל. וּבְלַעַ"ז טמבור"ו:
15.en: made like a kind of sieve whose walls are round and they stretch thin leather over its mouth and strike it with a mallet and it produces a clear sound. TAMBOROV in the foreign tongue (i.e., tambourine).

15.he: אִם יָשַׁב עָלָיו זָב וְזָבָה נִדָּה וְיוֹלֶדֶת, נַעֲשֶׂה אַב הַטֻּמְאָה לְטַמֵּא אָדָם לְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים. דִּכְלִי הַמְיֻחָד לִישִׁיבָה הוּא:
15.en: if a person with gonorrhea or a woman with a flux, a menstruating woman or a woman who gave birth to a child sat upon it, it becomes a primary form of Levitical impurity to ritually defile people [and] to ritually defile clothing. For it is a vessel that is special for sitting.

15.he: כְּלוֹמַר הַמְקוֹנֶנֶת וּמְיַלֶּלֶת יוֹשֶׁבֶת עָלָיו, לְפִי שֶׁרְגִילִין לִסְפֹּד וּלְקוֹנֵן עַל יְדֵי נִגּוּן שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ כְלִי. וְכֵן הַמִּנְהָג הַיּוֹם בְּאַרְצוֹת הַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִים:
15.en: that is to say those [women] who sing dirges and howl sit upon it, for they would regularly eulogize and sing dirges through the melody of that instrument. And such is the custom today in the countries of the Ishmaelites.

15.he: לְשׁוֹן אֱלִי כִבְתוּלָה חֲגֻרַת שַׂק (יואל א). וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
15.en: it is the language of (Joel 1:8): “Lament – like a maiden girt with sackcloth [for the husband of her youth!]"אלי כבתולה חגרת-שק [על-בעל נעוריה]". But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

15.he: שֶׁיֶּשׁ עָלֶיהָ צוּרַת כְּלִי. מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן לִמְצוֹדַת עַכְבָּר:
15.en: because it has upon it the form of a vessel, which is not the case regarding the trap of the mouse.

16.he: שֻׁלְחָן הַכָּפוּל. עָשׂוּי חֻלְיוֹת אוֹ פְרָקִים, וּלְאַחַר שֶׁמְּסִירִים אוֹתוֹ כּוֹפְלִים חֻלְיוֹתָיו אוֹ פְרָקָיו זוֹ עַל זוֹ, וְכָל חֻלְיָא הַוְיָא כְּלִי בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ:
16.en: it is made by links/segment of earth cut out in digging a pit and piled up on its border or sections, and after they remove it, they fold the segments or sections one top of the other, and each segment is a vessel on its own.

16.he: קְעָרָה גְדוֹלָה מְאֹד וּבְתוֹכָהּ קְעָרוֹת קְטַנּוֹת, וְנוֹתְנִים בְּכָל קְעָרָה מִן הַקְּטַנּוֹת מִין אֶחָד שֶׁל תַּבְשִׁיל. וּלְפִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בְּתוֹכָהּ מִינִים הַרְבֵּה, נִקְרָא תַמְחוּי הַמִּזְנוֹן. תַּרְגּוּם לְמִינוֹ לִזְנוֹהִי:
16.en: each of which, if separated, may be a receptacle) – a very large dish and within it are small dishes, and they place on each of the smaller dishes a course of cooked food. And because there is within it many different kinds, it is called תמחוי המזנון/a plate with many partitions. And in Aramaic translation it is called למינו לזנוהי.

16.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁל פְּרָקִים:
16.en: protuberance/shape of the human buttock) – the seat of limbs.

16.he: תַּרְגּוּם קְעָרָה מְגִיסְתָּא:
16.en: the Aramaic translation of קערה מגיסתא/a dish from a tray.

16.he: כְּמִין קְעָרָה שֶׁל עֵץ. וּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים הוּא, בִּמְקֵדָה בְזוּיָה, פֵּרוּשׁ קְעָרָה בְזוּיָה. וְכָל הַכֵּלִים הַלָּלוּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ, נִשְׁאָר לְכָל חֵלֶק מֵהֶם צוּרַת כְּלִי. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
16.en: fragments of which may be used as a receptacle) – like a kind of wooden dish. And it is the language of the Sages, as it is explained, of a מקדה בזויה/fragment of a degraded vessel used for carrying fire. And all of these vessels, even though they were divided, remained in each section of them the form of a vessel. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

16.he: לְהָסִיר קִסְמִין שֶׁבָּהֶם, דְּקֹדֶם לָכֵן לֹא חֲזוּ לִמְלַאכְתָּן, שֶׁמְּשָׂרְטִים אֶת הַבָּשָׂר. אֲבָל אִם אֵינָן מְחֻסָּרִין אֶלָּא שִׁיפָה שֶׁל צִחְצוּחַ וּמְרִיקָה, הָא קַיְמָא לָן [חֻלִּין כה] דְּגָלְמֵי כְלֵי עֵץ שֶׁעָתִיד לְשַׁבֵּץ וְלָשׁוּף טְמֵאִין:
16.en: to remove the chips that are in them. For prior to this, they are not appropriate for the work, that they wound the skin. But if they are not lacking anything other than the rubbing of glistening and scouring/washing, we hold [see Tractate Hullin 25a]: “unfinished wood vessels that is to be adorned with designs and polished are ritually impure.”

16.he: שֶׁגָּמַר בְּלִבּוֹ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יָשׁוּף עוֹד:
16.en: he determined in his heart to use them even though he will not polish/rub them any further.

16.he: כְּשֶׁמְּסָרְגִים הַמִּטָּה בַחֲבָלִים, בֵּין כָּל חֶבֶל לְחֶבֶל קָרוּי בַּיִת. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר:
16.en: when they make a partition by means of net-work/like lattices to the bed with ropes, between each rope it is called a בית/row. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Meir.

16.he: מֵאֵימָתַי גְּמַר מְלַאכְתָּן:
16.en: from when is the completion of their manufacture?

16.he: כְּשֶׁאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה קֻפָּה אוֹ סַל וְגוֹמֵר אֶת שְׂפָתוֹ זוֹ הִיא חֲסִימָה:
16.en: when a person makes a large vessel or a basket and completes the rim/peels them, this is החסימה/forming of the rim of a basket.

16.he: לְאַחַר שֶׁגּוֹמֵר הַשָּׂפָה, וְנִשְׁתַּיְּרוּ קִסְמִין רָאשֵׁי קְרוּמִיּוֹת הַבּוֹלְטִין, פּוֹסְקָן וְקוֹטְמָן, וְזוֹ הִיא קְנִיבָה:
16.en: pinched off the projecting pricks) – after he completes the rim, when there remained the chips at the head of the protruding skin-like, scaly envelope of reed, he cuts and lops them off. And this is קניבה/trimming

16.he: סַלִּים הָעֲשׂוּיִן מֵחֲרִיּוֹת שֶׁל דֶּקֶל:
16.en: baskets made from dried branches/twigs of palm-trees.

16.he: בְּלֹא קְנִיבָה:
16.en: without trimming.

16.he: סַל שֶׁל גֶּמִי:
16.en: containing chosen fruits-designated for use) – a basket made of bulrushes.

16.he: שֶׁיִּגְמֹר הַחֶבֶל שֶׁתּוֹלֶה בָהּ:
כְּלִי שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין בּוֹ לְגִינִין לִשְׁמֹר:
16.en: a vessel in which they place flasks for preservation.

16.he: כְּלִי שֶׁמַּצְנִיעִין בּוֹ כּוֹסוֹת:
16.en: a vessel that they hide cups In it

16.he: קָנוֹן שֶׁבּוֹרְרִים בּוֹ קִטְנִית. וְהוּא נַעֲשֶׂה מֵחֲרִיּוֹת שֶׁל דֶּקֶל:
16.en: a reed basket that they select in it pulse. And it is made from the twigs of palm trees.

16.he: קֻפּוֹת קְטַנּוֹת:
16.en: small vessels.

16.he: קֻפּוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת:
16.en: large vessels [with partitions].

16.he: לְאַחַר שֶׁאָרְגוּ שׁוּלֵי הַקֻּפָּה, אוֹרְגִים סְבִיבוֹתֶיהָ עִגּוּלִים כְּפִי מַה שֶּׁרוֹצֶה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה רְחָבָה בְדָפְנוֹתֶיהָ בְּגָבְהָהּ, וְאוֹתָן עִגּוּלִים שֶׁל דְּפָנוֹת קְרוּיִין דּוּרִים:
16.en: after they wove the rims of the vessel, they weave around it circles according to what they want to be the width of the walls in its height, and those round/circular bands/walls are called דורים/wreaths.

16.he: הַבָּסִיס שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים עָלָיו הַמֹּאזְנַיִם:
16.en: the base on which they place upon it the balance.

16.he: מִשֶּׁיַּגְבִּיהַּ עַל שְׂפָתוֹ עִגּוּל אֶחָד:
16.en: from when he lifts up the rim by one circular band.

16.he: שְׁתֵּי סִבּוּבִים:
16.en: two goings-around.

16.he: שֶׁאֵין שְׂפָתוֹ גְבוֹהָה כִּשְׂפַת הַקֻּפָּה:
16.en: that its rim is not as tall as the rim of the large vessel.

16.he: וְעָרָק עָשׂוּי מִשַּׁעַם וְאָרְכּוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵרָחְבּוֹ, כְּתֵבָה שֶׁל רַצְעָנִים. וְקָרוּי עָרָק. וְעַד שְׂרוֹךְ נַעַל (בראשית יד), תַּרְגּוּם וְעַד עַרְקַת מְסָאנָא. וּמִשּׁוּם דִּכְלֵי גֶמִי וְשַׁעַם דִּין כְּלֵי עֵץ יֵשׁ לָהֶם, הִלְכָּךְ תְּנִינְהוּ גַבֵּי הֲדָדֵי עִם כְּלֵי עֵץ:
16.en: and the long and flat vessel made of bamboo and its length is greater than its width, the writing of shoe-makers/saddlers is called ערק/long and flat vessel made of bamboo. It is the Aramaic translation of (Genesis 14:23): “[I will not take] so much as a thread or a sandal strap [of what is yours]” until the sandal strap. But because it is a bulrush and shoe, they have the law of a wooden vessel, therefore, we teach them together with wooden vessels.

16.he: כִּיס שֶׁל עוֹר גָּדוֹל, שֶׁהָרוֹעֶה נוֹתֵן בּוֹ מְזוֹנוֹת וְכָל דָּבָר. וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ, וְלֹא הָרוֹעֶה בְתַרְמִילוֹ:
16.en: a large leather pouch/bag that the shepherd places food and all things. And it is similar to it, but not the shepherd with his sack/bag.

16.he: מִסְגְּרוֹתָיו, כְּמִין אָזְנַיִם קְטַנּוֹת סְבִיבוֹת הַתּוּרְמֵל, וּמַכְנִיסִים בְּאוֹתָן אָזְנַיִם חֲבָלִים שֶׁסּוֹגְרִים אוֹתוֹ:
16.en: its rims, like kinds of small ears/handles surrounding the leather bag, and he puts into those handles ropes that they close it with.

16.he: עוֹר שֶׁלּוֹבְשִׁים הָעַבְּדָנִים בִּשְׁעַת מְלַאכְתָּן:
16.en: leather that the tanners wear at the time of their work.

16.he: כְּעֵין צִיצִית שֶׁל טַלִּית, כָּךְ עוֹשִׂין לָהּ פְּתִילִים עַל כְּנָפַיִם לְקָשְׁרָם בָּהֶן. וְרַמְבַּ"ם פֵּרֵשׁ, סְקֹרְטְיָא עוֹר שֶׁאוֹכְלִים עָלָיו, וְצִיצָתָהּ, הוּא אֶמְצַע הָעוֹר שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בּוֹ טַס שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת לְנוֹי, לְשׁוֹן צִיץ הַזָּהָב, שֶׁהוּא טַס שֶׁל זָהָב:
16.en: like a kind of ritual fringes/Tzitzit of a Tallit/prayer shawl. So, we make the threads on its corners to tie attach them. But Maimonides explained, that סקורטיא, is leather that we eat upon, and its show-fringes is in the middle of the leather that we place upon it a foil/plate of metal for adornment, the language of the golden front plate (ציץ הזהב), which is a foil/plate of gold.

16.he: טַבַּעַת נְחֹשֶׁת אוֹ בַּרְזֶל שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בִּקְצֵה הַסְּקֹרְטְיָא:
16.en: a copper or iron ring that they place on the edge of the leather coat.

16.he: עוֹר שֶׁמַּצִּיעִים עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה. וְקוֹרִים לוֹ בַעֲרָבִי נט"ע, וּפְשׁוּטֵי כְלֵי עוֹר מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה מִדְּרַבָּנָן בִּלְבַד, כִּפְשׁוּטֵי כְלֵי עֵץ, וְדִינָן בָּזֶה שָׁוֶה, שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה מִדְּאוֹרַיְתָא אֶלָּא מִדְּרַבָּנָן בְּכָל שְׁאָר טֻמְאוֹת, חוּץ מִמִּשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב, שֶׁהֵן נַעֲשִׂים מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב מִדְּאוֹרַיְתָא כְּשֶׁהֵן מְיֻחָדִים לְכָךְ:
16.en: hide spread over the bed frame) – leather that they spread over the bed. And they call it NATAH in Arabic. And flat leather vessels are susceptible to receive ritual defilement from the Rabbis alone, like flat wooden utensils, and their law is similar in that they are not susceptible to receive ritual defilement from Torah, but rather from the Rabbis in all of the rest of the defilements except for the uncleanness caused by an unclean person lying o an object and the uncleanness caused by an unclean person’s sitting (i.e., the unclean seat) which ae made uncleanness by lying and uncleanness by sitting from the Torah when they are designated for this.

16.he: כַּר קָטָן מִכֶּסֶת, וְעָשׂוּי לְהַנִּיחַ תַּחַת מְרַאֲשׁוֹתָיו. וְכֶסֶת תַּחַת כָּל גּוּפוֹ:
16.en: a mattress is smaller than a cushion, and is made to place under their heads. But the cushion [is made to be placed] underneath all of his body.

16.he: מְשַׁיְּרִים מִשּׁוּם פֶּתַח לְהַכְנִיס מִשָּׁם הַמּוֹךְ לְמַלְּאוֹת הַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת:
16.en: they leave over/reserve because of the opening to bring in from there the hackled wool/lint/soft spongy substance to fill the mattress and the cushion.

16.he: קֻפָּה עֲשׂוּיָה מִמִּינִים שֶׁל עֲרָבָה, וְאוֹצְרִים בָּהּ גְּרוֹגָרוֹת:
16.en: a sort of bale for packing dates, figs, etc.) – a basket made from species of trough, and they store in it dried figs.

16.he: כְּמִין קֻפָּה עֲשׂוּיָה מִקּוֹצִים, וּמְשִׂימִין בָּהּ טִיט:
16.en: like a kind of basket made from thorns, and they place plaster/clay upon it.

16.he: לְשׁוֹן סוּגָה בַשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים, עוֹשִׂין כְּמִין כְּפִיפָה קְטַנָּה מִן הֶעָלִים וּמְכַסִּים בָּהּ פֵּרוֹת, וְאֵינָהּ אֶלָּא מְלֶאכֶת עֲרַאי:
16.en: it is the language of סוגה בשושנים/”hedged about with lilies (Song of Songs 7:3). They make a kind of small basket of osier from the leaves and they cover fruits with it, but it is not other than a temporary construction.

16.he: מִצּוּרֵי הַדֶּקֶל:
16.en: from the band made of palm-bark (i.e., wicker).

16.he: כְּלִי שֶׁעוֹשִׂים מֵחֲרָיּוֹת שֶׁל דֶּקֶל, וּמַנִּיחִין בּוֹ תְּמָרִים לַחִים וְהֵן מִתְבַּשְּׁלִים בְּתוֹכוֹ:
16.en: without cutting it open/wrapper of reed-matting) – a vessel that we make from the dried branches of the palm, and we place in it moist palm and they ripen in it.

16.he: אֲבָל אִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא הַתְּמָרִים אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יִקְרָעֶנּוּ אוֹ יַתִּיר הַחֲרִיּוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ, טָהוֹר, דְּכֵיוָן דְּקוֹרְעוֹ אוֹ מַתִּירוֹ מַשְׁלִיכוֹ לָאַשְׁפָּה, וְהָוֵי לְתַשְׁמִישׁ עֲרַאי:
16.en: but if he is not able to remove the date-palms unless he tears it or loosens his dried palm branches, it is pure, for since he tears it or loosens it/unties it, he casts it into the dunghill/trash for it is of temporary use.

16.he: בֵּית יָד שֶׁל עוֹר:
16.en: a leather glove.

16.dibur: שֶׁל זוֹרֵי גְרָנוֹת וְהוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים וְשֶׁל עוֹשֵׂי פִשְׁתָּן טְמֵאָה.
16.he: דְּכֵיוָן דְּהִיא עֲשׂוּיָה כְּדֵי לֶאֱחֹז הַדָּבָר בְּיָדוֹ יָפֶה שֶׁלֹּא יִשָּׁמֵט מִמֶּנּוּ, אוֹ כְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִתְחֹב לוֹ קוֹץ בְּיָדוֹ, מִקְּרֵי עָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַדָּבָר שֶׁהוּא אוֹחֵז בּוֹ נִשְׁעָן עַל הַבֵּית יָד וּמְקַבְּלוֹ:
16.en: for since it is made in order to hold the thing in his hand well so that it not become detached from him, or in order that a thorn not become inserted/stuck in his hand, it is called made for reception, for since the thing that he is holding on to lies on the glove and receives it.

16.he: הָעוֹשִׂים גְּרִיסוֹת שֶׁל פּוֹל בָּרֵחַיִם:
16.en: that make pounded beans in the millstone.

16.he: לִשְׁאֹב אֶת הַזֵּעָה כְּדֵי לְהָקֵר בְּשָׂרוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיעַ. אִי נַמִּי, שֶׁלֹּא תְטַנֵּף זֵיעַת יָדָיו הַדָּבָר שֶׁהוּא אוֹחֵז בּוֹ:
16.en: to absorb the perspiration in order to cool off his skin that he not perspire. Alternatively, the sweat of his hands will soil the thing that he is holding on to.

16.he: דְּתַשְׁמִישׁ עֲרַאי חֲשׁוּב:
16.en: for it is considered temporary usage.

16.he: עוֹר שֶׁמְּשִׂימִין בְּעֵינֵי הַפָּרָה כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּסַבֵּב וְתָדוּשׁ:
16.en: for receiving the excrements of working cattle) – leather that they place in the eyes of the cow in order that it should turn around and thresh.

16.he: כְּמִין מְצוֹדָה קְטַנָּה שֶׁל חֲבָלִים שֶׁחוֹסְמִים בָּהּ פִּי הַפָּרָה שֶׁלֹּא תֹאכַל:
16.en: like a kind of small net/trap of ropes that muzzle the in it the mouth of the cow in order that it cannot eat.

16.he: כְּלִי שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים בּוֹ אֵשׁ וּגְלָלֵי בָקָר וּמְעַשְּׁנִים כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּבְרְחוּ הַנְּחִילִים שֶׁל דְּבוֹרִים מִן הַכַּוֶּרֶת וְיִקַּח הַדְּבַשׁ. מִלְּשׁוֹן אֲשֶׁר תִּדְפֶנּוּ רוּחַ (תהלים א):
16.en: a vessel that they place in it fire and the dung of cattle and they fumigate in order that the swarms of bees from the beehive will flee and he will take the honey. [This is] from the language of (Psalms 1:4): “[they are like the chaff] that wind blows away/אשר-תדפנו רוח.”

16.he: כְּלִי שֶׁמְּנִיפִין בּוֹ בִימוֹת הַחַמָּה לְהָבִיא הָרוּחַ:
16.en: a vessel/utensil that they wave on the hot days to bring the wind.

16.he: כְּמִין אַרְגָּז קָטָן שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה נוֹתֶנֶת בּוֹ תַכְשִׁיטֶיהָ וְנוֹתֶנֶת עָלָיו כְּסוּת מִלְּמַעְלָה:
16.en: a kind of small box/chest that the woman places in it her ornaments and places upon it a cover from above.

16.he: תֵּבָה שֶׁשּׁוֹמְרִים בָּהּ הַבְּגָדִים. עַל הַמֶּלְתָּחָה (מלכים ב י), מְתַרְגְּמִינַן עַל קוּמְטְרָה:
16.en: a chest that they protect clothing in it. We translate in Aramaic [the Biblical phrase] (2 Kings 10:22): “[He said to the man in charge] of the wardrobe, [‘Bring out the vestments for all the worshipers of Baal]” as on the chest protecting the clothing.

16.he: [כָּל חָרָשׁ עֵצִים] לְפִי מְלַאכְתּוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹ מָקוֹם שֶׁכּוֹבֵשׁ וְעוֹצֵר הָעֵץ כְּשֶׁהוּא מְעֻוָּת וְעָקֹם עַד שֶׁמְּיַשְּׁרוֹ:
16.en: for straightening wood) – [every wood carpenter/artisan] has, according his trade a place that he stores and gathers the wood that is crooked and curved until he straightens it out.

16.he: הַמִּכְסֶה שֶׁעַל הַתֵּבָה הֶעָשׂוּי כְּעֵין קֻבָּה:
16.en: the cover that is upon the chest that is made like a kind of arched compartment.

16.he: נַרְתִּיק שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לַסֵּפֶר וּמַכְנִיסִים אוֹתוֹ בְתוֹכוֹ:
16.en: a leather case that they make for a Scroll and they place it inside of it.

16.he: נַרְתִּיק שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בְּתוֹכוֹ הַנֶּגֶר, הוּא הַיָּתֵד שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים אֲחוֹרֵי הַדֶּלֶת:
16.en: a leather case that the carpenter puts inside of it, which is the peg that they place on the back of the door.

16.he: נַרְתִּיק שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בּוֹ הַמַּנְעוּל שֶׁנּוֹעֲלִים בּוֹ הַדֶּלֶת:
16.en: ובית המנעול (lock-socket)– the leather case that they place in it the lock that locks the door.

16.he: קָנֶה שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בּוֹ הַמְּזוּזָה:
16.en: the metal beam that they place the Mezuzah in.

16.he: דְּפוּס כְּעֵין רֹאשׁ שֶׁל אָדָם שֶׁמְּתַקְּנִים עָלָיו הַמִּצְנֶפֶת:
16.en: a frame like a kind of head of a person that they prepare for him the priest’s turban.

16.he: כְּמִין סוּס שֶׁל עֵץ שֶׁהַלֵּיצָנִים מְשַׂחֲקִים בּוֹ. וְאִית דִּמְפָרְשֵׁי, כְּלִי שֶׁל עֵץ אֶרֶז הֶעָשׂוּי לְזַמֵּר:
16.en: it is like a kind of wooden horse that the jesters/scoffers play with. But there are those who interpret/explain this, a wooden utensil of cedar that is made for music.

16.he: וּבִמְנַעַנְעִים וּבִמְצַלְצְלִין, מְתַרְגְּמִינַן וּבִרְבִיעִין וּבְצֶלְצֱלִין:
16.en: and “with sistrums and cymbals,”(see II Samuel 6:5) that we translate in the Aramaic: “a sistra and cymbals.”

16.he: שֶׁל הַמְקוֹנֶנֶת. כְּמוֹ (יואל א) אֱלִי כִבְתוּלָה חֲגוּרַת שַׂק:
16.en: of the female wailers. Like (Joel 1:8): “Lament – like a maiden girt with sackcloth [for the husband of her youth!].”

16.he: תַּרְמִילוֹ שֶׁל עָנִי:
קוֹרוֹת שֶׁסּוֹמְכִין בָּהֶן הַמִּטָּה שֶׁלֹּא תִפֹּל:
16.en: beams that support the bed that it would not fall.

16.he: כְּמוֹ דְפוּס שֶׁל תְּפִלִּין:
16.en: like the frame of the Tefillin.

16.he: דְּפוּס שֶׁל עוֹשֵׂי שַׁלְשְׁלָאוֹת. שֶׁעוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן עַל גַּבֵּי אֵמוּם הַיְנוּ [עַל גַּבֵּי] דְּפוּס. וְרַמְבַּ"ם גָּרֵיס, עוֹשֵׂי סוּתוֹת, לְשׁוֹן וּבְדַם עֲנָבִים סוּתוֹ (בראשית מט), וְהוּא הַדְּפוּס שֶׁל עֵץ שֶׁאוֹרְגִין עָלָיו הַבְּגָדִים:
16.en: frame of those who make chains. That they make them on top of a model/frame, that is [on top of] a block. But Maimonides has the reading, עושי סותות/those who make dresses. It is the language of (Genesis 49:11): “His robe in blood of grapes.” And it is a wooden frame that one sews clothing upon it.

16.he: כְּגוֹן כִּסּוּיֵי כֵלִים וְנַרְתִּיקֵי כֵלִים, שֶׁהֵם נַעֲשׂוּ לְשַׁמֵּשׁ הַכֵּלִים הַמְשַׁמְּשִׁים אֶת הָאָדָם:
16.en: as for example, the coverings of utensils/vessels and the cases of vessels, which are made to serve the utensils that human beings use.

16.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַכִּסּוּי מְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת הַכְּלִי לִשְׁמֹר מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ, וְהַיְנוּ שְׁעַת מְלָאכָה דִידֵיהּ, וּכְשֶׁאֵין כְּלוּם בַּכְּלִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְכִסּוּי קָרֵי לֵיהּ שֶׁלֹּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה. וְיֵשׁ כֵּלִים שֶׁמַּנִּיחִים עֲלֵיהֶן הַכִּסּוּי תָּמִיד בֵּין כְּשֶׁהוּא מָלֵא בֵּין כְּשֶׁהוּא רֵיקָן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַכִּסּוּי מְחֻבָּר בּוֹ, חֲשִׁיב כַּכְּלִי גוּפֵיהּ לְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה אֲפִלּוּ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחֻבָּר בּוֹ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָגִיל לִהְיוֹת תָּמִיד עָלָיו. וְהַאי כְּלָלָא דְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אַפְּשׁוּטֵי כְלֵי עֵץ הַמְשַׁמְּשִׁין אֶת הַכֵּלִים קָאֵי. אֲבָל כְּלֵי קִבּוּל, מִטַּמְּאִין בְּכָל עִנְיָן. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
16.en: at the time when the covering services the vessel to protect what is within it, which is at the time of its service. But when there is nothing inside the vessel, that it doesn’t require a covering, it is called, not at the time of its service. But there are vessels that they always place the covering upon them whether it is full or whether it is empty, even though the covering is not attached to it, since it us generally always upon it. And this general principle of Rabbi Yossi refers to flat wooden vessels that service the vessels, but receptacles defile in every matter. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yossi.

16.he: סַכִּין שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי פִיּוֹת:
16.en: a knife that has wo mouths.

16.he: תִּיק הַכְּלִי שֶׁבּוֹ כּוֹחֲלִין הָעַיִן:
16.en: the case of a utensil that they paint the eye with it.

16.he: הַכְּלִי שֶׁשּׁוֹמְרִים בּוֹ אֶת הַכְּחוֹל:
16.en: the vessel that protects the eye-paint that is in it.

16.he: קֻלְמוֹס שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת וּבַרְזֶל:
16.en: a bronze and iron writing pen/reed.

16.he: תְּרֵין תִּיק. וְהוּא כְלִי אֶחָד וּבוֹ תִיקִין הַרְבֵּה חֲלוּקִים, לַקֻּלְמוֹס וְלַסַּכִּין וְלַמִּסְפָּרַיִם. וְרוֹפְאֵי הַחַבּוּרוֹת מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בִּכְלִי זֶה הַרְבֵּה. וּבְלַעַ"ז פינארו"ל:
16.en: probably for leveling the paper) – two cases. And it is one vessel and inside are many divided cases/sheaths, for reeds, knives and scissors. And the doctors of the associations/communities use this vessel a great deal. And in the foreign language, PINAROL.

16.he: חִצִּים רְחָבִים. וּמְחִי קָבָלּוֹ [יְחֶזְקֵאל כו], מְתַרְגְּמִינַן וּמְחַת פָּגוֹשׁוֹהִי:
16.en: wide arrows and they wound those who receive them and we translate it in Aramaic ומחת פגושוהי/and he wounds with a battering projectile.

16.he: כְּלִי זֶמֶר שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת:
16.en: that all that one he brings into it from the side is not considered a case but rather a mere covering.

16.he: שֶׁכָּל שֶׁמַּכְנִיסוֹ מִן הַצַּד אֵינוֹ חֲשׁוּב נַרְתִּיק, אֶלָּא מִכְסֶה בְעָלְמָא:
16.en: a [molten] metal musical instrument.

16.he: שֵׁבֶט שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ עִגּוּל כְּמוֹ כַדּוּר, וְיוֹצְאִים בּוֹ יְתֵדוֹת שֶׁדּוֹמוֹת לִשְׁקֵדִים, בַּעֲרָבִי קוֹרִין לוֹ דבו"ס, וּבְלַעַ"ז מאצ"א:
16.en: a copper staff and at its top is a circle like a ball, and pegs that are similar to almonds come out from it. In Arabi they call is DVUS.

16.he: לְמִכְסֶה. תַּרְגּוּם מִכְסֶה, חוֹפָאָה:
16.en: for covering. It is the Aramaic translation of cover/roofing.

16.he: דְּתַנְיָא, יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה חִפּוּי כֵלִים לְטֻמְאָה, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא יא) אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בָהֶם, פְּרָט לְחִפּוּי כֵּלִים:
16.en: as it is taught in a Baraita, it is possible that I increase the covering of vessels for impurity, as the inference teaches us (Leviticus 11:32): “[And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall be impure: be it any article of wood, or a cloth or a skin, or a sack – ] any such article that can be put to use [shall be dipped in water, and it shall remain impure until evening; then it shall be pure].”

17.dibur: כָּל כְּלֵי בַעֲלֵי בָתִּים שִׁעוּרָן בְּרִמּוֹנִים.
17.he: אִם נִקְּבוּ בְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן, טְהוֹרִים:
17.en: if they made an incision while removing a pomegranate, they are ritually pure.

17.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים שִׁעוּרָן כְּשֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִין לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן מֵעֵין הַתַּשְׁמִישׁ שֶׁהָיוּ מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בָּהֶן תְּחִלָּה, כְּגוֹן כֵּלִים הַמְיֻחָדִים לַתְּאֵנִים שִׁעוּרָן בְּמוֹצִיא תְאֵנָה, וְהַמְיֻחָדִים לַזֵּיתִים שִׁעוּרָן בְּמוֹצִיא זַיִת. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
17.en: all the vessel, their measure is when they are not appropriate to use them in the form the usage that they would initially use them. As for example, vessels that are designated for figs, their measure is when they remove a fig, and those which are designated for olives, their measure is when one removes an olive. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Eliezer.

17.he: קֻפּוֹת בַּעֲלֵי הַגִּנּוֹת שֶׁעֲשׂוּיִין לִתֵּן בָּהֶם יְרָקוֹת:
17.en: baskets that those who own the gardens that they are used to place vegetables in them.

17.he: וּבְהָא מוֹדֶה תַנָּא קַמָּא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאֵין שִׁעוּרָן בְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן:
17.en: שיעורן במוציא אגודות ירק  and in this, the first Tanna/teacher agrees with Rabbi Eliezer that their measure is not when removing a pomegranate.

17.he: בְּמוֹצִיא תֶבֶן:
17.en: when removing straw.

17.he: תֶּבֶן דַּק מְעֹרָב בְּזֶבֶל. תַּרְגּוּם לְקוֹשֵׁשׁ קַשׁ (שמות ה), לְגַבָּבָא גִילָא. וְהַבַּלָּנִים דְּהַיְנוּ בַּעֲלֵי הַמֶּרְחֲצָאוֹת שׂוֹרְפִין אוֹתוֹ בַמֶּרְחֲצָאוֹת:
17.en: thin straw mixed in manure. It is the Aramaic translation of (Exodus 5:12): “[Then the people scattered throughout the land of Egypt] to gather stubble for straw,” raking stubble/straw [that is rounded]. But the bathing attendants, that is, the owners of the bathhouses burn it in the bathhouses.

17.he: בֵּין שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים בֵּין שֶׁל גַּנָּנִים. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
17.en: whether they are of those who own homes or those who are gardeners. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehoshua.

17.he: מַטְוֵה הַשְּׁתִי דַק מִשֶּׁל עֵרֶב. כִּדְמוּכָח בִּכְתֻבּוֹת בְּפֶרֶק אַף עַל פִּי [דַּף סד]. וּפְקָעִיּוֹת שֶׁל שְׁתִי הֵן קְטַנִּים מִפְּקָעִיּוֹת שֶׁל עֵרֶב. וּפֵרוּשׁ פְּקָעִיּוֹת, גלוממור"י בְּלַעַ"ז. אִי נַמִּי מטאס"י בְּלַעַ"ז:
17.en: the yarn of the warp/longitudinal clews is thinner than that of the latitudinal ones, as is found in [Tractate] Ketubot 64b, in Chapter [Five]"אף על פי" /Even though. And the longitudinal/warp clews are smaller than the latitudinal/woof clews. And the explanation of פקעיות is GLOMARI in the foreign tongue. Alternatively, MATASI in the foreign tongue.

17.dibur: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבֶּלֶת שֶׁל עֵרֶב טְמֵאָה.
17.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת שֶׁל שְׁתִי אִם מְקַבֶּלֶת שֶׁל עֵרֶב טְמֵאָה, שֶׁשִּׁעוּרָהּ בְּמוֹצִיא עֵרֶב, שֶׁהוּא גָדוֹל מִמּוֹצִיא שְׁתִי. וְכֵן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל אֶת הַתַּמְחוּיִין טָמֵא, כְּלוֹמַר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַנֶּקֶב גָּדוֹל שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת אֶת הַקְּעָרוֹת, אִם מְקַבֵּל אֶת הַתַּמְחוּיִין שֶׁהֵן גְּדוֹלִים מִן הַקְּעָרוֹת, עֲדַיִן מִקְּרֵי חֲזִי לְתַשְׁמִישׁוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹן וְטָמֵא:
17.en: this is what he said: But even though it does not receive warp clews, if it receives woof clews, it is ritually unclean. That its measure is the removal of the woof, which is larger than removing the warp. And similarly, even though it holds trays, it is ritually impure, that is to say, even though the incision is large and it doesn’t hold/receive the dishes, if it holds/receives the trays which are larger than the dishes, it is still called worthy of its first usage and is ritually impure.

17.dibur: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל אֶת הָרְעִי.
17.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל אֶת הַמַּשְׁקִין, אִם מְקַבֵּל אֶת הָרְעִי טָמֵא. בֵּית הָרְאִי, כְּמוֹ בֵית הָרְעִי. כְּלִי שֶׁנִּפְנֶה בוֹ וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ צוֹאָה וּמֵי רַגְלַיִם:
17.en: even though it (i.e., a night chamber/chamber pot) [which is too defective] does not receive/retain the liquids, if it retains solid excrement, like the chamber pot/night chamber, it is ritually impure. The digestive organ, like the night chamber/chamber pot. A vessel that one eases oneself in and it has excrement and urine in it.

17.he: גָּרְסִינַן. וְאִית דְּגָרְסֵי, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְקַיְּמִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאַמִּלְּתָא דְתַנָּא קַמָּא קָאֵי, דְּאָמַר אִם מְקַבֵּל אֶת הָעֵרֶב וְאֶת הַתַּמְחוּיִין וְאֶת הָרְעִי טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְקַיְּמִין וְשׁוֹמְרִים אוֹתוֹ, כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזִי לְהָכִי. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
17.en: is our reading (“because they do not keep it”). But there are those who have the reading of “because they keep it.” But it refers to the matter of the first Tanna/teacher, who stated, that if it keeps the woof and the trays and the digestive organ is ritually impure, because they keep it and protect it, since it is appropriate for this. But the Halakha is not according to Rabban Gamaliel.

17.he: שִׁעוּר שְׁבִירָתָן, בְּמוֹצִיא כִכָּרוֹת שֶׁל פַּת:
17.en: the measure of their breakage through the removal of loaves of bread.

17.he: כְּלִי אָרוּג מִקָּנִים אוֹ זְמוֹרוֹת:
17.en: to which reeds were fastened from the bottom upwards – crosswise – for support) – a woven utensil made from reeds or vine-shoots.

17.he: שֶׁנִּפְחֲתוּ שׁוּלֵיהֶן וְהִכְנִיס קָנִים מִמַּטָּה לְמַעְלָה לְהַחְזִיק הַשּׁוּלַיִם:
17.en: that their borders/rims were opened and they brought in reeds from the bottom to the top to strength the rims at the bottom of the vessel.

17.he: שֶׁגִּפְּפָהּ סָבִיב. תַּרְגּוּם וַיְחַבֵּק, וְגַפֵּיף. פֵּרוּשׁ אַחֵר, גַּפַּיִם, שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהּ אָזְנַיִם:
17.en: that they attached as a rim. [It is] the Aramaic translation of ויחבק/and he embraced and throw arms around. Another explanation: arms/handles – that he made for them handles.

17.he: שֶׁכְּשֶׁאוֹחֵז בַּגַּפַּיִם אֵין הַכְּלִי עוֹלֶה עִמּוֹ:
17.en: that when he holds the handles, the vessel does not go up with him (and it is not susceptible to receiving ritual defilement).

17.he: הָא דִתְנַן בְּרֵישׁ פִּרְקִין כָּל כְּלֵי בַעֲלֵי בָתִּים שִׁעוּרָן בְּרִמּוֹנִים, כְּשֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה רִמּוֹנִים אֲחוּזִים זֶה בָזֶה וְיֵצֵא הָאֶחָד דֶּרֶךְ הַנֶּקֶב, זֶהוּ שִׁעוּר שֶׁל מוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן:
17.en: that which is taught at the beginning of our chapter, “All Utensils of householders – their measure [is] with pomegranates” (Chapter 17, Mishnah 1), when there would be three pomegranates fastened with each other, and one came out through the path of an incision, this is the measure of someone removing a pomegranate.

17.he: שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ נִעְנוּעַ שֶׁל נְטִילָה וְהִלּוּךְ מְמַהֵר הָרִמּוֹן לָצֵאת דֶּרֶךְ הַנֶּקֶב:
17.en: that through the waving/shaking of taking it and shaking it – the pomegranate speedily leaves through the incision.

17.he: שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַפְשָׁלָה לַאֲחוֹרָיו הוּא מְמַהֵר לָצֵאת:
17.en: that through hanging it behind him, he quickens the [pomegranate’s] leaving.

17.he: שֶׁהֵן קְטַנִּים:
17.en: that they are small.

17.he: רֹבַע הַקַּב:
17.en: a quarter of a Kab.

17.he: כֵּיוָן דְּנִפְחַת רֻבּוֹ, טָהוֹר:
17.en: since the majority was reduced/lowered, it is ritually pure.

17.he: נִפְחֲתוּ וְחָסְרוּ:
17.en: נפרצו (if they were broken through) they were lessened and missing.

17.he: בְּשִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶן:
17.en: i.e., the sides of the vessel after becoming too thin) – at theirat their borders/rims.

17.he: אִם נִשְׁאַר בָּהֶן כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל כָּל שֶׁהוּא, טְמֵאִין. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
17.en: if there remains In them to receive/retain any amount, they are ritually impure. But the Halakha is according to Rabbi Shimon.

17.he: דִּכְלִי שֶׁנִּקַּב בְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן טָהוֹר:
17.en: that a vessel that is perforated with the removal of a pomegranate is ritually pure.

17.he: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין מְשַׁעֲרִין בָּהֶן, אֶלָּא בְרִמּוֹן בֵּינוֹנִי:
17.en: because we don’t estimate through them, other than through an intermediate-sized pomegranate.

17.he: שֶׁאִם אֶחָד מֵרִמּוֹנֵי בָדָאן שֶׁל עָרְלָה אוֹ שֶׁל כִּלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם נִתְעָרֵב עִם אֶלֶף רִמּוֹנִים שֶׁל הֶתֵּר, נִתְקַדְּשׁוּ כֻּלָּן וְנֶאֶסְרוּ. מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּרִמּוֹנִים שֶׁל שְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת:
17.en: that if one of the pomegranates of Baddan are Orlah/fruit that grows during the first three years after a tree was planted or of food crops in a vineyard (i.e., it is forbidden to plant or maintain other crops in a vineyard – rendering the entire vineyard forbidden) that is mixed up/combined with one-thousand pomegranates that are permitted, all of them are sanctified/dedicated and forbidden, which is not the case with the pomegranates of other places.

17.he: שֵׁם מָקוֹם:
17.en: Baddan is the name of a place.

17.he: קָסָבַר דְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן דְּכֵלִים, בְּרִמּוֹנֵי בָדָאן מְשַׁעֲרִינַן:
17.en: for he holds that a person who removes a pomegranate of vessels, the pomegranates of Baddan measure them.

17.dibur: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא הֻזְכְּרוּ רִמּוֹנֵי בָדָאן וְכוּ'.
17.he: אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן קִדּוּשׁ אֵין חִלּוּק בֵּין רִמּוֹנֵי בָדָאן לִשְׁאָר רִמּוֹנִים, דְּכֻלָּן מְקַדְּשִׁים, דְּסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כָּל שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִמָּנוֹת מְקַדֵּשׁ. בְּפֶרֶק הַתַּעֲרֹבוֹת וּבְרֵישׁ מַסֶּכֶת בֵּיצָה:
17.en: but in regard to sanctification, there is no distinction between the pomegranates of Baddan and the rest of the pomegranates, for all are sanctified. For Rabbi Yehuda holds that everything whose manner is to be counted is sanctified. In the Chapter of the Mixtures (Chapter 8 of Tractate Zevakhim), and at the beginning of the Tractate Betzah (3a).

17.he: שְׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁל כּוּתִים הֵן, וְנִכָּרִים הָיוּ רִמּוֹנִים וְחָצִיר שֶׁל מְקוֹמוֹת הַלָּלוּ [מֵרִמּוֹן וְחָצִיר] שֶׁל שְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת. וְכוּתָאֵי וַדַּאי לֹא מְעַשְּׂרֵי מַאי דִּמְזַבְּנֵי לְאַחֲרִינֵי, דְּלֹא חָיְשֵׁי אַלִּפְנֵי עִוֵּר לֹא תִתֵּן מִכְשׁוֹל, אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְנַפְשַׁיְהוּ מְעַשְּׂרֵי. הִלְכָּךְ מִתְעַשְּׂרִים וַדַּאי בְּכָל מָקוֹם:
17.en: two places of Cutheans, and the pomegranates and leeks of these places [from Rimon and Hatzir] of the rest of the places. But the Cutheans definitely do not tithe what they sell to others, and they are not anxious regarding [the Biblical verse in Leviticus 19:16): “place a stumbling block before the blind,” for even though for themselves they tithe, therefore, they definitely tithe in every place (previously certainly untithed).

17.he: כָּרְתִי פורו"ש בְּלַעַ"ז. כְּמוֹ אֶת הֶחָצִיר וְאֶת הַבְּצָלִים (במדבר יא):
17.en: leeks are called PURUSH in the foreign tongue, like (Numbers 11:5): “the leeks and the onions.”

17.he: גַּבֵּי טֻמְאַת אֳכָלִים, שֶׁאֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּפָחוֹת מִכַּבֵּיצָה:
17.en: regarding the ritual impurity of food, that they do not defile with less than an egg’s bulk.

17.he: מְמַלֵּא כוֹס מַיִם, וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹכוֹ גְדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּגְּדוֹלוֹת וּקְטַנָּה שֶׁבַּקְּטַנּוֹת, וְחוֹלֵק הַמַּיִם הַיּוֹצְאִין לִשְׁנֵי חֲלָקִים, וְהַחֵלֶק הָאֶחָד הוּא שִׁעוּר בֵּיצָה:
17.en: he fills a cup of water, and places into the largest of the large ones and the smallest of the small ones (i.e., eggs), and divides the volume of the water coming out into two parts and the one part is the measurement of an egg.

17.he: כְּלוֹמַר כְּשֶׁלּוֹקֵחַ גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּגְּדוֹלוֹת שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה הֵימֶנָּה. וְכֵן קְטַנָּה שֶׁבַּקְּטַנּוֹת שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ יוֹתֵר קְטַנָּה מִמֶּנָּה:
17.en: that is to say, that when a person takes the largest of the large ones, perhaps there is one larger than [even] that one. And similarly, the smallest of the small, perhaps thee is something smaller than it.

17.he: לְפִי אֹמֶד דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁהִיא בֵּינוֹנִית לְמַרְאֵה עֵינָיו. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
17.en: according to the estimate of his mind, which is the intermediate according to his eyesight. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yossi.

17.he: לְהוֹצָאַת שַׁבָּת, וּלְשִׁתּוּפֵי מְבוֹאוֹת. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
17.en: for the removal [of foodstuffs] on Shabbat and to the merging of alleyways. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda (see also Tractate Shabbat, Chapter Seven, Mishnah Four and Tractate Eruvin, Chapter 7, Mishnah 8).

17.he: כְּגוֹן כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת וּמִן הַנְּבֵלָה שֶׁמְּטַמֵּא, וְרֹב שִׁעוּרִים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בְכַזַּיִת:
17.en: as for example, like an olive’s bulk from the dead or from the carrion that ritually defiles, and most of the measurements that are in the Torah are like an olive’s bulk.

17.he: שֶׁשַּׁמְנוֹ אָגוּר בְּתוֹכוֹ:
17.en: whose oil is stored within it (see Tractate Berakhot 39a).

17.he: עֶצֶם כַּשְּׂעֹרָה:
17.en: a bone like a barleycorn (see also Tractate Negaim, Chapter Four, Mishnah Six).

17.he: שֶׁרֶץ מְטַמֵּא בְכָעֲדָשָׁה, וּמִחְיָה בְכָעֲדָשָׁה:
17.en: a creeping thing defiles like that of a lentil, and is sustenance like that of a lentil.

17.he: עַל אָדָם הַנּוֹשְׂאָן:
17.en: upon a person who carries them.

17.he: דְּהַיְנוּ מַלְמַד הַבָּקָר. וְעָבְיוֹ אֶצְבַּע וּשְׁלִישׁ אֶצְבַּע בְּגֻדָּל, שֶׁהֵם שְׁתֵּי אֶצְבָּעוֹת בִּקְטַנּוֹת. שֶׁהַטֶּפַח אַרְבַּע אֶצְבָּעוֹת בְּגֻדָּל, שֶׁהֵם שֵׁשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת קְטַנּוֹת. וְנִמְצָא הֶקֵּפוֹ טֶפַח. שֶׁכָּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בְּרָחְבּוֹ טֶפַח יֵשׁ בְּהֶקֵפוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים. וְגָזְרוּ עַל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בְּהֶקֵפוֹ טֶפַח, אַטּוּ עַל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בְּעָבְיוֹ טֶפַח שֶׁהוּא מֵבִיא אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה:
17.en: that is from the study of cattle, and its thickness is one finger and a third-of a finger in size, which are two fingers in smallness. And the handbreadth is four fingers in size, which are six small fingers. And it is found that its circumference is a handbreadth. For everything that is its width of a handbreadth there is in its circumference three handbreadths, but they (i.e., the Rabbis) decreed on that which has a circumference of a handbreadth, on account of that whose thickness is a handbreadth, that he brings the ritual defilement from the Torah.

17.he: לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת וְעֵרוּבִין וְסֻכָּה וּמִדּוֹת וְכִלְאַיִם:
17.en: to the matters of Shabbat and Eruvin and Sukkah and the measurements [of the Temple] and Kilayim/mixed seeds.

17.he: הִיא אַמָּה בַּת שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים. דְּאִיכָּא אַמָּה בַּת חֲמִשָּׁה [קְטַנָּה מִמֶּנָּה], וְאִיכָּא אַמָּה גְדוֹלָה בַּת שִׁשָּׁה וְאֶצְבַּע, וְאַמָּה בַּת שִׁשָּׁה הִיא הַבֵּינוֹנִית:
17.en: this cubit is six handbreadths long. For there is a cubit that is five [handbreadths] [that is smaller than it]. And there is larger cubit that is six [handbreadths] and a finger in length. But the cubit that is six [handbreadths] is the medium-sized one.

17.he: שְׁתֵּי מִדּוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶן מוֹדְדִים הָאַמּוֹת, וְכָל אַחַת מֵהֶן אַמָּה:
17.en: two measurements that with them they measure the cubits, and each one of them is a cubit.

17.he: חֶדֶר אֶחָד בָּנוּי עַל שַׁעַר מִזְרָחִי שֶׁל עֲזָרָה, וְעָלָיו שׁוּשָׁן הַבִּירָה מְצֻיֶּרֶת, כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא עֲלֵיהֶם אֵימַת מַלְכוּת:
17.en: one room is built on the eastern gate of the courtyard, and upon it, the capital city of Shushan is painted on it, in order that the fear of the kingdom be upon them.

17.he: עַל אַמָּה בַּת שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים:
17.en: on the cubit that is six handbreadths long.

17.he: שֶׁהָיָה הַגִּזְבָּר מַתְנֶה עִם הָאֻמָּנִים, כָּךְ וְכָךְ אַמּוֹת בִּנְיָן תַּעֲשׂוּ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת מֵאַמּוֹת שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה, בְּכָךְ וְכָךְ דָּמִים, וּמַחְזִירִים לוֹ בְמִדַּת הָאַמָּה הַיְתֵרָה עָלֶיהָ אֶצְבַּע, כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוֹסִיפוּ מִשֶּׁלָּהֶם עַל תְּנָאָם, פֶּן יִפְחֲתוּ וְנִמְצְאוּ בָאִין לִידֵי מְעִילָה שֶׁנֶּהֱנוּ מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ. וְלָמָּה שְׁתַּיִם, חֲדָא לְכַסְפָּא וְדַהֲבָא, שֶׁכְּשֶׁמַּתְנִים עִם צוֹרְפֵי זָהָב וָכֶסֶף לַעֲשׂוֹת טַבְלָא בַּת אַרְבַּע וְחָמֵשׁ אַמּוֹת בָּאַמָּה שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה, מַחֲזִירִים לַמִּדָּה הַיְתֵרָה עָלֶיהָ חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע, לֹא לַמִּדָּה הַיְתֵרָה עָלֶיהָ אֶצְבַּע, לְפִי שֶׁאֻמָּנוּת יְקָרָה הִיא וְאֵין מַפְסִידִין אוֹתָן כָּל כָּךְ:
17.en: that the treasurer/manager would make a condition with the artisans – such-and-such cubits they would make in the building for the keeping of the Temple in repair, from the cubits of Moses, such and such a costs, and they would return to him by a finger (see Tractate Menahot 98a) the measurement of the longer cubit upon it, in order that they would add from their own on their condition, lest they make it less, and it is found that they come to commit a religious sacrilege that they benefited from that which was dedicated to the Temple. And why two? One for silver and gold, that when they make a condition with those who smelt gold and silver to make a tablet of four or five cubits in the cubit of Moses, they restore to the extra measure of it a half-finger, not for the additional measurement upon it of a finger, since the artistry is costly and they don’t cause them to lose so much.

17.he: בְּאַמָּה בַּת שִׁשָּׁה:
17.en: which a cubit that is six handbreadths in length.

17.he: שֶׁהָיָה אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה:
17.en: that was a cubit by a cubit.

17.he: שֶׁל מִזְבַּח הַנְּחֹשֶׁת. שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ עַל אַרְבַּע פִּנּוֹתָיו אַרְבַּע אֲבָנִים שֶׁל אַמָּה גֹבַהּ, וְאַמָּה עַל אַמָּה עֳבִי. וְאוֹתָהּ אַמָּה הָיְתָה בְּאַמָּה בַּת חֲמִשָּׁה:
17.en: of the bronze altar. For it had on its four corners four stones of a cubit in height and a cubit by a cubit in thickness. And that cubit was with the cubit that was five [handbreadths in length].

17.he: שֶׁל מִזְבַּח הַנְּחֹשֶׁת. וּבְפֶרֶק ג'‏ דְּמַסֶּכֶת מִדּוֹת הֵן מְפֹרָשִׁים:
17.en: of the bronze altar. And in the third chapter of [Tractate] Middot, they are explained (see Tractate Middot, Chapter three, Mishnah one).

17.he: כְּגוֹן חוֹמַת הַבַּיִת וּמִזְבַּח הָעוֹלָה:
17.en: such as the wall of the Temple and the altar of the burnt-offering.

17.he: כְּגוֹן אָרוֹן וְשֻׁלְחָן וּמִזְבַּח הַזָּהָב. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר:
17.en: such as the Ark, and the table and the Golden Altar. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Meir.

17.he: שֶׁל מִדְבָּר קְרוּיָה מִדָּה דַקָּה. לְפִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ מִדְבָּרִית יְרוּשַׁלְמִית וְצִפּוֹרִית, וּמִדְבָּרִית קְטַנָּה שֶׁבְּכֻלָּן:
17.en: of the wilderness, it is called the smaller measure, because there is the Jerusalem wilderness and the Tzipori/Sepphoris [measurement] (in the Upper Galilee), but the wilderness one is smaller than all of them.

17.he: הִין וַחֲצִי הִין:
17.en: a Hin (i.e., twelve LOG or 72 egg bulks) and one-half of a Hin.

17.he: עִשָּׂרוֹן וַחֲצִי עִשָּׂרוֹן:
17.en: the Issaron (i.e., one-tenth of an Ephah) and the half-Issaron.

17.he: בְּמִדָּה שֶׁל אִיטָלִיאָה שֶׁל יָוָן. וְזוֹ הִיא מִדְבָּרִית שֶׁהָיְתָה בִימֵי מֹשֶׁה:
17.en: באיטלקי in the Italian measurement of Greece, and this is the wilderness one that existed at the time of Moses.

17.he: בֵּין קָטָן וּבֵין גָּדוֹל:
17.en: whether small or large [as in the size of the person].

17.he: דִּכְתִיב (ויקרא ב) וְקָמַץ מִמֶּנּוּ מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ:
17.en: as it is written (Leviticus 2:2): “[The priest] shall scoop out of it a handful [of its choice flour and oil, as well as all of its frankincense].”

17.he: שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, דִּכְתִיב (שם טז) וּמְלֹא חָפְנָיו קְטֹרֶת סַמִּים דַּקָּה:
17.en: of Yom Kippur, as it is written (Leviticus 16:12): “and two handfuls of finely ground aromatic incense.”

17.he: אִם שָׁתָה מְלֹא לֻגְמָיו בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, חַיָּב. וּלְפִי לֻגְמָיו שֶׁל שׁוֹתֶה מְשַׁעֲרִינַן:
17.en: if he drank a mouthful on Yom Kippur, he is liable. And according to the mouthful of the person who drinks we measure/estimate.

17.he: עֵרוּבֵי תְחוּמִין אֵינוֹ בְּפָחוֹת מִמְּזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת:
17.en: the joining of borders is not with less than food for two meals.

17.he: כְּמָזוֹן לִשְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת שֶׁל חֹל שֶׁאוֹכֵל מְעַט, וְלֹא כִמְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת שֶׁל שַׁבָּת דְּאָכֵיל טְפֵי, מִשּׁוּם דִּבְסִים תַּבְשִׁילֵיהּ, וְרַוְחָא לִבְסוּמֵי שְׁכִיחַ:
17.en: like the food for two meals of a weekday when he eats a little bit, but not like the food for two meals on Shabbat that he eats more because of the sweetness of his cooking, it is found that for delicacies there is always room.

17.he: דְּאַדְּרַבָּה, שְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת שֶׁל שַׁבָּת פְּחוּתִים מִשְּׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת שֶׁל חֹל, כֵּיוָן דִּבְשַׁבָּת סָעֵיד שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת, אֵינוֹ מַרְבֶּה לֶאֱכֹל בְּכָל סְעוּדָה:
17.en: for on the contrary, two meals of the Sabbath day are less than two meals of the weekday, because a person eats three meals on Shabbat and he doesn’t increase his eating at each meal.

17.he: כָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶן מִתְכַּוֵּן לְמָעֵט בַּכִּכָּר שֶׁל עֵרוּב:
17.en: each one of them intendents to lessen the loaf of the Eruv.

17.he: דַּי לָעֵרוּב בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת שֶׁל כִּכָּר שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ כִּכָּרוֹת לַקָּב, נִמְצָא כִכָּר שָׁלֵם שְׁלִישִׁית הַקָּב, וּשְׁתֵּי יְדוֹתֶיהָ הָוֵי כִּכָּר שֶׁל עֵרוּב:
17.en: משתי ידות לככר משלש לקב ([it should consist] of two-thirds of a loaf [of a size] three to the Kab)-it is enough for an Eruv with two-thirds of loaf of [a size] three loaves to the Kab. It is found that a complete loaf is one-third of a Kab, and its two-thirds of a loaf is a loaf of the Eruv.

17.he: כִּכָּר הַלָּקוּחַ בְּפֻנְדְּיוֹן מִן הַנַּחְתּוֹם כְּשֶׁנִּמְכָּרִים אַרְבַּע סְאִים בְּסֶלַע. וְאַרְבַּע סְאִים הֵן עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה קַבִּין שֶׁכָּל סְאָה הִיא שִׁשָּׁה קַבִּין, וְהַסֶּלַע הִיא אַרְבָּעָה דִינָרִים, וְהַדִּינָר שֵׁשׁ מָעִין, נִמְצָא הַסֶּלַע עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע מָעִין, וְנִמְצָא עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה קַבִּין לְעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מָעִין קַב לְכָל מָעָה, וְהַמָּעָה שְׁנֵי פֻנְדְּיוֹנִים, הֲרֵי הַכִּכָּר הַנִּמְכָּר בְּפֻנְדְּיוֹן הוּא חֲצִי קַב. אֲבָל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַחֶנְוָנִי רוֹצֶה לְהִשְׂתַּכֵּר, וִיצִיאַת הָאֲפִיָּה וְהַטְּחִינָה, לֹא יִהְיֶה הַכִּכָּר הַנִּמְכָּר בְּפֻנְדְּיוֹן כְּשֶׁנִּמְכָּרִים אַרְבַּע סְאִין בְּסֶלַע אֶלָּא רֹבַע קַב, וְהָרֹבַע הָאַחֵר הוֹלֵךְ בִּשְׂכַר הַחֶנְוָנִי וִיצִיאַת הָאֲפִיָּה וְהַטְּחִינָה. הֲרֵי כִּכָּר הַלָּקוּחַ בְּפֻנְדְּיוֹן הוּא רֹבַע הַקַּב, דְּהַיְנוּ שֵׁשׁ בֵּיצִים, וְהוּא שִׁעוּר שְׁתֵּי סְעֻדּוֹת, וְהַיְנוּ כִכָּר שֶׁל עֵרוּב. וְכֵן הֲלָכָה:
17.en: a loaf that is purchased with a Pundiyon/Dupondium (a Roman coin equal to two I ssar/16 Perutot) from the baker when four Seah of what are worth one Sela. And four Seah are twenty-four Kab that each Seah is six Kabim. And the Sela is four Denarim and the Denar is worth six Ma’ah, and he Ma’ah is worth two Pundiyonim, therefore, the loaf that is sold for Pundiyon is one-half of Kab. But because the shopkeeper wishes to make a profit, and the costs of baking and grinding , the loaf will not be sold for a Pundiyon when they are sold four Seah for a Sela, but rather one-quarter of a Kab, and the other one-quarter goes to the profit of the shopkeeper and the expenses of baking and grinding. Therefore, a loaf that is purchased for a Pundiyon is one-quarter of a Kab, which is six eggs, and it is the measurement of two meals, which is the loaf of the Eruv. And this is the Halakha (according to Rabbi Yohanan ben Beroka).

17.he: מְלֹא כַף עַפְרוּרִית מִן הַמֵּת אַחַר שֶׁכָּלָה כָּל לַחוּת שֶׁבּוֹ:
17.en: see also – Tractate Nazir, Chapter 7, Mishnah 2 (a spoonful of Rakab) – he filled a spoon of sandy-matter of grain from the corpse after all the moistness has been depleted.

17.he: שֶׁהוּא גָדוֹל מִשְּׁאָר תַּרְוָדִים. וְשִׁעוּרוֹ מְלֹא חָפְנַיִם:
17.en: two handfuls) – which is larger than all the ladles, and its measure is two handfuls.

17.he: כַּחֲצִי פוֹל הַבָּא מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ קִלְקִי, וְהַפּוֹלִים שֶׁבּוֹ גְּדוֹלִים מִשְּׁאָר פּוֹלִים. וְשִׁעוּר מְקוֹם גְּרִיס הַקִּלְקִי, תֵּשַׁע עֲדָשׁוֹת שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מְרֻבָּעוֹת. וּמְקוֹם עֲדָשָׁה, אַרְבַּע שְׂעָרוֹת, נִמְצָא מְקוֹם הַגְּרִיס שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשֵׁשׁ שְׂעָרוֹת:
17.en: it is a bean that comes from a place whose name is Kilki, and the beans there are larger than all other beans. And the measure of the place of the Cilician split bean is nine lentils, three-by-three square. And the place of the lentil, is four hairs, and it is found that the place of split bean is thirty-six hairs.

17.he: גְּדוֹלָה מִשְּׁאָר תְּמָרִים. וְשִׁעוּרָהּ מְעַט פָּחוֹת מִכַּבֵּיצָה:
17.en: larger than other date-palms, and its measure is a bit less than that of an egg.

17.he: שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִמְעֹךְ חֲלָלָהּ:
17.en: that one must crush its open space.

17.he: שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁנִּקְּבוּ, שִׁעוּר הַנֶּקֶב שֶׁלָּהֶן:
17.en: of leather that were perforated, the measure of their perforation.

17.he: שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים בַּפֶּלֶךְ כְּשֶׁהַנָּשִׁים טֹווֹת בּוֹ:
17.en: that they place in the spindle that women spin with.

17.he: כְּמִין חַלּוֹן שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ הָאוֹרָה נִכְנֶסֶת לַבַּיִת:
17.en: it is a kind of window from which the light enters into the house.

17.he: כְּגוֹן חוֹר שֶׁחֵרְרוּהוּ מַיִם אוֹ שְׁרָצִים, אוֹ שֶׁנָּפַל הֶעָפָר מֵאֵלָיו וְנַעֲשָׂה שָׁם נֶקֶב. וְאִם לֹא חָשַׁב עָלָיו לְתַשְׁמִישׁ אוֹ לְמָאוֹר, שִׁעוּרוֹ לְהָבִיא אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה מֵאֹהֶל הַמֵּת לַבַּיִת לְדֶרֶךְ הַנֶּקֶב:
17.en: as for example a cavity/hole that water or reptiles make, or that the dirt fell on its own and a perforation was made there. But if he did not think of it for use or for as a source of light, its measure to bring the defilement from the tent of the corpse to the house through the path of the incision.

17.he: דְּהַיְנוּ אָדָם יָדוּעַ אֶצְלָם, וּבֶן בָּטִיחַ שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁהָיָה אֶגְרוֹפוֹ גָדוֹל:
17.en: that is a man known among them and Ben Batiach is his name, that he had a large fist.

17.he: שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ אָדָם לְהַכְנִיס אֶת הָאוֹרָה:
17.en: or that a person made it to bring in the light.

17.he: מַטְבֵּעַ שֶׁל נֵירוֹן קֵיסָר:
17.en: a coin of Nero Caesar.

17.he: מְלֹא מַקְדֵּחַ שֶׁל לִשְׁכָּה. וּפֻנְדְּיוֹן הָאִיטַלְקִי וְסֶלַע הַנֵּירוֹנִית וּמְלֹא נֶקֶב שֶׁבָּעֹל, כֻּלָּן שִׁעוּר אֶחָד לָהֶן. וְיֵשׁ מְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ יוֹדְעִים בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן וְלֹא בְאַחֵר, הִלְכָּךְ תְּנִינְהוּ לְכֻלְּהוּ:
17.en: like [the hole made by] the larger carpenters’ borer kept in the Temple cell. And the Italian Pundiyon and the Neronian stone, and the hole in a yoke, all of them is one measurement. But there are places where they knew about one of them, but not the other, Therefore, we teach all of them.

17.he: כָּל בְּרִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּיָּם אִם עָשָׂה מֵעוֹרָן כֵּלִים, אֵין מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה, דִּכְתִיב (ויקרא יא) אוֹ בֶגֶד אוֹ עוֹר אוֹ שַׂק, מַה בֶּגֶד מִן הַגָּדֵל מִן הָאָרֶץ, אַף עוֹר מִן הַגָּדֵל מִן הָאָרֶץ:
17.en: all the creatures that are I the sea, if he made vessels from their skin, they do not receive defilement, as it is written (Leviticus 11:32): “[And anything on which one of them falls when dead shall be impure: be it any article of wood,] or a cloth, or a skin, or a sack –[any such article that can be put to use shall be dipped in water, and it shall remain impure until evening, then it shall be pure],” just as cloth is from something that grows from the earth, even too the skin that that which grows in the earth.

17.he: לְפִי שֶׁכָּל שְׁאָר בְּרִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּיָּם אֵין אֶחָד מֵהֶם בּוֹרֵחַ לַיַּבָּשָׁה כְּשֶׁבָּאִים לָצוּד אוֹתָם, אֶלָּא כֶלֶב הַיָּם בִּלְבַד, הִלְכָּךְ הָוֵי בִכְלַל עוֹרוֹת הַיַּבָּשָׁה, וְאִם עָשָׂה כְלִי מֵעוֹרוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
17.en: because all the rest of the creatures of the sea – not one of them flees to the dry land when [hunters] come to hunt them, other than the sea dog alone, therefore, it is included within the skins of the dry land, and if he made a vessel from its skin, it is susceptible to receive defilement. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Akiva.

17.he: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּחַבְּרֶנּוּ לוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִם הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם מִן הַגָּדֵל בָּאָרֶץ מְחֻבָּרִים בְּחִבּוּר כָּזֶה הָיָה טָמֵא הָאֶחָד כְּשֶׁנִּטְמָא חֲבֵרוֹ:
17.en: and as long as he connects them for himself on the road that if both of them were from what grows on the land are attached with a connection like this, the one would become defiled when its partner was defiled.

17.dibur: יֵשׁ בְּמַה שֶּׁנִּבְרָא בַיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן טֻמְאָה.
17.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר, יֵשׁ דְּבָרִים שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ בְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהָעוֹשֶׂה כְלִי מֵהֶם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם טֻמְאָה, כְּגוֹן הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּבְרֵאת בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, וּכְלֵי חֶרֶס הַנַּעֲשִׂים מִמֶּנָּה טְמֵאִים:
17.en: this is what he said: There are things that were created on the First Day [of the Creation of the world], that one who makes vessels from them, they have ritual defilement, such as the land which was created on the first day, and earthenware vessels that are made from it are ritually defiled.

17.he: שֶׁבּוֹ נִבְרָא רָקִיעַ וְאֵין בּוֹ טֻמְאָה:
17.en: for on it, the firmament was created and it lacks ritual defilement.

17.he: נִבְרְאוּ אִילָנוֹת, וּכְלֵי עֵץ הַנַּעֲשִׂים מֵהֶם מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה:
17.en: [on the third day] trees were created, and wood vessels made from them are susceptible to receive ritual defilement.

17.he: נִתְלוּ הַמְּאוֹרוֹת, וְאֵין בָּהֶם טֻמְאָה:
17.en: the heavenly lights were suspended [in the sky], and they lack ritual defilement.

17.he: עוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים, וְאִם עָשָׂה מֵהֶן כֵּלִים אֵין מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה:
17.en: [on the Fifth day] birds and fish [were created], and if he made vessels from them, they are not susceptible to receive ritual defilement.

17.he: כְּנַף הָעָזְנִיָּה. דְּרַבָּנָן גָּזְרוּ טֻמְאָה בְכֵלִים הַנַּעֲשִׂים מִמֶּנָּה, דְּאָתֵי לְאַחְלוּפֵי בִשְׁאָר כֵּלִים:
17.en: the wing of the black eagle, for the Rabbis decreed ritual defilement with vessels made from her, for one can come to switch it with other vessels.

17.he: בַּת הַיַּעֲנָה מְתַרְגְּמִינַן נַעֲמִיתָא. וְרַבָּנָן גָּזְרוּ טֻמְאָה בְבֵיצָתָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא מְצֻפָּה, כֵּיוָן דִּבְלֹא צִפּוּי נַמִּי עוֹמֶדֶת. אֲבָל בִּשְׁאָר בֵּיצִים, אֲפִלּוּ בִמְצֻפָּה לֹא גָזְרוּ, כֵּיוָן דִּבְאֵינָהּ מְצֻפָּה לֹא קַיְמָא כְלָל:
17.en: we translate into Aramaic the בת היענה (see Leviticus 11:16) – the egg of an ostrich is called נעמיתא/an ostrich egg. But the Rabbis decreed ritual defilement on its egg when it is a glazed shell, since without he covering, it also stands, but the rest of the eggs, even with a glazed shell, they did not make a decree, since it is not covered, it doesn’t exist at all.

17.he: חַיּוֹת וּבְהֵמוֹת וּשְׁרָצִים וְאָדָם. אִם עָשָׂה כֵלִים מֵעַצְמוֹתֵיהֶן אוֹ מֵעוֹרוֹתֵיהֶן, מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה:
17.en: beasts and animals and reptiles and mankind [were created on the Sixth day of Creation], if one made vessels from their bones or from their skins, they are susceptible to receive ritual defilement.

17.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ לֹא עֲשָׂאוֹ רָאוּי לְקַבֵּל אֶלָּא מַשֶּׁהוּ:
17.en: and even if he did not make it, it is worthy to receive [ritual defilement] other than something.

17.he: לִישִׁיבָה מֻעֶטֶת. כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה נִשְׁעָן אוֹ נִתְלֶה בוֹ:
17.en: for sitting a little bit, as for example, that he was leaning or suspended upon it.

17.he: דְּלֹא מָלִיחַ וְלֹא קָמִיחַ וְלֹא עָפִיץ:
17.en: that it was not pickled nor its hides dressed with flour, nor tanned [with gall-nut].

17.he: הֶעָשׂוּי מֵעֲשָׂבִים:
17.en: that is made from grasses.

17.he: כֵּיוָן שֶׁחֲקָקוּם:
17.en: since they hollowed them out [to shape a vessel].

17.he: אִם חָשְׁבוּ לָמֹד בָּהֶן עָפָר כְּמוֹת שֶׁהֵן חֲקוּקִים מֵאֲלֵיהֶן וְלֹא עָשׂוּ בָהֶן מְלָאכָה, אֵין מַחְשַׁבְתָּן מְבִיאָתָן לִידֵי טֻמְאָה:
17.en: if they thought to fashion the dirt as it fashioned on is own, but they didn’t do any work, their intention does not bring them to ritual defilement.

17.he: הָרַמָּאִים עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ חָלוּל וּמַנִּיחִין בַּחֲלָלוֹ כֶסֶף חַי, וּכְשֶׁשּׁוֹקְלִין מַטִּין בַּקָּנֶה מְעַט וְהוֹלֵךְ הַכֶּסֶף חַי לְצַד הַדָּבָר הַנִּשְׁקָל וּמַכְבִּיד וּמַכְרִיעוֹ:
17.en: The deceivers make it hollowed out and place in the hallowed out section, pure silver, and when they weigh it, it diverts/perverts the beam a bit and the live silver goes to the side of the thing that is being weighted and makes it heavy and overwhelms it.

17.he: שֶׁמּוֹחֲקִין בּוֹ הַמִּדָּה כְשֶׁהִיא גְדוּשָׁה. וְאִם עוֹשִׂין אוֹתָהּ שֶׁל דְּלַעַת וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָהּ מִן הַדְּבָרִים הַקַּלִּים, הוּא מֵקֵל, וְרַע לַמּוֹכֵר. וְאִם עוֹשִׂים אוֹתוֹ מִמַּתֶּכֶת, הוּא מַכְבִּיד, וְרַע לַלּוֹקֵחַ. אֲבָל עוֹשִׂים אוֹתוֹ שֶׁל זַיִת וְשֶׁל אֱגוֹז וְשֶׁל אֶשְׁכְּרוֹעַ. וְהָרַמַּאי עוֹשֶׂה הַמָּחוֹק שֶׁל זַיִת וְשֶׁל אֱגוֹז חָלוּל, כְּשֶׁהוּא מוֹכֵר מַכְנִיס בּוֹ מַתֶּכֶת כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּכְבִּיד, וּכְשֶׁהוּא קוֹנֶה מְסַלְּקוֹ:
17.en: that blots out the measurement when it is heaped up. But if they make it of gourds/cucumbers and similar things like it from the light things which lighten it and are bad for the seller, but if one makes of metal which makes it heavy and bad for the purchaser. But one makes it of olives and nuts and of box-tree/ebony tree. But the deceiver makes the instrument for levelling a measure of grain of olive and of hallowed out nuts, and when he sells it, he brings in metal in order that it would be made heavy, but when he purchases, he removes it.

17.he: מוֹט שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִים בּוֹ בַכָּתֵף. וּכְשֶׁיֶּשׁ פּוֹעֲלִים מְרֻבִּים, לְאַחַר שֶׁקִּבֵּל שָׂכָר מֵשִׂים בְּבֵית קִבּוּל שֶׁבַּמּוֹט אֶת שְׂכָרוֹ, וְאוֹמֵר לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת לֹא נָתַתָּ לִי שְׂכָרִי, וּכְשֶׁמְּחַפְּשִׂים אוֹתוֹ אֵין נוֹתְנִים לֵב לְחַפֵּשׂ שָׁם:
17.en: in which there is a hidden receptacle for money) – a balancing pole/staff that they carry it on the shoulder. But when there are many workers, after he has received his payment/compensation, he places the compensation in the receptacle that is in the balancing pole/staff, and states to the house owner (i.e., the boss), “You did not give me my compensation,” and when they search him, they don’t give attention to search there [in the carrying pole].

17.dibur: קָנֶה שֶׁל עָנִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל מַיִם.
17.he: וְשׁוֹתֶה מֵהֶן, וּכְשֶׁשּׁוֹאֲלִים אוֹתוֹ אִם טָעַם כְּלוּם, אוֹמֵר אֲנִי מִתְעַנֶּה הַיּוֹם. וְרַבּוֹתַי פֵּרְשׁוּ, בֵּית קִבּוּל מַיִם, בֵּית קִבּוּל מַשְׁקִין, וּכְשֶׁטּוֹרֵחַ אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בְּבֵית הַבַּד גּוֹנֵב בּוֹ מִן הַשֶּׁמֶן:
17.en: and he drinks from them, and when they ask him if he tasted anything, he states, “I am fasting today.” But My Rabbis explained, a receptacle for water is a receptacle for liquids, and when he is busy [with his work] with the owner/the boss in the olive press, he steals from the oil there.

17.dibur: מַקֵּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל מְזוּזָה וּמַרְגָּלִית.
17.he: וְעוֹשִׂין כֵּן כְּדֵי לִגְנֹב בּוֹ אֶת הַמֶּכֶס:
17.en: and they use them as such in order to steal in it the taxes/tolls.

17.he: שֶׁמָּא יִלְמְדוּ מִמֶּנִּי בְנֵי אָדָם לְרַמּוֹת:
17.en: perhaps/lest that people learn from me to deceive [others].

17.he: שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ הָרַמָּאִין, אֵין תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּקִיאִים בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֵינוּ, וּמִתּוֹךְ כָּךְ יָבֹאוּ לְרַמּוֹת יוֹתֵר. וְלָמָּה אֲמָרָם, מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב (הושע יד) כִּי יְשָׁרִים דַּרְכֵי ה'‏ צַדִּיקִים יֵלְכוּ בָם וּפוֹשְׁעִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ בָם:
17.en: perhaps/lest the deceivers will say that the Sages are not experts in the work of our hands, and through this they will come to deceive even more. And why did he say [these things]? Because it is written (Hosea 14:10): “For the paths of the LORD are smooth; The righteous can walk on them, while sinners stumble on them.”

17.he: צוֹרְפֵי זָהָב וָכֶסֶף יֵשׁ תַּחְתֵּיהֶם כְּלִי שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ תַחְתִּית, וְהוּא עָשׂוּי לָתֵת בְּתוֹכוֹ גְרוּטָאוֹת שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁל זָהָב. אֲבָל שֶׁל נַפָּחִים אֵין עָשׂוּי לְקַבֵּל וְלֹא מְיֻחָד נַמִּי לִישִׁיבָה:
17.en: those who smelter gold and silver, their bottoms/base are a vessel which is called a frame in which an anvil is set. And it is made to place within it silver and/or gold rubbish/broken ware. But that of a smith is not made to receive, and it is not made explicitly also for sitting.

17.he: שֶׁל עֵץ שֶׁמַּשְׁחִיזִין בָּהּ אֶת הַסַּכִּין. וְעוֹשִׂין לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל שֶׁמֶן, שֶׁמּוֹשְׁחִין בָּהּ שֶׁמֶן לְהַשְׁחִיז:
17.en: of wood that they sharpen/whet the knives. And they make for it a receptacle for oil that they smear [the implements] with oil to sharpen them.

17.he: שֶׁיֶּשׁ לַחֶנְוָנִי וְלַשֻּׁלְחָנִי שֶׁכּוֹתֵב עָלָיו בְּחֶרֶט:
17.en: that the storekeeper has and the money changer that he writes upon it with a stylus/engraving tool.

17.he: זַנְבוֹת הַשִּׁבֳּלִים. וְעוֹשִׂים מֵהֶם מַחְצְלָאוֹת:
17.en: the tails of the ears of grain, and make mats out of them.

17.he: שֶׁהוּא חָלוּל וְיֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית קִבּוּל:
17.en: which is hollow and it has a receptacle.

17.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקִּבּוּלוֹ מֻעָט, דְּהָא תְנַן לְעֵיל הָעוֹשֶׂה כְלִי קִבּוּל מִכָּל מָקוֹם טָמֵא. וְקָמִפְלְגֵי אִי הָוֵי דָבָר הָעוֹמֵד אִי לֹא, דְּאֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא דָבָר הָעוֹמֵד מֵאֵלָיו. וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא חֲשִׁיב לֵיהּ דָּבָר הָעוֹמֵד, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לָא חֲשִׁיב לֵיהּ דָּבָר הָעוֹמֵד. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
17.en: and even though its receptacle is small, for it is taught in the Mishnah above (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 17, Mishnah 15), “that a person who makes a receptacle of any sort – it is ritually defiled.” And there is a difference of opinion if it is thing that is standing or not, for there is nothing unclean/defiled other than if it stands on its own. But Rabbi Akiva considers something that is standing, whereas Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri does not consider for himself something that is standing. But the Halakha is according to Rabbi Akiva.

17.he: דְּלַעַת מִדְבָּרִית. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים אֲבַטִּיחִים קְטַנִּים מָרִים, וְקָנֶה שֶׁלָּהֶן חָלוּל כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁל קַשׁ:
17.en: a desert gourd. But there are those who say, small, bitter melons. And their reed is hollow like the tube of straw.

17.he: מִין עֵשֶׂב הוּא וְעוֹשִׂים מִמֶּנּוּ חֲלָפִים וּמַחְצְלָאוֹת. וְקוֹרִין לוֹ בַעֲרָבִי חלפ"ה:
17.en: it is a kind of grass and they make from it shoots/rush and mats. And they call it CHALFA in Arabic.

17.he: מִטֻּמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ. אֲבָל לֹא מִמִּשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב. שֶׁהִיא מִטַּמְּאָה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב דְּאוֹרַיְתָא אִם אֵינָהּ עֲשׂוּיָה לְסַכֵּךְ:
17.en: from the ritual defilement of a reptile, but not from laying and sitting, for according to the Torah, if it is not made for overhanging boughs or twigs.

17.he: לָתֵת בּוֹ כְּחֹל וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ:
17.en: to place in it powder for painting the eye-lids/stibium.

17.he: הַמֹּחַ הַלָּבָן שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַקָּנֶה. וְקֹדֶם לָכֵן אֵין לַקָּנֶה טֻמְאָה וַאֲפִלּוּ מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים:
17.en: the white marrow that is withing the reed. But prior to this, the reed does no have susceptibility to receive defilement, and even according to the words of the Scribes.

18.he: נִמְדֶּדֶת מִבִּפְנִים. דִּתְנַן לְעֵיל (פרק טו) כְּלֵי עֵץ שֶׁהַמַּחֲזִיק אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה בְלַח שֶׁהֵן כּוֹרַיִם בְּיָבֵשׁ, טָהוֹר, וְהַיְנוּ אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה בְרוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת. וְהָכָא קָמִפְלְגֵי כֵיצַד מוֹדְדִים, לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי מוֹדְדִין חָלָל שֶׁבִּפְנִים, וְלֹא עֳבִי הַדְּפָנוֹת וְהַשּׁוּלַיִם. וּלְבֵית הִלֵּל הַכֹּל מוֹדְדִין, חוּץ מֵעֳבִי הָרַגְלַיִם וּלְבַזְבְּזִים שֶׁהוּא הַזֵּר שֶׁעַל הַשָּׂפָה. וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מוֹדְדִים אַף עֳבִי רַגְלֵי הַשִּׁדָּה וְהַלְּבַזְבְּזִים. וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִם אֵין רַגְלֶיהָ גְּבוֹהִים טֶפַח מוֹדְדִים אַף הָאֲוִיר שֶׁבֵּין רֶגֶל לְרֶגֶל. וַהֲלָכָה כְּבֵית הִלֵּל אַלִּיבָּא דְתַנָּא קַמָּא:
18.en: as it is taught in the Mishnah above (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 15, Mishnah 1), all wooden utensils that hold forty Seah in something moist, which are iron tools for crowding olives into the vat when dry, is ritually pure, that is a cubit by a cubit by a height of three cubits. And here there is a matter of dispute – how does one measure it? According to the School of Shammai, they measure the hollow that is within, and not the thickness of the walls and rims. But according to the School of Hillel, they measure except from the thickness of the legs and the vertical rim/edge (by which a flat vessel is made into a vessel-like receptacle) which he pressed/molded on the rim. And according to Rabi Yossi, hey measure the thickness of the legs of the chest and the vertical rim. But according to Rabbi Shimon, if its legs are not a handbreadth high, they measure even the airspace that is between each leg. But the Halakha is according to the School of Hillel in accordance with the first Tanna/teacher.

18.he: אוֹפַן כְּעֵין אוֹפַנֵּי הָעֲגָלָה. וּלְפִי שֶׁהַשִּׁדָּה נִשֵּׂאת עָלֶיהָ קְרוּיָה מוּכְנִי. לְשׁוֹן אֶת הַכִּיּוֹר וְאֶת כַּנּוֹ (שמות ל):
18.en: it is a wheel, like a sort of wheels of a wagon, and since the chest is carried upon it, it is called a מוכני/wheel-work. It is the language of (Exodus 30:28): “and the laver and its stand.”

18.he: שֶׁאָדָם יָכוֹל לְסַלְּקָהּ מִן הָעֲגָלָה:
18.en: that a person may remove it from the wheel.

18.he: וְהִיא חֲשׁוּבָה כְּלִי לְעַצְמָהּ. וְאִי שִׁדָּה בַּת קִבּוּלֵי טֻמְאָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְנִטְמֵאת הַשִּׁדָּה, לֹא נִטְמֵאת הַמּוּכְנִי, וְאִי לָאו בַּת קִבּוּלֵי טֻמְאָה הִיא וְנָגְעָה טֻמְאָה בַמּוּכְנִי, הַמּוּכְנִי טְמֵאָה, דְּלָא חֲשִׁיבָא מִן הַשִּׁדָּה, וְהִיא מִטַּלְטֶלֶת מְלֵאָה וְרֵיקָנִית וְיֵשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל:
18.en: and it is considered a vessel to itself. But if is a chest with a receptacle, it is a defilement that does not hold forty Seah, and the chest is defiled, but the wheel-work is not defiled, but if it is not a receptacle, it is defilement, and the defilement came in contact with the wheel-work, the wheel-work is ritually impure, because it is not considered from the chest, and it is carried full and empty and there is a receptacle.

18.he: בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹן אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה בְּרוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת. דְּלָא חֲשִׁיבָא כָעֳבִי הָרַגְלַיִם, וַאֲפִלּוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֵינָהּ נִמְדֶּדֶת עִמָּהּ:
18.en: in the accounting of a cubit by a cubit at the height of three cubits, for it is considered like the thickness of the legs, and even according to Rabbi Yossi, it is not measured with it.

18.he: שֶׁאִם הַשִּׁדָּה בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת מַצֶּלֶת עַל כֵּלִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ, כֵּיוָן דְּמַחְזֶקֶת אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה. וְאִם בּוֹלְטִים מִמֶּנָּה כֵּלִים כְּנֶגֶד [גֹּבַהּ] הַמּוּכְנִי מִלְּמַעְלָה, אֵין הַמּוּכְנִי מַצֶּלֶת עָלֶיהָ, דְּמוּכְנִי מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה וְאֵינָהּ חוֹצֶצֶת בִּפְנֵי הַטֻּמְאָה:
18.en: for if the chest is in the cemetery, it protects over the vessels that are within it, since it supports/strengthens forty Seah. But if vessels protrude from it corresponding [to the height] of the wheel-work from above, the wheel-work does not protect it, for a wheel-work is susceptible to receive defilement and does not interpose before the defilement.

18.he: דִּכְלִי בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ הִיא, וּבָסִיס לְדָבָר הָאָסוּר. אֲבָל אִם אֵינָהּ נִשְׁמֶטֶת שָׁרֵי, מֵאַחַר דְּלֹא הָווּ בְתוֹךְ הַשִּׁדָּה שֶׁהִיא עִקַּר הַכְּלִי:
18.en: it is a vessel of is own accord, and is the base for a prohibited thing, but it is permitted if it is not detached, for after that they were not within the chest which is the essence of the vessel.

18.he: כְּעֵין קֻבָּא שֶׁעוֹשִׂין עַל גַּבֵּי הַשִּׁדָּה:
18.en: like a kind of arched compartment over the chest.

18.he: לְהַשְׁלִים אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה:
18.en: to complete the forty Seah.

18.he: כְּשֶׁהוּא קָבוּעַ:
18.en: when it is fixed.

18.he: בַּאֲלַכְסוֹן. דְּהַאי קִמְרוֹן אֵינוֹ כְנֶגֶד כָּל הַשִּׁדָּה אֶלָּא כִפָּה כְנֶגֶד מִקְצָת חֲלָלָהּ, וּכְשֶׁבָּא לִמְדֹּד אֲוִירָהּ רוֹאִין כְּאִלּוּ חוּט נָתוּן בַּאֲלַכְסוֹן מִכֹּתֶל הַשִּׁדָּה עַד רֹאשׁ הַכִּפָּה, וְחָלָל שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו נִמְדָּד:
18.en: a diagonal line. For this arched lid does not correspond to the entire chest, but rather it covers over part of the empty space, and he comes to measure the airspace, we view it as if a chord is placed in the diagonal line from the wall of the chest until the top of the arch, and the empty space that is below it is measured.

18.dibur: אִם אֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ.
18.he: הַשִּׁדָּה בְלֹא הַקִּמְרוֹן הַקָּבוּעַ בָּהּ:
18.en: the chest without the arched lid that is fixed in it.

18.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
18.en: even though it does not hold forty Seah. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

18.he: כְּלוֹמַר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִקְּבוּ בִנְטִילַת הָרַגְלַיִם וְיֵשׁ לָהֶן בֵּית קִבּוּל כְּבַתְּחִלָּה:
18.en: that is to say, even though they did not make an incision while taking the legs, and they have a receptacle as at the outset.

18.he: שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּטַּל אַחַת מִן רַגְלֵיהֶן שׁוּב אֵינָן חֲשׁוּבִין כְּלִי, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין כְּדַרְכָּן אֶלָּא נוֹטִין לְצַד אֶחָד וְכִשְׁבוּרִים דָּמוּ:
18.en: that since he took one of their legs off, they were no longer regarded as a vessel, because they do not receive/retain in their manner, but rather lean to one side and are like they are broken.

18.he: כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא נִקְּבוּ בִנְטִילַת אַחַת מֵרַגְלֵיהֶן. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי. וְרַמְבַּ"ם גָּרֵיס, וְשֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלִים כְּדַרְכָּן רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא. וּמִלְּתָא בְאַנְפֵּי נַפְשַׁהּ הִיא, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר, שִׁדָּה תֵבָה וּמִגְדָּל שֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה כְּשֶׁהֵן יוֹשְׁבִין כְּדַרְכָּן וְאִם מַטִּין אוֹתָן מְקַבְּלִין אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין מְקַבְּלִים כְּדַרְכָּן, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים הוֹאִיל וּמְקַבְּלִים מִכָּל מָקוֹם, חֲשִׁיבֵי מַחְזִיקִים אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וּטְהוֹרִין:
18.en: since no incision had been made in them with the removal of one of their legs. But the Halakah is not according to Rabbi Yossi. But Maimonides had a different reading:"ושאינן מקבלים כדרכן ר' יוסי מטמא." (i.e., instead of saying: “even though that they do not contain something according to their usual fashion. Rabbi Yossi declares ritually impure/unclean,” Maimonides’ version of the text states, “they do not contain something according to their usual fashion.”). But it is something for itself, and this is how he understood it. A chest, a box and a turret which do not contain forty Seah when they sit in the prescribed manner, if one tilts them/causes them to lean, they contain forty Seah, Rabbi Yossi declares them unclean/impure since they don’t contain according to their usual fashion, but the Sages state for since that they do contain/retain, nevertheless, they are considered and containing forty Seah and are pure.

18.he: שְׁנֵי עַמּוּדִים אֶחָד מְרַאֲשׁוֹתֵי הַמִּטָּה וְאֶחָד בְּמַרְגְּלוֹתֶיהָ, וּמְשִׂימִין מַקֵּל מִזֶּה לָזֶה וּמַשְׁלִיכִין עָלָיו סָדִין וְנַעֲשֶׂה אֹהֶל:
18.en: two pillars, one from about the head of the bed and one at its foot and they place a staff from one to the other and cast a sheet over it and it becomes a tent.

18.he: תַּחַת מַלְבֵּן הַמִּטָּה מְשִׂימִין עֵץ חָלוּל שֶׁהַמַּלְבֵּן מֻנָּח עָלָיו וְנִקְרָא חֲמוֹר:
18.en: under the frame of the bed, they place a hallow piece of wood that he frame is lying upon, and it is called a חמור/a stand.

18.he: כְּגוֹן צִפּוּי שֶׁמְּצַפִּים הַמִּטָּה וְנַקְלִיטֶיהָ:
18.en: as for example, a covering that cover the bed and its poles.

18.he: דַּהֲוֵי מַתֶּכֶת הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְעֵץ:
18.en: that is metal which serves the wood.

18.he: לוּחוֹת חֲלוּלִים עֲשׂוּיִים לְהַנִּיחַ תַּחַת כַּרְעֵי הַמִּטָּה שֶׁלֹּא יֵרָקְבוּ מִלַּחְלוּחִית הַקַּרְקַע. וּמִטַּלְטְלִים עִם הַמִּטָּה, הִלְכָּךְ טְמֵאִים, דְּכַמִּטָּה דָמוּ:
18.en: hollow tablets made to be placed under the legs of the bed so that they do not rot from the moistness of the ground, and they are carried with the bed, therefore they are ritually impure, for they are similar to the bed.

18.he: לְפִי שֶׁרְגִילִין לַעֲלוֹת לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְהוֹלְכִים מֵעִיר לְעִיר, וְאֵין מוֹלִיכִין הַמִּטּוֹת עִמָּהֶן וּמוֹלִיכִין הַמַּלְבְּנִים, הִלְכָּךְ אֲפִלּוּ קְבוּעִים בְּקַרְקְעֵי הַמִּטָּה הוֹאִיל וְסוֹפָן לִנָּטֵל לָאו כַּמִּטָּה חֲשִׁיבֵי:
18.en: because they would regularly go to Jerusalem and would go from city to city and they don’t bring the beds with them but they do bring the frames, therefore, even though they are fixed in the bottoms of the bed, for since they will ultimately be taken up, they are not considered like the bed.

18.he: עֵץ הֶעָשׂוּי כְּעֵין לָשׁוֹן שֶׁהַמַּלְבֵּן מֻנָּח עָלָיו:
18.en: wood made like a longue that the bed frame is lying upon.

18.he: שֶׁאַף הוּא מִטַּלְטֵל עִם הַמִּטָּה כְּמוֹ מַלְבֵּן:
18.en: that even this is carried with the bed like the frame.

18.he: דְּלֹא מִטַּלְטֵל בַּהֲדֵי מִטָּה כֻלֵּי הַאי. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
18.en: that it is not carried with the bed all that much. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yossi and Rabbi Shimon.

18.he: וְאַף עַל גַּב דִּקְבִיעֵי בְכַרְעֵי הַמִּטָּה, הוֹאִיל וְסוֹפָן לִנָּטֵל טְהוֹרִים, הָנֵי לְשׁוֹנוֹת נַמִּי פְעָמִים נִטָּלִים מִמַּלְבְּנֵי הַמִּטָּה וְלָאו כַּמִּטָּה חֲשִׁיבֵי:
18.en: for even though that they are fixed in the legs of the bed, since that ultimately they are taken off, they are ritually pure, these tongues are also sometimes removed from the frames of the bed, and are not considered like the bed.

18.he: שֶׁשָּׁכַב עָלֶיהָ זָב, אוֹ נִתְלָה אוֹ נִשְׁעַן:
18.en: that a person with gonorrhea who lay on it or was suspending from it or leaning on it.

18.he: אוֹתָן עֵצִים שֶׁבְּרֹחַב הַמִּטָּה לְצַד מְרַאֲשֹׁתֶיהָ אוֹ מַרְגְּלוֹתֶיהָ:
18.en: those pieces of wood that are at the width of the bed to the side from its head or from its feet.

18.he: אוֹתָן עֵצִים שֶׁבְּאֹרֶךְ הַמִּטָּה מִיָּמִין אוֹ מִשְּׂמֹאל, וְהֵם נִקְרָאִים אֲרֻכּוֹת הַמִּטָּה:
18.en: those pieces of wood that are at the length of the bed from the right or from the left, and they are called ארוכות המטה/long board, long side of the bedstead.

18.he: דְּתוּ לֹא חַזְיָא וְהַוְיָא כְשִׁבְרֵי כֵלִים שֶׁהֵן טְהוֹרִים:
18.en: for they further are not proper and they are like shards of vessels that are ritually pure.

18.he: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה:
18.en: But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Nehemiah.

18.he: חָתַךְ וְקָטַע. כְּמוֹ גֹדוּ אִילָנָא:
18.en: he severed and broke off (i.e., cut) like cut down a tree.

18.he: שְׁנֵי עֵצִים הָעֲשׂוּיִין כְּלָשׁוֹן, שֶׁמַּלְבְּנֵי הַמִּטָּה מֻנָּחִים עֲלֵיהֶן. חֲתָכָן בָּאֲלַכְסוֹן, אֶחָד שֶׁבְּמִקְצוֹעַ מִזְרָחִית דְּרוֹמִית וְאֶחָד שֶׁבְּמִקְצוֹעַ מַעֲרָבִית צְפוֹנִית, טְהוֹרָה, דְּתוּ לֹא חַזְיָא. וְכֵן אִם גָּדַד שְׁתֵּי כְרָעַיִם טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח לוֹכְסָן, מִכֶּרַע שֶׁבְּמִקְצוֹעַ מִזְרָחִית דְּרוֹמִית גָּדַד טֶפַח, וּמִכֶּרַע שֶׁבְּמִקְצוֹעַ מַעֲרָבִית צְפוֹנִית גָּדַד טֶפַח, כִּשְׁבוּרָה דָמְיָא:
18.en: two pieces of wood that are made like a tongue, that the frames of the bed are placed upon them, he cuts them with crosswise/diagonally, one that is in the southeastern corner and one that is in the northwest corner, are ritually pure, for they are not appropriate. And similarly if he cut two legs a handbreadth by a handbreadth diagonally, from the leg that is in the southeast corner he cut a handbreadth, and from the leg in the northwest corner he cut a handbreadth, it is like it is broken.

18.he: שֶׁגָּדַד רַגְלֶיהָ וְאֵין טֶפַח מִן הַמִּטָּה לָאָרֶץ, לָא חֲשִׁיבָא:
18.en: that he cut its legs and there is no handbreadth from the bed to the ground, it is not considered [of value, and hence is pure].

18.he: עֲדַיִן עוֹמֶדֶת בְּטֻמְאָתָהּ, כֵּיוָן דְּקַיְמָא שְׁנִיָּה:
18.en: it still stands in its defilement/impurity, since the second side exists.

18.he: אַף עַל גַּב דְּנִתַּקְּנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה קֹדֶם שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה שְׁנִיָּה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם טְהוֹרָה, דְּפָנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת בָּאוּ לְכָאן, שֶׁלְּאַחַר שֶׁיָּרְדָה לָהּ טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס נִתְחַדְּשׁוּ לָהּ פָּנִים הַלָּלוּ וְאֵין זוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, מֵאַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַלְקֵל בָּהּ כְּדֵי בִטּוּלָהּ:
18.en: even though the first was repaired prior to the second side being broken. Nevertheless, it is ritually pure/clean, for new faces had appeared here, for after it went down through the defilement of treading/Midras, these faces renewed themselves and this is not the first, for after it had been ruined enough in order that it be voided.
