18.he: מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲרֻכָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה כְשֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה וְתִקְּנָהּ שֶׁהֵבִיא אֲרֻכָּה אַחֶרֶת תַּחַת הַשְּׁבוּרָה וְחִבְּרָהּ לַמִּטָּה, נִטְמֵאת מַגַּע מִדְרָס, שֶׁהֲרֵי נָגְעָה בַמִּטָּה הַטְּמֵאָה מִדְרָס, וְכִי נִשְׁבְּרָה שְׁנִיָּה דְפָרַח מִנַּהּ טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס, אִשְׁתַּיַּר בָּהּ טֻמְאַת מַגָּע, דְּכָל הַמִּטָּה מְחֻבֶּרֶת לָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁנִּתַּקְּנָה:
18.en: because the long side of the bedstead was first when it was broken and fixed and he brought a new long side in place of the broken one and attached it below, it became defiled through contact via treading/Midras, for it (the person with gonorrhea) had touched the bed who was impure through treading, and when the second [board] was broken, that it sprouting from it the defilement of treading, there remained in it the defilement of contact, for the entire bed is connected to the first board when it was fixed.

18.he: דְּכֵיוָן דְּנִשְׁבְּרוּ שְׁתֵּי הָאֲרֻכּוֹת, תּוּ לֹא חַזְיָא. וְלֹא דָמֵי לְהֵיכָא דְנִתְפָּרְקָה וְכֻלָּהּ קַיֶּמֶת, דְּהָתָם סוֹפוֹ לְהַחֲזִיר פְּרָקֶיהָ וּלְחַבְּרָהּ:
18.en: it – the bed is pure) – for since the two long bedsteads were broken, they are no longer fit for use. And it is not similar to where it was taken apart and all of it exists, for there, it will be eventually be put back together with its fellow parts.

18.he: שֶׁל מִטָּה שֶׁהָיְתָה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס. שֶׁדָּרַס הַזָּב עַל הַכֶּרַע כְּשֶׁהָיָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מְחֻבָּר לַמִּטָּה:
18.en: [leg] of a bed which was impure with defilement by treading. That the person with gonorrhea tread on the bed leg when he was on its own and it was not connected to the med.

18.he: דְּחִבּוּר עֲבִיד לָהּ כְּאִלּוּ כֻלָּהּ גוּף אֶחָד:
18.en: for attachment was done to it, as if it is all one body.

18.he: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּגְעָה בְמֵת:
18.en: such as, for example, that it came in contact with a corpse.

18.he: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּגְעָה בִטְמֵא מֵת:
18.en: that it came in contact with someone who was defiled through contact with a corpse.

18.he: דְּלֹא נִטְמֵאת בִּנְגִיעַת הַכֶּרַע. דְּרִאשׁוֹן הֲוָה, וְאֵין אָדָם וְכֵלִים מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה אֶלָּא מֵאַב הַטֻּמְאָה:
18.en: that it (8.e. the bed) was not defiled through contact of the leg [of the bed]. For it was first [degree of ritual impurity], and a person nor vessels are susceptible to defilement other than from a primary source of defilement.

18.he: כְּלִי עֵץ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שִׁנַּיִם וּמְהַפְּכִים בּוֹ אֶת הַתֶּבֶן, וְשִׁנָּיו שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת. וּלְפִי שֶׁהַשִּׁנַּיִם שֶׁל פְּרָקִים וּנְעוּצִים בּוֹ, דִּינוֹ כְדִין מִטָּה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל פְּרָקִים. וְהַאי וְכֵן, אַטֻּמְאַת שִׁבְעָה קָאֵי, דְּאֵין מַעְדֵּר מִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס:
18.en: passing the grain from one side to the other) – a wooden vessel/utensil that has teeth that turn over the straw, and its teeth are metal. And because the teeth are of joints inserted therein, its law is like that of a bed which is of links. And this and similar to it, it is referring to the defilement for seven days, for the share of the plough does not defile through treading.

18.he: בִּתְפִלִּין שֶׁל רֹאשׁ שֶׁנָּגְעוּ בְמֵת אַיְרֵי, שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה בָתִּים, וְכָל בַּיִת נִקְרֵאת קְצִיצָה:
18.en: it is speaking of the Tefillin of the head that came in contact with a corpse, for it has four compartments, and every compartment is called a קציצה/capsule, compartment.

18.he: הֶעֱבִיר בַּיִת אֶחָד וְהֵבִיא אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו:
18.en: he removed one compartment and brought another in its place.

18.he: דְּחִבּוּרָן מְשַׁוֵּי לְהוּ גוּף אֶחָד:
18.en: that their connection/attachment makes them one body.

18.he: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהָרְבִיעִית קַיֶּמֶת, מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמְּחֻבֶּרֶת לָרְבִיעִית. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהֶעֱבִיר גַּם הָרְבִיעִית וְהֶחְלִיפָהּ בְּאַחֶרֶת, פָּרְחָה מִנַּיְהוּ טֻמְאַת מֵת, וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר בַּשָּׁלֹשׁ קְצִיצוֹת טֻמְאַת מַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת, שֶׁהֲרֵי נָגְעוּ בָרְבִיעִית כְּשֶׁחִבְּרָן וְהִיא עֲדַיִן קַיֶּמֶת. אֲבָל רְבִיעִית כְּשֶׁהֻחְלְפָה, אֵין בְּגוּפָהּ טֻמְאָה כְלָל, דְּאִי מִשּׁוּם דְּנָגְעָה בַשָּׁלֹשׁ, אֵין מַגָּע עוֹשֶׂה מַגָּע, שֶׁהַשָּׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת נִינְהוּ שֶׁנָּגְעוּ בִטְמֵא מֵת, וְאֵין הָרְבִיעִית הַחֲדָשָׁה מְקַבֶּלֶת מֵהֶן טֻמְאָה, וְאֵין טֻמְאָה בָרְבִיעִית הַחֲדָשָׁה אֶלָּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמְּחֻבֶּרֶת לַשָּׁלֹשׁ הַטְּמֵאוֹת מַגָּע. הִלְכָּךְ כְּשֶׁחָזַר וְהֶחְלִיף הַשָּׁלֹשׁ פַּעַם שְׁנִיָּה, טָהֲרוּ כֻלָּן וַאֲפִלּוּ מַגָּע לֵית בְּהוּ:
18.en: all the time that the fourth [compartment] exists. On account that it is attached to the fourth [compartment]. But when he removed also the fourth and exchanged it for another, the defilement from [contact with] the dead flies out from it, and there remains in the three compartments/capsules [of the Tefillin of the head] the defilement from contact with something which had been defiled through contact with a corpse, for it came in contact with the fourth [capsule/compartment] when they attached them and it still exists. But the Fourth [capsule/compartment], when it was switched out, there is no defilement in its body at all, for if it was because it come in contact with the three [other] compartments, contact [uncleanness] does not cause contact uncleanness, since the first three [compartments] are new, that came in contact with someone who had been in contact with a corpse, the new forth [compartment] does not receive defilement from them, and there is no defilement in the new fourth [compartment] other than on account that is attached to the three which are defiled through contact. Therefore, when he return and switched out the three [compartments] a second time, all of them are pure, and there is no contact [with defilement] in them.

18.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ אִיכָּא אֲרֻכָּה וּשְׁתֵּי כְרָעַיִם, הוֹאִיל וְאֵין בְּדַעְתָּם לְהַחֲזִיר. וְכִי מַהֲנֵי, דַּוְקָא בְמָקוֹם שֶׁהַכֹּל לְאָדָם אֶחָד:
18.en: and even where there is a longboard/bedside and two legs, but it is not their intention to restore, and where they benefit, is specifically in a place that everything belongs to one person.

18.he: אֲבָל לְמַפְרֵעַ לֹא, דְּכֵיוָן דְּחִלְּקוּהָ פָּרְחָה טֻמְאָה מִנַּהּ:
18.en: but not retroactively, for when they (i.e., the brothers or joint owners) divided it half, the defilement flew off from it.

18.he: אִם פֵּרְשָׁה הַכֶּרַע מִן הָאֲרֻכָּה וְעוֹמֶדֶת עִם הַקְּצָרָה, הָוֵי חִבּוּר, וְאִם נִטְמֵאת הַכֶּרַע נִטְמֵאת הַקְּצָרָה. כְּשֵׁם שֶׁכְּשֶׁכֻּלָּהּ שְׁלֵמָה אִם נִטְמָא אֶחָד מֵאֲבָרֶיהָ נִטְמֵאת כֻּלָּהּ, כָּךְ נַמִּי כְּשֶׁפֵּרַשׁ הַכֶּרַע מִן הָאֲרֻכָּה וְעוֹמֶדֶת עִם הַקְּצָרָה, נַעֲשֵׂית חֲבִילָה עִם הַקְּצָרָה, וּכְשֶׁנִּטְמֵאת הַכֶּרַע נִטְמֵאת הַקְּצָרָה עִמָּהּ:
18.en: if the leg [of the bed] was removed from the longboard/beside and stands with the short board/the board at the head and at the foot of the bed, it is combined/connected, but if the leg is defiled, the longboard is defiled. For just as when it is complete/whole, if one of its pieces is defiled, all of it is defiled, so also when they remove the leg from the longboard and it stands with the shortboard, and when the leg is defiled, the shortboard is defiled as well.

18.he: שֶׁאִם הִטְבִּיל הַכֶּרַע עִם הַקְּצָרָה אֵין הַקְּצָרָה חוֹצֶצֶת עָלֶיהָ, כִּי הֵיכִי דְלָא חַיְצָה עָלֶיהָ כְּשֶׁמַּטְבִּילָהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא שְׁלֵמָה:
18.en: and if he immersed the leg [of the bed] in a Mikveh/ritual bath with the shortboard of the bed, the shortboard does not interpose upon it, for just as it does not interpose upon it when we immerse it (i.e., the bed) when it is whole/complete.

18.he: וְלֹא חֲבִילָה. דְּאִם נִטְמֵאת כֶּרַע, הִיא טְמֵאָה וְלֹא קְצָרָה, דְּאֵינָהּ חִבּוּר כִּשְׁלֵמָה:
18.en: and not when combined, that if the leg [of the bed] had become defiled, it [alone] is defiled and not the shortboard [of the bed], for it is not combined like something whole/complete.

18.he: כְּשֶׁבָּא לְהַטְבִּילָהּ מַטְבִּיל הַכֶּרַע בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ, וְלֹא חֲבִילָה עִם הַקְּצָרָה, שֶׁהַקְּצָרָה חוֹצֶצֶת עָלֶיהָ, דְּאֵינָהּ חִבּוּר כִּשְׁלֵמָה, דְּמַטְבִּיל מִטָּה שְׁלֵמָה טְהוֹרָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא פֵרְקָהּ, אֲבָל הַשְׁתָּא דְפֵרְשָׁה הַכֶּרַע מִן הָאֲרֻכָּה לֹא הָוֵי חֲבִילָה עִם הַקְּצָרָה, וְצָרִיךְ לְהַטְבִּילָהּ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים. כָּךְ נִרְאֵית פֵּרוּשׁ מִשְׁנָה זוֹ מִן הַתּוֹסֶפְתָּא, וְכָךְ פֵּרְשׁוּהָ רַבּוֹתַי:
18.en: when he comes to immerse it [in a Mikveh/ritual bath], the leg is by itself, and not the combination with the short board [of the bed] for the short board interposes upon it. That which is not connected is like a whole [bed], for when one immerses a whole bed [in the Mikveh] it is ritually pure even though he did not break it apart, but now that it separated the leg from the long board, it is not combined with the shortboard, and it is necessary to immerse it [in a Mikveh] on its own. The Halakha is according to the Sages. So it appeared that the explanation of this Mishnah is from the Tosefta (Tractate Kelim Bava Metzia, Chapter 8, Halakha 8), such is how my teachers/Rabbis explained it.

19.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּטַּהֶרֶת כְּשֶׁהִיא שְׁלֵמָה, פְּעָמִים שֶׁהִיא גְדוֹלָה וְאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לִכָּנֵס בַּמִּקְוֶה וְצָרִיךְ לְפָרְקָהּ:
19.en: even though it had become defiled while it was whole/complete, sometimes, on occasion when it is large and is unable to enter the Mikveh [whole], and one needs to take it apart.

19.he: גָּרְסִינַן, כְּלוֹמַר, בֵּין מְפָרֵק בֵּין נוֹגֵעַ בַּחֲבָלִים טָהוֹר. וּבְמִטָּה שֶׁנִּטְמֵאת בְּמֵת אוֹ בְמִשְׁכַּב הַזָּב אַיְרֵי, וּכְגוֹן שֶׁאֵין בַּמִּטָּה אֲרֻכָּה וּשְׁתֵּי כְרָעַיִם, וַאֲפִלּוּ הָכִי צָרִיךְ לְהַטְבִּילָהּ, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תַּחֲזֹר לְטֻמְאָתָהּ כְּשֶׁיְּחַבְּרֶנָהּ. וְהַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּחֲבָלִים טָהוֹר, דְּמִכֵּיוָן שֶׁפֵּרְקָהּ שׁוּב אֵין הַחֲבָלִים חִבּוּר:
19.en: this is our reading. Meaning to say, whether one takes it (i.e., the bed) apart or one touches the ropes, one is ritually pure. But we are speaking about a bed that was defiled through contact with a corpse or though a person with gonorrhea lying on it, and as for example, that is no on the bed a long board and two legs, even though, it is necessary to immerse it [in a Mikveh], in order that it not return to its defilement when it is connected. But the person who touches the ropes is ritually pure, for since he took it (i.e., the bed) apart, the ropes are no longer connected.

19.he: בִּתְחִלָּה כְּשֶׁאָדָם מְסָרֵג אֶת הַמִּטָּה שְׁלֵמָה וְסוֹרֵג בָּהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה בָתִּים וַעֲדַיִן נִשְׁאָר הַחֶבֶל אָרֹךְ הַרְבֵּה, נִטְמֵאת הַמִּטָּה נִטְמָא הַחֶבֶל, וְהַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּחֶבֶל, טָמֵא, דְּכֻלּוֹ חִבּוּר הוֹאִיל וְסוֹפוֹ לְסָרְגוֹ:
19.en: at the outset when a person makes a partition by means of net-work/makes a zig-zag completely and girds it with three [rows of] meshes with it, and the rope still remains very long. If the bed became defiled, the rope is defiled. And a person who touches the rope, is impure. For it is all connected/attached, for ultimately, one is making a partition by means of net-work.

19.he: אִם קָשַׁר חֶבֶל אַחֵר לְזֶה הַחֶבֶל שֶׁסּוֹרֵג בּוֹ, אֵין הַחֶבֶל הָאַחֵר חִבּוּר מִן הַקֶּשֶׁר וְלַחוּץ:
19.en: if he tied another rope to this rope that he is making a lattice-work with, the other rope is not attached from the knot and outward.

19.he: כְּשֶׁקּוֹשְׁרִים שְׁנֵי חֲבָלִים זֶה בָזֶה מַנִּיחִין מְעַט מֵרָאשֵׁי הַחֲבָלִים מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה יוֹצְאִים חוּץ לַקֶּשֶׁר, וְהֵן נִקְרָאִים נִימֵי הַקֶּשֶׁר:
19.en: when they tie in a knot two ropes with one another, they leave a bit from the heads of the ropes from this side and from that side they exit beyond the knot, and they are called the “fringes of a knot.”

19.he: דְּכֵיוָן דְּצֹרֶךְ לַקֶּשֶׁר הֵם, שֶׁאִם הָיָה קוֹשֵׁר בְּרֹאשׁ הַחֶבֶל מַמָּשׁ הָיָה הַקֶּשֶׁר נִתָּר, נִמְצָא שֶׁאֵלּוּ הַנִּימִין מַעֲמִידִים הַקֶּשֶׁר וְכַקֶּשֶׁר דָּמוּ:
19.en: for since there is a need to tie them in a knot, that if the knot at the actual top of the of the rope was an extra knot, it is found that these fringes establish the knot an they are like the knot itself.

19.he: הָווּ חִבּוּר, דְּהוּא צֹרֶךְ הַקֶּשֶׁר. טְפֵי לֹא:
19.en: is an attachment/connection, and he requires the knot, but not more.

19.he: מַה שֶּׁנִּשְׁאַר מִמֶּנּוּ לְאַחַר שֶׁגָּמַר הַסֵּרוּג:
19.en: what remains from it [hangs over the bed] after he completed the plaiting.

19.he: דְּלֹא חֲזִי לְמִידִי לְצֹרֶךְ הַמִּטָּה, וְלָא חֲשִׁיב לָהּ יָד:
19.en: for it is not appropriate for the needs of the bed, and it is not considered a handle.

19.he: דַּחֲזִי לִקְשֹׁר בָּהּ הַפְּסָחִים. שֶׁהָיוּ רְגִילִים לִקְשֹׁר שָׁם הַפֶּסַח בַּחֶבֶל שֶׁבְּכַרְעֵי הַמִּטָּה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְזֻמָּן לָהֶם. וַחֲזִי נַמִּי לְשַׁלְשֵׁל בּוֹ אֶת הַמִּטָּה, כְּלוֹמַר לְהוֹרִידָהּ מִן הָעֲלִיָּה לַגַּג, אִי נַמִּי לְהוֹרִידָהּ אֶל הַמִּקְוֶה לְהַטְבִּילָהּ כְּשֶׁנִּטְמֵאת:
19.en: for it is appropriate to knot with it the Passover sacrifices. For they would regularly tie up the Passover sacrifices with a rope that is on the leg of the bed in order that it be ready for them. And it was appropriate also to let it down [over the side of the bed] , that is to say, to lower it from the attic to the roof. Alternatively, to lower it to the ritual bath to immerse it when it became defiled.

19.he: דְּמַה שֶּׁיֶּשׁ בַּחֶבֶל יוֹתֵר מֵעֲשָׂרָה אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְצֹרֶךְ הַמִּטָּה כְּלוּם:
19.en: for what there is on a rope more than ten [handbreadths] he does not use at all for the purposes of the bed.

19.he: כְּמִין אֵזוֹר אוֹ אַבְנֵט שֶׁל אָרִיג שֶׁכּוֹרְכִים אוֹתוֹ סְבִיב הַמִּטָּה כְּדֵי לְחַבֵּר פְּרָקֶיהָ. וּפְעָמִים שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל הַרְבֵּה וְנִגְרָר וְיוֹצֵא חוּץ מִן הַמִּטָּה:
19.en: a strap of cloth which is wound over the bed to keep the covering in position) – a kind of girdle or woven belt that they tie around the bed in order to attach its joints/links. But sometimes it is too large and it drags and extends beyond the bed.

19.he: וְהַמִּטָּה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס:
19.en: and the bed is impure from treading.

19.he: אֲפִלּוּ יוֹצֵא כַּמָּה אַמּוֹת חוּץ לַמִּטָּה, הַכֹּל טָמֵא:
19.en: even if it extends outward a few cubits beyond the bed, everything is impure.

19.dibur: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר עַד עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
19.he: טָמֵא בְטֻמְאַת הַמִּטָּה. מֵעֲשָׂרָה וּלְמַעְלָה טָהוֹר. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
19.en: it is impure through the defilement of the bed. From ten [handbreadths] and beyond it is pure. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yossi.

19.he: מִזְרָן שֶׁבָּלָה וְנִקְרַע, כַּמָּה יִשְׁתַּיֵּר מִמֶּנּוּ וְיִהְיֶה טָמֵא:
19.en: a girth that was worn out or torn, whatever that will remain from it, and it will be ritually impure.

19.he: דִּבְצִיר מֵהָכִי לֹא חֲזִי לְמִידִי וְלָא חֲשִׁיב כְּלִי:
19.en: for less than this, it is not appropriate for anything and it is not considered a vessel.

19.he: יֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, בֶּגֶד עָב וְקָשֶׁה שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים עַל הַחֲמוֹר כְּשֶׁבָּא מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ וְהוּא מַזִּיעַ, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִצְטַנֵּן לְאַחַר שֶׁמְּסִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ הָאֻכָּף. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים אוֹתוֹ עַל מַשְּׂאוֹי הַחֲמוֹר כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֻפְסַד אִם יֵרְדוּ עָלָיו גְּשָׁמִים:
19.en: there are those who explain/interpret , a thick and hard piece of cloth that they place on the donkey when it comes from the road and it is sweating, , in order that it not catch cold when they remove the saddle from it. And there are those who explain, that they place it on the burden of the donkey in order that it not be lost if rains fell upon it.

19.dibur: נִשָּׂא הַזָּב עַל הַמִּטָּה וְעַל הַמִּזְרָן.
19.he: לָאו דַּוְקָא נִשָּׂא עַל הַמִּזְרָן, אֶלָּא נִשָּׂא הַזָּב עַל הַמִּטָּה שֶׁהַמִּזְרָן כָּרוּךְ סְבִיבוֹתֶיהָ וְיוֹצֵא מִמֶּנָּה:
19.en: not exactly carried on the bed girth, but rather that the person with gonorrhea was carried on the bed that the girth is tied around it and extends from it.

19.dibur: מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
19.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְטַעֲמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר לְעֵיל דַּאֲפִלּוּ הַמִּזְרָן יוֹצֵא מִן הַמִּטָּה כָּל שֶׁהוּא וַאֲפִלּוּ טוּבָא הָוֵי חִבּוּר לַמִּטָּה וּמְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, כַּמִּטָּה עַצְמָהּ. שֶׁכָּל שֶׁהַזָּב נִשָּׂא עָלָיו וְנַעֲשָׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב שֶׁל זָב, הָוֵי אַב הַטֻּמְאָה, וְהַנּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ הָוֵי רִאשׁוֹן, וְרִאשׁוֹן עוֹשֶׂה שֵׁנִי, וְשֵׁנִי עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִישִׁי לִפְסֹל אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה בִּלְבַד אֲבָל לֹא לְטַמֵּא. וְהַיְנוּ מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם דְּהַיְנוּ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי, וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד וְהוּא שְׁלִישִׁי שֶׁהוּא פָסוּל בַּתְּרוּמָה בִּלְבַד, וְהַמִּזְרָן כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא פֵּרַשׁ מִן הַמִּטָּה חֲשִׁיב כְּאַב הַטֻּמְאָה וּמְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, אֲבָל לְאַחַר שֶׁפֵּרַשׁ לֹא הָוֵי אֶלָּא כִוְלַד הַטֻּמְאָה וּמְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, כְּדִין נוֹגֵעַ בְּמִשְׁכַּב הַזָּב:
19.en: Rabbi Meir according to his reason that he stated above (see previous Mishnah, Tractate Kelim, Chapter 19, Mishnah 3), that even if the bed birth extends from the bed a little bit, and even more, it is attached/connected to the bed, and the two are made impure and renders [the heave-offering] unit, like the bed itself. For all that the person with gonorrhea is carried upon and acts of lying and sitting are performed by the person with gonorrhea, which is a primary category of ritual impurity, and the person who touches is first degree [level of ritual impurity], and something that is first-degree [level of ritual impurity] makes something else second [degree level of ritual impurity] , and something that is second degree [level of ritual impurity] makes something third [degree level of ritual impurity] to invalidate the heave-offering/priest’s due alone, but not to make it impure. And this is where he defiles two degrees, which are first [degree of ritual impurity] and second [degree of ritual impurity] and he invalidates one and it is third [degree level of impurity] and it is invalid for heave offering alone. And the bed girth all the while that it was not removed from the bed is considered like a primary source of ritual impurity, and it defiles two and invalidates one, but after he removes it, it is nothing other than a derivative of the defilement which defiles one and invalidates one, according to the law of a person who touches that which the person with gonorrhea lies upon.

19.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְטַעֲמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר לְעֵיל [עַד] עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים וְתוּ לֹא. הִלְכָּךְ זֶה שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה חֲשׁוּב חִבּוּר לַמִּשְׁכָּב וּמְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא פֵּרַשׁ, אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁחוּץ לַעֲשָׂרָה לֹא חֲשׁוּב חִבּוּר לַמִּשְׁכָּב, וְדִינוֹ כְּפֵרַשׁ, דִּמְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד:
19.en: ר' יוסי אומר = Rabbi Yossi according to his reasoning, who stated above (in Tractate Kelim, Chapter 19, Mishnah 3) ten handbreadths and not further. Therefore, that which is within ten [handbreadths] is considered a connection/attachment to lying [by a person with gonorrhea], and it defiles two and invalidates one all the while that he did not remove it. But what is beyond ten [handbreadths] is not considered an attachment to the lying [by a person with gonorrhea], and its law is as it was explained, that it defiles one and invalidates one.

19.dibur: נִשָּׂא עַל הַמִּזְרָן מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלִפְנִים טְמֵאָה.
19.he: גָּרְסִינַן, וְלֹא גָרְסִינַן טָמֵא. וְהָכִי פֵרוּשָׁא, נִשָּׂא הַזָּב עַל הַמִּזְרָן הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַמִּטָּה, אִם נִשָּׂא מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלִפְנִים לְצַד הַמִּטָּה, הַמִּטָּה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, דְּכֵיוָן דְּכָל עֲשָׂרָה חֲשִׁיבֵי חִבּוּר לַמִּטָּה, כְּשֶׁנִּטְמָא מִזְרָן נִטְמֵאת הַמִּטָּה. אֲבָל מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלַחוּץ דְּלֹא הָווּ חִבּוּר לַמִּטָּה, טְהוֹרָה הַמִּטָּה וְלֹא נִטְמֵאת [בְּטֻמְאַת] הַמִּזְרָן. כָּךְ נִרְאֵית בְּעֵינַי פֵּרוּשׁ מִשְׁנָה זוֹ. וְגִרְסַת רַבּוֹתַי דְּגָרְסֵי טָמֵא וְטָהוֹר וּפֵרוּשָׁן, לֹא נִתְקַבֵּל לִי. וְכֵן דִּבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ"ם שֶׁכָּתַב בְּפֵרוּשׁ מִשְׁנָה זוֹ לֹא נִכְנְסוּ בְּאָזְנַי כְּלָל. וְדִקְדַּקְתִּי אַחַר כָּךְ בְּחִבּוּרוֹ בְּהִלְכוֹת כֵּלִים פֶּרֶק כ"א [הֲלָכָה ט], נִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁשָּׁם חָזַר בּוֹ וּפֵרֵשׁ מִשְׁנָה זוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרַשְׁתִּיהָ כָּאן:
19.en: this is our reading (i.e., טמאה). But we don’t have the reading of טמא/impure. And this is an explanation: if the person with gonorrhea was carried on the bed girth that extends from the bed, if he was carried from ten [handbreadths] and within to the side of the bed, the bed is impure through treading/Midras, for since all ten [handbreadths] are considered an attachment to the bed, but from ten [handbreadths] and beyond it is not an attachment/connection to the bed, and the bed is pure and its not defiled [with the defilement] of the bed girth. Such it appears in my eyes an explanation/commentary on this Mishnah. And the reading of my Teachers/Rabbis who have the [textual] reading "טמא וטהור" /impure and pure and their explanation, but it was not acceptable to me. And similarly the words of Maimonides who wrote in his commentary to this Mishnah did not enter my eyes are all. And I investigated afterwards in his work (i.e., the Mishneh Torah) in the Laws of Kelim/Vessels, Chapter 21 [Halakha 9] – it appears to me that there he retracted and explained this Mishnah as I explained it here.

19.he: וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא פֵּרַשׁ הַמִּזְרָן מִן הַמִּטָּה הָוֵי כַמִּטָּה עַצְמָהּ כִּדְפָרֵשִׁית:
19.en: ;and all the time that he did not remove the bed girth from the bed, it is like the bed itself, as I have explained.

19.he: וּמְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, כְּדִין כָּל נוֹגֵעַ בְּאַב הַטֻּמְאָה:
19.en: and it defiles one and invalids one, like the law of all who touch/come in contact with a primary category of ritual impurity.

19.he: כְּשֶׁהֵן כְּרוּכִים יַחַד:
19.en: when they are wrapped together.

19.he: בְּהָא לֹא פָלֵיג רַבִּי יוֹסֵי. דְּדַוְקָא בְטֻמְאַת מִדְרָס קָאָמַר עַד עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים טָמֵא מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלַחוּץ טָהוֹר, אֲבָל לִשְׁאָר טֻמְאוֹת, אֲפִלּוּ מֵאָה אַמָּה כֻּלּוֹ חִבּוּר. כְּגוֹן מִזְרָן שֶׁהוּא כָּרוּךְ עַל הַמִּטָּה וְנִכְנְסָה הַמִּטָּה לְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת אוֹ נָגְעָה בְשֶׁרֶץ, וְכֵן אִם נִכְנַס קָצֶה מִן הַמִּזְרָן לְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת אוֹ נָגַע בְּשֶׁרֶץ, נִטְמֵאת הַמִּטָּה נִטְמָא הַמִּזְרָן, נִטְמָא הַמִּזְרָן נִטְמֵאת הַמִּטָּה, וַאֲפִלּוּ הָיָה הַמִּזְרָן יוֹצֵא מִן הַמִּטָּה מֵאָה אַמָּה:
19.en: in this, Rabbi Yossi does not dispute. For especially in the defilement of treading/Midras it is stated, up until ten handbreadths it is impure; from ten [handbreadths] and beyond it is ritually pure. But concerning the rest of the defilements, even one hundred cubits all together is an attachment, such as the bed girth which is wrapped on a bed and the bed enters into the tent of a corpse or that it touched a reptile, and similarly if a piece from the bed girth enters into the tent of a corpse or touched a reptile, if the bed is defiled, the bed girth is defiled; if the bed girth is defiled, the bed is defiled, and even if the bed birth extends from the bed for one-hundred cubits.

19.he: וְלֹא הָווּ כְּכֵלִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּבְּרוּ, כֵּיוָן דְּכָל אֶחָד מֵהֶן כְּלִי בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ. אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְעִנְיַן קַבָּלַת טֻמְאָה חֲשׁוּבִים כִּכְלִי אֶחָד וּכְשֶׁנָּגְעָה טֻמְאָה בְאֶחָד מֵהֶן נִטְמָא הָאַחֵר:
19.en: and they are not like vessels that were broken, since each one of them is a vessel in its own right. Even though that regarding the matter of acquiring defilement they are considered like one vessel, and when defilement touched one of them, the other was defiled [as well].

19.he: וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ, וְהֵן רְאוּיוֹת לְהַחְזִירָן לִמְקוֹמָן, הִלְכָּךְ לֹא טָהֲרָה הַמִּטָּה מִטֻּמְאָתָהּ בִּנְטִילַת הָאֲרֻכּוֹת:
19.en: its [two long pieces], and they did not beak. And they are appropriate to be restored to their places, therefore, the bed was not purified from its defilement with the taking of the long pieces.

19.he: שֶׁהֲרֵי הַיְשָׁנוֹת קַיָּמוֹת וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּנּוּ הַנְּקָבִים, וְהָוֵי כְנִתְפָּרְקָה אֵבָר אֵבָר וְכָל אֵבָרֶיהָ שְׁלֵמִים. אֲבָל נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ הַיְשָׁנוֹת, טְהוֹרָה, לְפִי שֶׁהַיְשָׁנוֹת הֵן שֶׁהָיוּ בַּמִּטָּה כְשֶׁנִּטְמֵאת, וּכְשֶׁנִּשְׁתַּבְּרוּ הָוֵי הַמִּטָּה שֶׁבֶר כְּלִי, דְּלֹא חַזְיָא בְלֹא אֲרֻכּוֹת:
19.en: for since the old ones and the sockets/perforations were not changed, and when he removed each part of the bedstead and all of its bedsteads are whole. But when the old ones were broken, they are pure, because the old ones were on the bed when it became defiled, and when they were broken, the bed is a broken vessel, for it is not appropriate without the long pieces.

19.he: הַכִּסּוּי שֶׁלָּהּ:
19.en: its covering.

19.he: דְּכֵיוָן דְּשׁוּלֶיהָ קַיָּמִים אַכַּתִּי חַזְיָא לְתַשְׁמִישׁ. וְדַוְקָא טֻמְאַת מֵת. אֲבָל לֹא טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס, דְּלֹא חַזְיָא לִישִׁיבָה:
19.en: because its rim/bottom still exists, it is worthy for use. And specifically, defilement through contact with the dead, but not defilement by treading, for it is not appropriate for sitting.

19.he: בְּשׁוּלֶיהָ. בָּטַל בֵּית קִבּוּל שֶׁלָּהּ וּטְהוֹרָה לְגַמְרֵי:
19.en: at its rims/bottoms, its receptacle was annulled and it is completely pure.

19.he: אוֹצָרוֹת שֶׁבָּהּ, דְּהַיְנוּ חֲדָרִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְחֲתוּ עִמָּהּ, טְמֵאוֹת:
19.en: the treasures/storehouse within, that is the rooms that are in it that were not damaged with it, are impure.

19.he: כִּיס גָּדוֹל שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁהָרוֹעֶה נוֹתֵן חֲפָצָיו לְתוֹכוֹ, וּבְתוֹךְ הַתּוּרְמֵל יֵשׁ כִּיסִין קְטַנִּים כְּמוֹ הַמְּגוּרוֹת בַּתֵּבָה:
19.en: the inside pocket of which has become defective) -a large leather pocket that the shepherd puts his belongings into, and within the bag, there are small pockets like the drawers in a box.

19.he: נֹאד שֶׁל עוֹר:
19.en: of a skin of a he-goat/wether) – leather skin or bottle.

19.he: כְּשֶׁמַּפְשִׁיטִין עוֹרוֹת הָאֵילִים וְהַתְּיָשִׁים הַזְּכָרִים נִשְׁאָר הָעוֹר שֶׁבִּמְקוֹם הַבֵּיצִים כְּמִין כִּיס קָטָן, וְאִם נִפְחֲתוּ טְהוֹרוֹת, דְּבָטַל בֵּית קִבּוּל שֶׁלָּהֶן:
19.en: שהביצים שלה מקבלות עמה when they flay/shed the skin of the male rams and wethers/he-goats, there remains the leather that is in place of the genitals/testicles, like a small pocket, but if they were damaged, they are ritually pure, for their receptacle has been nullified.

19.he: כְּשֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִלְּמַעְלָה אֵינָהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, דְּאִם יָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ וּבָאִים לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ עֲמֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִן הַצַּד, יָכוֹל לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב עָלֶיהָ:
19.en: When it was damaged from above, it was not impure by treading, for if he sat upon it and comes to use it, they say to him: “Stand and let us do our work.” But when it was damaged from the side, it is possible to use it even though he sits upon it.

19.he: כְּשֶׁגְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה לֹא חַזְיָא לִישִׁיבָה כֻלֵּי הַאי:
19.en: when it is ten [handbreadths] high, it is not appropriate for sitting all that much.

19.he: דִּכְשֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ לִזְבֵּז מַזִּיק לַיּוֹשֵׁב:
19.en: buy which a flat vessel is made into a vessel-like receptacle) – when it has a vertical rim which damages the person who sits upon it.

19.he: בְּשׁוּלֶיהָ. לֹא חַזְיָא לְתַשְׁמִישׁ, אֲבָל חַזְיָא לִישִׁיבָה:
19.en: at its rim/bottom. It is not appropriate for use, but is appropriate for sitting.

19.he: עִקַּר הַתֵּבָה הִיא עֲשׂוּיָה לְהַחְזִיק בְּשׁוּלֶיהָ מַה שֶּׁמְּשִׂימִים בְּתוֹכָהּ, וְעַל יָדָם הִיא נִקְרֵאת כְּלִי. וְכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּפְחֲתוּ שׁוּלֶיהָ וּבָטְלוּ, בָּטְלוּ גַם דָּפְנוֹתֶיהָ מִלְּמַעֲלָן וְשׁוּב אֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת שׁוּם טֻמְאָה. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:
19.en: the primary purpose of the box is that its made to support its rim what one places within it, and through that, it is called a vessel. But because its rim was damaged and it was nullified, also its walls from above are nullified and it no longer receives any form of defilement. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.

19.he: קֻפָּה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין בָּהּ הַזֶּבֶל וְהָאַשְׁפָּה:
19.en: a large basket that they carry the manure and the trash.

19.he: שֶׁזֶּהוּ שִׁעוּרָהּ לִטַּהֵר כְּשֶׁנִּקְּבָה בְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן:
19.en: for this is its measure to become purified, when an incision is made when removing pomegranates.

19.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא טְהוֹרָה מִשְּׁאָר טֻמְאוֹת, טְמֵאָה הִיא מִדְרָס, שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִישִׁיבָה:
19.en: even though it is more pure than all of the other defilement things, it is impure from treading, which is appropriate for sitting.

19.he: וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:
19.en: And the Halakha is according to the Sages [for when the primary purpose is annulled, the secondary purpose is annulled].

20.he: עֲשׂוּיִין לְמַלְּאוֹתָן צֶמֶר אוֹ נוֹצָה, וְאָדָם נוֹתְנָן תַּחַת מְרַאֲשׁוֹתָיו:
20.en: made to be filled with wool or feathers/down, a a person places them underneath his head.

20.he: כְּמוֹ כָרִים הֵן, אֶלָּא שֶׁהֵן אֲרֻכִּים וּגְדוֹלִים וְכָל גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם שׁוֹכֵב עֲלֵיהֶן:
20.en: they ae like mattresses, but they are long and large, and the entire body of a person lies on them.

20.he: כְּמִין שַׂקִּים שֶׁל עוֹר גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בָּהֶן סְחוֹרוֹת שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין בַּסְּפִינוֹת:
20.en: adapted for ship-loads) – like a species of large leather sacks that they place in them goods that they take on ships.

20.he: דְּכָל הָנֵי עֲבִידֵי נַמִּי לִשְׁכִיבָה:
20.en: fo all of these are used also for lying.

20.he: כְּמִין סַל וּכְפִיפָה שֶׁתּוֹלִין בְּפִי הַבְּהֵמָה, וְנוֹתְנִים בָּהּ מִסְפּוֹא וּשְׂעֹרִים וְהַבְּהֵמָה אוֹכֶלֶת כְּשֶׁהִיא מְהַלֶּכֶת:
20.en: fodder basked used instead of a muzzle) – a kind of folded basket that they suspend in the mouth of an animal, and they put in it fodder and barley-corn and the animal eats when it is walking.

20.he: כִּיס גָּדוֹל שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁהָרוֹעֶה נוֹתֵן שָׁם כָּל חֲפָצָיו:
20.en: a large leather pocket that the shepherd places there all of his belongings.

20.he: שַׂק שֶׁל עוֹר קָטָן:
20.en: a small leather bag.

20.he: חֵמֶת קָטָן שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים בּוֹ בְשָׂמִים:
20.en: small leather bag that they place spices in.

20.he: כְּלִי שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בּוֹ צֵידָה לַדֶּרֶךְ. תַּרְגּוּם צֵידָה זְוָדִין:
20.en: a vessel that they place in it food/provisions for travel. The Aramaic translation of "צידה" – is "זוודין" – travel bag.

20.he: כָּל אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנוּיִים בַּמִּשְׁנָה, אִם יֵשׁ בְּכֻלָּן הַשִּׁעוּר הַמְפֹרָשׁ בָּהֶן אוֹ יוֹתֵר, מְטַמְּאִין מִדְרָס, דִּמְשַׁמְּשִׁין שְׁכִיבָה עִם מְלַאכְתָּן. אֲבָל בְּפָחוֹת מִכְּשִׁעוּר הַמְפֹרָשׁ בָּהֶן, לֹא:
20.en: all of these that are taught in the Mishnah, if each of them has the measurement that is explained with them or more, they defile through treading/Midras, and they are used for lying with their work/task. But not with less than the defined measure [of the Mishnah].

20.he: שֶׁכָּל אֵלּוּ עֲשׂוּיִין לְקַבֵּל, שֶׁהַקִּבּוּל הַהוּא מְכִינָם וּמַזְמִינָם לִהְיוֹת רְאוּיִין לְמִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב, וּכְשֶׁנִּפְחַת בָּטַל הָעִקָּר שֶׁהוּא הַקִּבּוּל שֶׁבַּעֲבוּרוֹ הָיָה קָרוּי כְּלִי:
20.en: for all of these are made to receive/hold things, that the receptacle prepares them and designates them to be fit for lying and sitting, and when it becomes damaged/worn out, the primary purpose which is reception is annulled , and for that purpose it was called a vessel.

20.he: שֶׁהִיא טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס:
20.en: which is defilement by treading.

20.he: חֵמֶת מָלֵא רוּחַ וּמְשִׂימִין הַחֲלִילִים בְּפִי הַחֵמֶת וְהָרוּחַ יוֹצֵא דֶרֶךְ הַנְּקָבִים וּמוֹצִיא מִן הַחֲלִילִים קוֹל שֶׁל שִׁיר:
20.en: a bag that is full of wind and they place the flutes in he mouth of the bag and the wind exits through the incisions/holes and produces from the flutes a sound of song.

20.he: דְּלֹא חַזְיָא לִשְׁכִיבָה:
20.en: for it is not fit for lying.

20.he: עֲרֵבָה שֶׁמְּבִיאִין בָּהּ אֲבָנִים קְטַנּוֹת וְרִגְבֵי אֲדָמָה כְּדֵי לָתֵת בַּנִּדְבָּכִים שֶׁל בִּנְיָן. וּפִיסוֹנוֹת לְשׁוֹן שְׁקַל פִּיסָא שְׁדָא בֵיהּ דְּאָמְרִינַן בַּגְּמָרָא בְסַנְהֶדְרִין גַּבֵּי מַרְקוּלִיס:
20.en: a trough that they bring into it small stones and clods of earth in order to provide a mold filled with earth or rubble of ethe building. And [the word] פיפוסנות is the language of “he took up a lump [of brittle stone] and threw it at it (the idolatrous statue)” as we state in the Gemara in [Tractate] Sanhedrin 64a concerning Mercurius (name of the Roman divinity, identified with the Grecian Hermes).

20.he: קָסָבְרֵי מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת שְׁכִיבָה עִם מְלַאכְתָּהּ. וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרֵי אֵינָהּ מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת:
20.en: for they hold that they use it for lying with their work. But the School of Hillel holds that they don’t use it.

20.he: וְאִם לֹא נִסְדְּקָה אֵינָהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, דְּאוֹמְרִין לוֹ עֲמֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה וּמוֹצִיאָה מַשְׁקִין, אֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה אֶלָּא לִשְׁכִיבָה. וּפְחוּתָה מִשְּׁנֵי לֻגִּים, אוֹ יְתֵרָה מִתִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין, אֵינָהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס וַאֲפִלּוּ נִסְדְּקָה:
20.en: but if it was not split, it not impure through treading, for we say to him: “Stand and let us do our work.” But when it was split and liquids come out, it is not worthy other than for lying. But less than two LOG or more than nine Kab, is not ritually impure through treading and even if it was split.

20.he: מֵחֲמַת גְּשָׁמִים מִתְנַפֵּחַ הָעֵץ וְנִסְתָּם הַסֶּדֶק:
20.en: on account of the rains the wood swells and the split is closed up.

20.he: כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה בַּתְּחִלָּה קֹדֶם שֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל. וְאֵינָהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, דְּאֵינָהּ מְיֻחֶדֶת לִשְׁכַּב עָלֶיהָ, הוֹאִיל וּמִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין בָּהּ בְּלִישָׁה:
20.en: as it was at the outset before it became split, because it has a receptacle. But it is not impure from treading, for it is not designated to lie upon it, for they use it in kneading.

20.he: לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְפַּח הָעֵץ וְנִסְתַּם הַסֶּדֶק, הִנִּיחָהּ בְּרוּחַ קָדִים וְנִסְדְּקָה:
20.en: after the wood had swelled up and the split had closed up, he placed it in an east wind and it split.

20.he: דְּחָזְרָה לִהְיוֹת רְאוּיָה לִשְׁכִיבָה וְלֹא לָלוּשׁ בָּהּ:
20.en: that it returned to being fit for lying but not to knead with it.

20.he: דִּתְחִלָּתָן אֵין טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס, וּכְשֶׁנִּסְדְּקוּ טְמֵאִים מִדְרָס:
20.en: that at their outset they are not impure through treading, but when they are split, they are impure through treading.

20.he: סַלִּים עֲשׂוּיִין מִנְּצָרִים שֶׁל עֲרָבָה וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן:
20.en: baskets made of wickerwork of willows and of similar things.

20.he: שֶׁתִּגָּמֵר שְׂפָתָן הָעֶלְיוֹנָה:
20.en: when their upper rim/lip is completed.

20.dibur: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ שִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶן כָּל שֶׁהֵן.
20.he: שֶׁנָּפְלוּ שִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶן וְלֹא נִשְׁאָר בְּשִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶן אֶלָּא כָּל שֶׁהֵן, טָמֵא:
20.en: that their lips fell and there doesn’t remain anything of their lips to any degree at all, they are ritually impure.

20.he: שֶׁל עֵץ בְּעָלְמָא שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ בֵית יָד לַקֻּרְדֹּם לְפִי שָׁעָה, שֶׁלֹּא קְבָעוֹ בְתוֹכוֹ:
20.en: merely [a wooden] staff that a handle/heft for a hatchet according to the time [of use], but did not fit it [permanently] within it.

20.he: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דִּבְאַפֵּי נַפְשֵׁיהּ פְּשׁוּטֵי כְלֵי עֵץ לֹא מְקַבְּלֵי טֻמְאָה, הָכָא בֵית יָד הוּא, וְיָדוֹת נִתְרַבּוּ לְכָל תּוֹרַת טֻמְאַת הַכְּלִי אוֹ הָאֹכֶל, וְאִם נִטְמָא הַקֻּרְדֹּם נִטְמָא הַבֵּית יָד, וְכֵן אִם נָגְעָה טֻמְאָה בַּבֵּית יָד נִטְמָא הוּא וְנִטְמָא הַקֻּרְדֹּם עִמּוֹ. וְדַוְקָא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה הָוֵי חִבּוּר לַטֻּמְאָה, שֶׁלֹּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה לֹא, דְּשֶׁלֹּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה אָדָם עָשׂוּי לְזָרְקוֹ לְבֵין הָעֵצִים:
20.en: even though that on its own, it is a plain wooden vessel, it does not receive ritual uncleanness; but here it is a sleeve, and handles increased through the Torah of the defilement of the vessel or the food, and if the ax/hatchet became defiled, the handle became defiled, and similarly, if the defilment came in contact with the handle, it is defiled, and the ax/hatchet became defiled with it. And specifically, at the time of work there is a connector/attachment to defilement, but not during the time when not working., for when it is not the time of work, a person generally would throw them among the wood.

20.he: כְּלִי הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ לִשְׁנֵי צְדָדִים. דְּיוּ, שְׁנַיִם. סְטָר, צַד. כְּדִמְתַרְגְּמִינַן לִסְטָר חַד. וְהוּא מַקֵּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁנֵי נְקָבִים אֶחָד מִלְּמַטָּה וְאֶחָד מִלְּמַעְלָה, וּשְׁתֵּי יְתֵדוֹת תְּחוּבוֹת בָּהֶן אַחַת מִמִּזְרָח לְמַעֲרָב וְאַחַת מִצָּפוֹן לְדָרוֹם, וְהַנָּשִׁים מְסֵכוֹת בּוֹ אֶת הַמַּטְוֶה שֶׁבַּפֶּלֶךְ, וְקוֹרִין לוֹ נספ"א בְּלַעַ"ז. וּפְעָמִים שֶׁעוֹשִׂין אוֹתָן יָדוֹת מִבַּרְזֶל וּמְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה:
20.en: a vessel that one uses for two sides. [The word דיוסטר – is now broken down into its component parts. "דיו" is “two;” "סטר" is “sides,” as we translate in Aramaic, “to one side.” And it is a staff that has two incisions, one from the bottom and the other from the top, and two handles are inserted in them, one from the east to the west and one from the north and the south, and the women roll the yarn that is in the spindle, and we call it NASPA in the foreign language. And sometimes they make these handles from iron and they receive ritual impurity.

20.he: קָבַע הַדְּיוּסְטָר דְּהַיְנוּ הַמַּקֵּל עִם שְׁתֵּי יְתֵדוֹתָיו בִּכְלוֹנָס, דְּהַיְנוּ עֵץ אָרֹךְ וְגָדוֹל הַתָּקוּעַ בָּאָרֶץ:
20.en: if he inserted the transverse staff of the pole reaching from end to end), that is the staff with its two handles/pegs in the beam, which is a long and large piece of wood that is fastened into the ground.

20.he: הַדְּיוּסְטָר מִכָּאן וָאֵילָךְ אִם נָגְעָה בוֹ טֻמְאָה, דַּהֲוֵי הַמַּקֵּל חִבּוּר לַיְתֵדוֹת בֵּין בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּקְבָּע, שֶׁאֵין אָדָם עָשׂוּי לְזָרְקוֹ לְבֵין הָעֵצִים. אֲבָל הַכְּלוֹנָס עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לוֹ, שֶׁאִם נָגְעָה טֻמְאָה בַכְּלוֹנָס לֹא נִטְמָא הַדְּיוּסְטָר:
20.en: the traverse staff of the upright loom reaching from end to end is impure from this side and that, if the defilement came in contact with it, for it is an attached staff to the handles/pegs whether at the time of work or not at the time of work, since it was affixed, a person is not likely to throw it among the wood, but the traverse staff of the loom in the beam, it is not attached to it, and the rest of it whether above or below is ritually pure, for the staff of the loom in the beam is long and large.

20.he: שֶׁקָּבַע שְׁתֵּי הַיְתֵדוֹת בְּגוּפוֹ שֶׁל כְּלוֹנָס:
מִן הַכְּלוֹנָס אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא לְצֹרֶךְ הַיְתֵדוֹת לְהָסֵךְ אֶת הַמַּטְוֶה, וְהַשְּׁאָר בֵּין מִלְּמַעְלָה בֵּין מִלְּמַטָּה טָהוֹר, שֶׁהַכְּלוֹנָס אָרֹךְ הוּא וְגָדוֹל:
שֶׁהוּא עָשׂוּי, וּקְבָעוֹ בִכְלוֹנָס, הַכִּסֵּא טָמֵא מִדְרָס, וְאֵין הַכְּלוֹנָס חִבּוּר לוֹ לִהְיוֹת מִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס כְּמוֹתוֹ:
20.en: that is made, and it is affixed into the traverse staff of the loom in the beam, the chair is impure through treading, but the traverse staff of the loom in the beam is not attached to it to be made impure through treading like it.

20.he: מִן הַכְּלוֹנָס עַצְמוֹ עָשָׂה כִסֵּא:
20.en: עשה בו כסא –from the traverse staff of the loom in the beam, he made a chair.

20.he: דְּהַיְנוּ צֹרֶךְ הַיְשִׁיבָה. וּשְׁאָר הַכְּלוֹנָס טָהוֹר:
20.en: that is, the need of the sitting. But the rest of the traverse staff of the loom in the beam is pure.

20.he: שֶׁעוֹצְרִים בָּהּ הַשֶּׁמֶן מִן הַזֵּיתִים. הַכִּסֵּא טָמֵא מִדְרָס, וְהַקּוֹרָה אֵינָהּ חִבּוּר וּטְהוֹרָה. וְאִם מֵעֵץ הַקּוֹרָה עַצְמָהּ הַכִּסֵּא עָשׂוּי בְּרֹאשָׁהּ הָאֶחָד, אַף הַכִּסֵּא טָהוֹר, דְּאוֹמְרִים לוֹ עֲמֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ. וְתַנְיָא בְתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים, אֲשֶׁר יֵשֵׁב עָלָיו יִטְמָא, יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ יֵשֵׁב עַל הָאֶבֶן וְעַל הַקּוֹרָה, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר, כְּלִי, וְלֹא אֶבֶן וְלֹא קוֹרָה. אוֹצִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ, וְלֹא אוֹצִיא כְלֵי אֲבָנִים כְּלֵי גְלָלִים כְּלֵי אֲדָמָה, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר הַכְּלִי, כְּלִי הַמְיֻחָד לְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, וְכֵלִים הַלָּלוּ אֵין מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה לְעוֹלָם. אֵין לִי אֶלָּא כִסֵּא וְסַפְסָל וְקַתֶּדְרָא הַמְיֻחָדִים לִישִׁיבָה, מִנַּיִן תֵּבַת הַבַּלָּנִים, תֵּבָה שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִצִּדָּהּ, עֲרֵבָה מִשְּׁנֵי לֹג עַד תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין שֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִרְחֹץ בָּהּ רַגְלוֹ אַחַת, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְכָל הַכְּלִי, רִבָּה. יָכוֹל אֲפִלּוּ כָפָה סְאָה וְיָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ, תַּרְקָב וְיָשַׁב עָלָיו, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אֲשֶׁר יֵשֵׁב, הַמְיֻחָד לִישִׁיבָה, לֹא שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לוֹ עֲמֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ:
20.en: that gathers/stores away the il from the olives, the chair is ritually impure through treading, but the beam is not attached and is a pure. But if from the wood of the beam itself the chair is made at one end, even the chair is pure, for we say to him: “Stand and let us do our work.” And it is taught in a Baraitha in Torat Kohanim [i.e., the Sifra, the Halakhic Midrash on the Book of Leviticus): “[Any bedding on which the one with the discharge lies shall be unclean, and every object] on which he sits shall be unclean” (Leviticus 15:4) – “it includes even one who sat on a stone or on the beam, the inference teaches us, a vessel, but not a stone nor a beam, and I will not exclude the vessels of stone, the vessels of excrement or vessels of earth, the inference teaches us the vessel, the vessel that is designated to receive impurity, but these vessels do not receive defilement ever (see Sifra Metzora, Parshat Zahav, portion 4, beginning of the seventh chapter, letter 10). I lack all other than a chair or a bench or a chair with a back/soft seat that is designated for sitting , from where is the chest of the bath attendant, a chest that opened from its side, a trough from two LOG until nine Kab that was chipped, he is unable to wash his foot in it, the inference teaches us, “and all the vessel,” which is an extension. It is possible even if he covered a Seah and sat upon it, a field requiring three Kab of seed and he sat upon it, the inference teaches us, “on which he sits” (Leviticus 15:4), that which is designated for sitting, we don’t say to him: “Stand up, and let us do our work” (see Talmud Shabbat 59a).

20.he: שֶׁיַּחְתְּכֶנָּה וִיתַקְּנֶנָּה לִישִׁיבָה. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:
20.en: that he would cut it off and establish it for sitting. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.

20.dibur: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקְּבָעָהּ בַּכֹּתֶל טְמֵאָה.
20.he: טֻמְאַת מֵת אוֹ שֶׁרֶץ. וְלֹא בָטְלָה מִתּוֹרַת כְּלִי וְלֹא אָמְרִינַן כְּלִי הַמְחֻבָּר לַקַּרְקַע כְּקַרְקַע דָּמֵי אֶלָּא כְשֶׁהָיָה מְחֻבָּר לַקַּרְקַע מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה כְדֵי לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת הַקַּרְקַע:
20.en: through defilement through a corpse or a reptile. But it is not annulled from being a vessel, and we don’t say a vessel that is attached to the ground is like the ground itself, but rather only when it was attached/connected to the ground at its outset, or that it was made in order to serve the ground.

20.he: כְּלִי הַמְיֻחָד לִישִׁיבָה, וְשֶׁל תְּמָרָה הוּא:
20.en: a vessel designated for sitting. And it is of date-palm.

20.he: בְּשׁוּרַת הַבִּנְיָן:
20.en: in the row of the building.

20.he: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהָאֻמָּנִים עוֹשִׂים שֶׁבּוֹנִים כִּפָּה עַל גַּבֵּי נְסָרִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְסִירִים אוֹתָם:
20.en: in the manner that the artisans do when building an arch/doorway over the boards and afterwards sawing them.

20.he: אִם יָשַׁב הַזָּב עַל הַבִּנְיָן שֶׁעָלָיו, נִטְמָא הַכֹּפֶת שֶׁתַּחַת הַבִּנְיָן, שֶׁהַזָּב מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּב וְאֶת הַמּוֹשָׁב שֶׁתַּחַת אֶבֶן מְסָמָא. וְכֵן כְּשֶׁקְּבָעוֹ וְלֹא בָנָה עָלָיו וְיָשַׁב הַזָּב עָלָיו כְּשֶׁהוּא קָבוּעַ, טָמֵא, דְּלֹא נִתְבַּטֵּל בְּהָכִי. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁקְּבָעוֹ וּבָנָה עָלָיו, בָּטֵל לְגַבֵּי כֹתֶל וּכְכֹתֶל דָּמֵי:
20.en: if he person with gonorrhea sat on the building that he is upon, the stool/block with a concave top to sit on that is under the building is defiled. For the person with gonorrhea defiles that which he sits upon and that which he lies upon that is under the stone used for closing a pit (which may be over a corpse). And similarly, they fixed it but did not build upon it and the person with gonorrhea sat upon it when it is fixed, it is ritually impure, but it is not nullified in this. But when he fixed it and built upon it, it is nullified in regard to the wall, and it is like a wall.

20.he: כְּמִין מַחְצֶלֶת עֲשׂוּיָה מִקָּנִים אוֹ מִגֶּמִי:
20.en: like the species of matting made from reeds or from bulrushes/reed-grass.

20.he: שֶׁל עֲלִיָּה:
20.en: of the attic.

20.he: טִיט וּצְרוֹרוֹת שֶׁל אֲבָנִים שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים עַל גַּבֵּי הַתִּקְרָה. וְכָל כַּמָּה שֶׁלֹּא קָבַע הַמַּפָּץ בַּקּוֹרוֹת וְיָשַׁב הַזָּב עַל הַמַּעֲזִיבָה, נִטְמָא הַמַּפָּץ שֶׁתַּחְתֶּיהָ וְלֹא בָטֵל מִתּוֹרַת כְּלִי, דְּאִי בָעֵי שָׁקֵיל לֵיהּ. וְכֵן אִם קְבָעוֹ וְלֹא נָתַן עָלָיו מַעֲזִיבָה וְיָשַׁב הַזָּב עָלָיו, טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב. וְלֹא בָטֵיל עַד שֶׁיִּקְבַּע וְיִתֵּן עָלָיו הַמַּעֲזִיבָה:
20.en: plaster and pebbles of stones that one places on the room. And all the while that one did not fix the mat of reeds in the walls and the person with gonorrhea sat on the concrete of stone chippings, the mat is defiled that is below it, but it is not annulled from the laws of a vessels, for if he wanted, he could take it. And similarly, if he fixed it but did not place upon it the concrete of stones and the person with gonorrhea sat upon it, it is impure from sitting. But it is not annulled until he fixes it and places the concrete of stone chippings upon it.

20.he: שׁוּלֶיהָ לְמַטָּה:
20.en: its rims below.

20.he: שׁוּלֶיהָ לְמַעְלָה:
20.en: its rims above.

20.he: שֶׁרָאוּי לִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס קָאָמַר, וְלֹא שֶׁנִּטְמָא מִדְרָס מַמָּשׁ. דְּאִם כֵּן אַדְּתָנֵי סֵיפָא אֲבָל טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת, לִתְנֵי אֲבָל טָמֵא מַגַּע מִדְרָס, כִּדְתָנֵי בְהַקּוֹמֵץ רַבָּה:
20.en: and it is appropriate to be defiled through treading, as it states, but it is not actually defiled through treading. For if so, as it is taught in the concluding section ‘of the Mishnah] “that is susceptible to uncleanness from corpse uncleanness,” let it be taught “but it is impure through contact with treading, as it is taught in the third chapter of Tractate Menahot (הקומץ רבה) [see also Tosefta Tractate Kelim Bava Metzia, Chapter 11, Halakha 9].

20.he: מָסָךְ לַפֶּתַח, אוֹ וִילוֹן לַסְּפִינָה. וְדַוְקָא שֶׁעָשָׂה בוֹ שִׁנּוּי מַעֲשֶׂה, אֲבָל מַחֲשָׁבָה אֵינָהּ מוֹצִיאַתּוּ מִידֵי טֻמְאָה שֶׁהָיוּ רְאוּיִין לָהּ:
20.en: a curtain for the opening, or a curtain for a ship. And specifically, when he made it through a change in action, but thought [alone] does not remove it from defilement that it was appropriate for it.

20.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַשַּׁמָּשׁ מִתְחַמֵּם כְּנֶגְדּוֹ וּמִתְעַטֵּף בְּשׁוּלָיו לִפְעָמִים, הִלְכָּךְ לֹא בָטֵיל מִתּוֹרַת כְּלִי:
20.en: because the sun warms it (see Talmud Betzah 14a) it (i.e., the sheet) is wrapped in its rims periodically, therefore, it is not annulled from the laws of a vessel.

20.he: שֶׁבָּטַל תּוֹרַת מִדְרָס מִמֶּנּוּ:
20.en: that the law of treading is annulled from it.

20.he: בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא מוּכָח דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי בָּעוּ שֶׁיִּקְרָעֶנּוּ וִיתַקְּנֶנּוּ לְמִדַּת הַפֶּתַח, וְיִתְפֹּר בּוֹ לוּלָאוֹת לִתְלוֹתוֹ בְמָסָךְ אוֹ בִסְפִינָה. וּבֵית הִלֵּל דְּאָמְרֵי מִשֶּׁיִּקָּשֵׁר, לֹא בָעוּ קְרִיעָה, אֶלָּא מִשֶּׁיִּקְשֹׁר בּוֹ הַלּוּלָאוֹת כְּדֵי לִתְלוֹתוֹ בָהֶם. וְאִית סְפָרִים דְּגָרְסֵי, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים מִשֶּׁיִּתָּבֵר. וְהִיא הִיא. כְּלוֹמַר מִשֶּׁיִּשְׁבְּרוּהוּ וְיִקְרָעוּהוּ כְדֵי לְתָפְרוֹ לְמִדַּת הַפֶּתַח:
20.en: In the Tosefta it is proven that the School of Shammai (see above, Tractate Kelim Bava Metzia 11:6) requires when it is torn and one fixes it to the measure of the opening, and one sews on it loops/couplings to hang it on a curtain or on a ship. But the School of Hillel states: “when he ties it up” and it doesn’t require tearing. But rather, one he ties on it the loops/couplings in order to suspend them upon them. And there are books that have the reading: “The School of Shammai states from when it is broken,” and that this is the reading, meaning to say, that when he breaks it and tears it in order to sew it to the measure of the opening.

20.he: מֵעֵת שֶׁיִּתְלֶה אוֹתוֹ עַל הַפֶּתַח אוֹ עַל הַסְּפִינָה. וַהֲלָכָה כְּבֵית הִלֵּל:
20.en: from the time that he will hang it on the opening or on the ship. And the Halakha is according to the School of Hillel.

20.he: אֹרֶךְ הַקָּנֶה לְאֹרֶךְ הַמַּחְצֶלֶת, טְהוֹרָה. דְּלֹא חַזְיָא לִשְׁכִיבָה, שֶׁהַקָּנִים מַזִּיקִין לַשּׁוֹכֵב, וְלֹא חַזְיָא כִּי אִם לְסִכּוּךְ:
20.en: the length of the reed corresponding to the length of the matting [of straw], is pure, but it is not appropriate for lying, for the reeds damage the person lying down, but they are not appropriate for anything other than interlacing.

20.he: יְוָנִית. שֶׁהִיא כְּמִין כ'‏ הֲפוּכָה שֶׁלָּנוּ. כְּלוֹמַר, לְעוֹלָם הִיא טְמֵאָה עַד שֶׁיִּמְשֹׁךְ הַקָּנִים מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה צְדָדִים. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:
20.en: the Greek [letter]. That is akin to the reverse of our [letter] "כ". Meaning to say, it is always impure until he surrounds the reeds from three sides. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.

20.he: אֹרֶךְ הַקָּנֶה לְרֹחַב הַמַּחְצֶלֶת:
20.en: the length of the reed to the width of the matting.

20.he: כְּשֶׁיֶּשׁ בֵּין קָנֶה לְקָנֶה אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים, חַזְיָא לִשְׁכַּב בֵּין שְׁנֵי הַקָּנִים:
20.en: when there is between each reed four handbreadths, it is appropriate to lie upon between the two reeds.

20.he: וְנִשְׁבְּרוּ הַקָּנִים שֶׁלָּהּ לְחֵצִי:
20.en: and its reeds were broken in-half.

20.he: דְּלֹא חַזְיָא לִשְׁכִיבָה. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
20.en: for it is not appropriate for lying. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

20.he: מִנְהַג עוֹשֵׂי מַחְצְלָאוֹת כְּשֶׁמַּשְׁלִימִין הַמַּחְצֶלֶת נִשְׁאַר כְּמִין מֶלֶל, וְגוֹדְלִים אוֹתוֹ בְכָל שְׁנֵי טְפָחִים גְּדִיל אֶחָד וְקוֹשְׁרוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִסָּתֵר הָאָרִיג. וְאִם נִתַּר עוֹמֵד לִסְתִירָה וְנִתְבַּטֵּל מִתּוֹרַת כְּלִי וּטְהוֹרָה:
20.en: it is custom of those who make matting that when they complete the mat, there remains a kind of border/hem. And they raise it in all two handbreadths a twisted thread and tie it so that the web will not be destroyed. For if it remains, it stands to be destroyed and would be annulled from the notion of being a vessel, and is pure.

20.he: קְשָׁרִים. כְּמוֹ וַיֵּלֵךְ אֵלָיו אֲגָג מַעֲדַנּוֹת (שמואל א טו), כְּלוֹמַר, קָשׁוּר כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁקּוֹשְׁרִים הָאֲסוּרִים. וְכֵן הַתְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּוֹת כִּימָה (איוב לח):
20.en: Reed matting, ties, like (I Samuel 15:32): “Agag approached him (i.e., Samuel) with faltering steps,” meaning to say, it is tied in the manner that forbidden things are tied, and similarly (Job 38:31): “Cast you tie cords to Pleiades.”

20.he: שְׁנֵי טְפָחִים בֵּין מַעֲדָן לְמַעֲדָן וְטֶפַח מִכָּאן וְטֶפַח מִכָּאן:
20.en: two handbreadths between each reed matting, and a handbreadth from here and a handbreadth from there.

20.he: מִשֶּׁיַּחְתֹּךְ וְיִקְטֹם רָאשֵׁי קְרוּמִים הַבּוֹלְטִים. וְזוֹ הִיא קְנִיבָה:
20.en: that he will sever/cut and lop off the heads of the protruding membrane, and this is cutting/trimming.

21.he: שְׁנֵי עֵצִים עֲגֻלִּים יֵשׁ לָאוֹרֵג, הָאֶחָד שֶׁחוּט הַשְּׁתִי כָּרוּךְ בּוֹ, וְהַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁלְּפָנָיו שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁאוֹרֵג וְהוֹלֵךְ כּוֹרֵךְ בּוֹ הַיְרִיעָה הַנֶּאֱרֶגֶת. וּלְפִי שֶׁהֵם כְּבֵדִים, נִקְרָאִים כֹּבֶד. וְכֹבֶד הָעֶלְיוֹן הוּא שֶׁלְּפָנָיו, וְכֹבֶד הַתַּחְתּוֹן הוּא הָרָחוֹק מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁכָּל הַשְּׁתִי כָּרוּךְ בּוֹ:
21.en: the roller on which the web is wound as it advances) is distant one from him for all the warp (longitudinal thread) is wrapped on it.

21.he: הֵן חוּטִים הָאֲרוּגִין עַל הַקָּנֶה, וּבַעֲבוּרָן מַגְבִּיהִין קְצָת הַחוּטִים וְעוֹשִׂין דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ בּוֹ הָאֶרֶג בַּחוּט:
21.en: the leashes or thrums to which the threads of the warp are attached) – they are the woven threads on the reed, and for them, they raise slightly the threads and make a path that the weaving of the thread goes.

21.he: מַסְרֵק שֶׁבּוֹ מַכִּים עַל הָאֲרִיגָה וּמְחַבְּרִים הַחוּטִים:
21.en: comb/strigil that one strikes on the weaving and fastens the threads

21.he: לְאַחַר שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂית הָרִקְמָה מְשִׂימִין חוּטִין עָלֶיהָ שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְלַכְלֵךְ, וְאוֹתָן חוּטִין לֹא הָווּ חִבּוּר לַבֶּגֶד:
21.en: after the embroidered garment is made, they place threads on it that it should not become soiled, and those threads were not attached to the cloth.

21.he: הוּא אִירָא הָאָמוּר בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְשַׁבָּת (דף יא) וְלֹא גָרְדִי בְאִירָא שֶׁבְּאָזְנוֹ. וְהִיא חֲתִיכָה קְטַנָּה מִצֶּמֶר אוֹ מִפִּשְׁתָּן אוֹ מִצֶּמֶר גֶּפֶן שֶׁאוֹרְגִים בְּתוֹךְ הַמִּטְפָּחוֹת לְנוֹי, וְזוֹרֵק אוֹתוֹ בְתוֹךְ הַשְּׁתִי וְחוּט שֶׁל עֵרֶב כָּרוּךְ בְּתוֹכָהּ, וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן שְׁחוֹרִים וַאֲדֻמִּים. וְאִם אֵינוֹ עָתִיד לְהַחֲזִירָהּ, כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִיא אֲדֻמָּה וְעַתָּה רוֹצֶה לְהַכְנִיס אִירָא שְׁחוֹרָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא פְסָקָהּ מִן הַבֶּגֶד לֹא הַוְיָא חִבּוּר:
21.en: this is the "אירא" /undyed wool or cotton that is mentioned in the first chapter of [Tractate] Shabbat [11b]: "ולא גדרי באירא שבאזנו"/nor a common weaver with undyed wool in his ear. And this is a small piece, from wool or flax or from wool of the vine that they weave within the wraps for beauty, and he throws it into the warp/longitudinal direction of the latitudinal direction/woof that is wrapped within it, and there are some of them that are black and red, and if it will not be eventually restored, such as for example that it is red and now he wants to bring in undyed black wool, and even those it has not split the cloth, there was no attachment/combination.

21.he: חוּטֵי הָעֵרֶב שֶׁהוֹלְכִים בְּתוֹךְ הַמַּסֶּכֶת כְּנֶפֶשׁ בְּתוֹךְ הַגּוּף, וְכָל דָּבָר שֶׁהָאוֹרֵג נוֹתֵן בְּתוֹךְ הַמַּסֶּכֶת לְתַקֵּן אֲרִיגָתוֹ, קָרוּי נֶפֶשׁ. וְהַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן כְּנוֹגֵעַ בַּבֶּגֶד, דַּהֲווּ חִבּוּר:
21.en: the threads of the woof/latitudinal direction that go within the warp/longitudinal direction within the body [of the garment], and every thing that the weaver places within the woof to repair his weaving is called "נפש" /the soul of the woof, and when he comes in contact with them it is coming into contact with the clothes – which is attachment.

21.he: שֶׁצָּרִיךְ עֲדַיִן לַבֶּגֶד וְעוֹמֵד לֵאָרֵג:
21.en: that he needs still for the clothing and stands to be woven.

21.he: חֲתִיכַת בֶּגֶד שֶׁתּוֹפְרִים עַל הָאַרְגָּמָן שֶׁלֹּא יִתְלַכְלֵךְ, הָוֵי חִבּוּר לַבֶּגֶד:
21.en: a piece of the cloth that they sew on the purple so that it doesn’t become soiled, it is like it is attached to the cloth.

21.he: כִּדְפָרֵישְׁנָא לְעֵיל:
21.en: as I have explained above.

21.he: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁגּוֹרְסִים הָעִימָה בְעַיִ"ן, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד. וְהוּא מַקֵּל אָרֹךְ אוֹ קָנֶה שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים כּוֹרְכוֹת בּוֹ אֶת הַצֶּמֶר וְטֹווֹת:
21.en: there are those who have the reading [of the word אימה as] עימה with an "ע" and it is all the same. And it is a long staff or a reed that the women tie up the wool and spin.

21.he: בַּצֶּמֶר שֶׁעַל הָאַשְׁוָיָא. וְאִימָּא וְאַשְׁוָיָא שְׁתֵּיהֶן לִטְווֹת עֲשׂוּיוֹת, אֶלָּא שֶׁמְּשֻׁנּוֹת זוֹ מִזּוֹ בְּצוּרָתָן:
21.en: the wool that is on the spool, and the distaff and/or the spool both of them are made for spilling, but each is different from the other in their shape/form.

21.he: דְּאֵינוֹ חִבּוּר:
21.en: for it is not attached.

21.he: כְּמִין עִגּוּל קָטָן שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ נֶקֶב, וְהַנָּשִׁים נוֹתְנוֹת אוֹתוֹ בְּרֹאשׁ הַפֶּלֶךְ לְהַכְבִּידוֹ. וְקוֹרִים לוֹ בְלַעַ"ז פוסרול"ו:
21.en: a kind of small round piece of metal that has an incision, that the women put into the top of the spindle/distaff to make it heavy, and they call it a POSROLAV in the foreign language.

21.he: קֹדֶם שֶׁיַּתִּירֶנָּה:
21.en: before releasing it.

21.he: לְאַחַר שֶׁהִתִּירָהּ:
21.en: once he released it.

21.he: מְפֹרָשׁ לְמַעְלָה פֶּרֶק כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת, שֶׁהֵן שְׁנֵי עֵצִים מִשְּׁנֵי צִדֵּי הָעֹל וְהֵן נְקוּבִים, וּמַכְנִיסִים בְּתוֹךְ אוֹתוֹ נֶקֶב עֵץ וּשְׁמוֹ קַטְרָב, וְקוֹשְׁרִים אוֹתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִשָׁמְטוּ הַבָּקָר:
21.en: it is explained above in Chapter “Metal Vessels” (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 14, Mishnah 4) which are two pieces of wood from two sides of the yoke in which incisions have been made , and they bring into this incision a piece of wood called a קטרג /cross-piece in front of yoked animals/the pin fastening the ropes of the yoke to the pole, and tie it so that the cattle will not become detached/slip away.

21.he: בֶּגֶד שֶׁל צֶמֶר אוֹ עוֹר אוֹ שַׂק שֶׁכּוֹרְכִים עַל צַוַּאר הַבְּהֵמָה, וְהָעֹל עָלָיו:
21.en: a halter of soft material) – a woolen or leather pad or sack that they tie on the neck of the animal and the yoke is upon it.

21.he: עֵץ אָרֹךְ וְעָב שֶׁבַּמַּחְרֵשָׁה, שֶׁנִּכְנָס בְּתוֹךְ הָעֹל:
21.en: the pole tied to the yoke by means of a knotted rope) – a long and thick piece of wood tha tis in the plough, that enters into the yoke.

21.he: עֵץ עָשׂוּי כִּדְמוּת חֶרֶב שֶׁתּוֹפֵס בּוֹ הַחוֹרֵשׁ:
21.en: a piece of wood made in the shape of a sword that catches in the wild-growing bushes.

21.he: עֵץ עָקֹם דּוֹמֶה לְמֶרְכָּב, וְהוּא הַנָּטוּשׁ עַל הַקַּרְקַע בְּעֵת הַחֲרִישָׁה:
21.en: a curved piece of wood similar to a saddle/handle of a saddle and it is sunk in the ground at the time of the ploughing.

21.he: עֵץ שֶׁתּוֹפֵס אוֹתוֹ הַחוֹרֵשׁ בְּיָדוֹ, וּבוֹ מַטֶּה הַמַּחְרֵשָׁה לְכָל צַד שֶׁיִּרְצֶה. וּפֵרוּשׁ יָצוּל, מַטֶּה. לֹא תַטֶּה מִשְׁפָּט (דברים טז), מְתַרְגְּמִינַן לֹא תַצְלֵי דִין:
21.en: a piece of wood that the person who ploughs holds in his hand, and he strikes the plough on each side when he wants. The explanation of – [the word] "יצול" – is a staff [as in] (Deuteronomy 16:19): “you shall not judge unfairly,” which we translate into Aramaic, “you shall not pervert the law.”

21.he: טַבַּעַת שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת:
21.en: the metal ring.

21.he: שְׁנֵי עֵצִים שֶׁבְּנִקְבֵי הָעֹל:
21.en: two pieces of wood that are in the incisions of the yoke.

21.he: עָשׂוּי כְּמִין כְּלִי שֶׁל מְסַתֵּת אֲבָנִים וּבוֹ מְשַׁבֵּר גּוּשִׁים שֶׁל עָפָר. וְקָרוּי עֲרָיִין מִלְּשׁוֹן עַרְעֵר תִּתְעַרְעַר (ירמיה נא), עָרוּ עָרוּ עַד הַיְסוֹד בָּהּ (תהלים קלז) וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁמְּטַהֵר בַּלְּחָיַיִם:
21.en: made like a kind of vessel of chiseling stones and with it breaks up clods of dirt. And it is called עריים from the language of (Jeremiah 51:58): “[Babylon’s broad wall] shall be knocked down,” (Psalms 137:7): “Strip her, Strip her to her very foundations!” But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda who declares the cheek pieces/plough guides to be pure [used to increase the soil].

21.he: בַּרְזֶל מָלֵא פְּגִימוֹת שֶׁמְּנַסְּרִים בּוֹ הַלּוּחוֹת וְהַנְּסָרִים. וּבְלַעַ"ז סיג"א. וְיֵשׁ לַמְּגֵרָה שְׁנֵי עֵצִים, אֶחָד מִצַּד זֶה וְאֶחָד מִצַּד זֶה, שֶׁבָּהֶם תּוֹפֵס חָרָשׁ עֵצִים בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמְּנַסֵּר הַלּוּחוֹת, וְהָעֵצִים הַלָּלוּ הֵן בֵּית יָד לַמְּגֵרָה. וְאִם נִטְמֵאת הַמְּגֵרָה, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן טָמֵא, דַּהֲווּ לַהּ יָדוֹת:
21.en: iron filled with notches that we saw with it the tablets and boards. And in the foreign language it is SIGA. And the saw has two pieces of wood, one from this side and another from the other side, and through them the carpenter/artisan captures wood and at the time that he saws the tablets, and these pieces of wood are a handle for the saw. But if the saw became defiled, a person who comes in contact with/touches them is impure, for they are handles to it.

21.he: בְּרֹאשׁ הָעֵצִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁהֵן בֵּית יָד, קוֹשְׁרִין חוּט וּמְשִׁיחָה וְחֶבֶל שֶׁהוֹלֵךְ עַל אֹרֶךְ הַמְּגֵרָה וּמְחַבֵּר בֵּין שְׁנֵיהֶן וּמַעֲמִידוֹ:
21.en: at the top of these pieces of wood which are handles, they tie a string or a rope or a rope’s length that goes over the length of the saw and attaches between its teeth and preserves it.

21.he: עֵץ אָרֹךְ שֶׁבְּאֶמְצַע אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנֵי עֵצִים וְהוֹלֵךְ עַל אֹרֶךְ הַמְּגֵרָה, קָרוּי אַמָּה:
21.en: a long piece of wood that is the middle of these two pieces of wood and goes throughout the length of the saw is called an אמה".”

21.he: עֵץ קָטָן נָתוּן מִן הַחוּט וְהַמְּשִׁיחָה עַד הָאַמָּה, וּבוֹ פוֹתְלִין וְגוֹדְלִין הַחוּט וְהַמְּשִׁיחָה, וְרֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד בְּתוֹךְ הַחוּט וְרֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד בָּאַמָּה. וּפְעָמִים יָשִׂים שְׁנַיִם:
21.en: a small piece of wood that is placed from the string and the rope of the saw until the crosspiece, and upon it, it twists and makes a fringe of the string and the rope of the saw, and one head is within the thread and the other is within the crosspiece, and sometimes he would put two there.

21.he: מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹ לֶחָרָשׁ עֵצִים שֶׁכּוֹבֵשׁ וְעוֹצֵר שָׁם הָעֵצִים הָעֲקוּמִים וְהַלּוּחוֹת הָעֲקֻמּוֹת וְהָעֲקֻשּׁוֹת כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְיַשְּׁרוּ, וְכֵן עוֹצֵר שָׁם הָעֵצִים וְהַנְּסָרִים שֶׁלֹּא יִתְנוֹעֲעוּ לְכָאן וּלְכָאן עַד שֶׁיְּתַקְּנֵם לִמְלַאכְתּוֹ:
21.en: it is a place that the carpenter has for wood that he presses and detains the curved pieces of wood and the curved tablets/boards and the crooked pieces in order to straighten them, and similarly, he detains there the wood and the boards that they should not move this way or that until he repairs them for his work.

21.he: כְּמִין קֶשֶׁת קָטָן שֶׁל עֵץ שֶׁתּוֹחֲבִים בּוֹ בַרְזֶל שֶׁל מַקְדֵּחַ כְּשֶׁרוֹצֶה לִקְדֹּחַ בּוֹ, וְהָאָדָם אוֹחֵז בַּקֶּשֶׁת וּמְגַלְגֵּל בּוֹ אֶת הַבַּרְזֶל. וְאִם הַבַּרְזֶל טָמֵא לֹא נִטְמָא הַקֶּשֶׁת, דְּלֹא הָוֵי חִבּוּר, שֶׁדַּרְכָּם הָיָה שֶׁלֹּא לְחַבֵּר הַקֶּשֶׁת בַּבַּרְזֶל:
21.en: like a kind of small bow of wood that they insert in it the iron of a borer when he wants to bore/penetrate into it, but when a person holds the bow and rolls the iron in it, but if the iron is impure, the bow is not defiled, for it is not considered an attachment, for it was their practice to not attach the bow to the iron.

21.he: מְגֵרָה גְדוֹלָה שֶׁעֲשׂוּיָה לְנַסֵּר קוֹרוֹת, וְעוֹשִׂים לָהּ כְּמִין מְרֻבָּע מֵעֵצִים דַּקִּים, וְהַמְּגֵרָה בָאֶמְצַע, וְאוֹתוֹ הַמְרֻבָּע קָרוּי מַלְבֵּן:
21.en: large saw that is made to saw beams, and they make it like a kind of square from thin pieces of wood and the saw is in the middle and that square is called a frame.

21.he: שֶׁאֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא מְקוֹם אֲחִיזַת בֵּית יָד בִּלְבַד. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
21.en: the part that is impure is only that of the place of the holding of the handle alone. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

21.he: חֶבֶל הַקֶּשֶׁת. לְשׁוֹן כּוֹנְנוּ חִצָּם עַל יֶתֶר (תהלים יא):
21.en: the cord of the bow. It is the language of (Psalms 11:2): “they set their arrow on the string.”

21.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַחֵץ בַּיֶּתֶר וּבַקֶּשֶׁת וּמְתוּחָה לִירוֹת בָּהּ וְנִטְמָא הַחֵץ, לֹא נִטְמָא הַקֶּשֶׁת וְהַיֶּתֶר, שֶׁאֵין הַחֵץ חִבּוּר לְקֶשֶׁת וְיֶתֶר:
21.en: even though the arrow in the bow-string and in the bow is stretched to shoot it, and the arrow is is defiled, the bow and the bow-string are not defiled, for the arrow is not connected/attached to the bow and the bow-string.

21.he: בְּרִיָּה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עֵינַיִם. הַתִּנְשֶׁמֶת מְתַרְגְּמִינַן אֵישׁוּתָא. וְצָדִין אוֹתָהּ לְפִי שֶׁמַּפְסֶדֶת אֶת הַשָּׂדוֹת:
21.en: it is a creature that has no eyes. And the owl, we translate into Aramaic as moles, and we hunt it because it destroys the fields.

21.he: שֶׁאֵינָהּ חֲשׁוּבָה כְלִי:
21.en: that it is not considered a vessel.

21.he: וְהַחֵץ שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל בָּהּ, אִם נִטְמָא הַחֵץ נִטְמֵאת הַמְּצוֹדָה. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
21.en: and an iron arrow is in it. If the arrow is defiled, the [mole] trap is defiled. Ut the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

22.he: כְּלִי עֵץ שֶׁמְּשִׂימִין בּוֹ צְלוֹחִיּוֹת וַאֲשִׁישׁוֹת וְאֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין, וּמִמֶּנּוּ נוֹטְלִין וּמְשִׂימִין עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן:
22.en: a wooden vessel that they place upon it flasks and jugs and food and liquids, and from it, they take and place it on the table.

22.he: שֶׁלֹּא נִפְחַת אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא חִפָּן. דְּאִי הֲוָה כֻּלּוֹ מְחֻפֶּה שַׁיִשׁ, הָיָה טָהוֹר כִּכְלֵי אֲבָנִים, דְּבָתַר חִפּוּי אָזְלִינַן:
22.en: which was not damaged or that was not covered [with marble], for if all it were covered with marble, it would be pure like a stone vessel, for we follow after its covering.

22.he: שֶׁל לֶחֶם וְשֶׁל בָּשָׂר. דְּאִם אֵין בַּשֻּׁלְחָן מְקוֹם הַנָּחַת חֲתִיכוֹת, לָאו שֻׁלְחָן הוּא וְלָאו דְּלֻפְקִי הוּא. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
22.en: of [pieces of] bread and meat. For if there was no place on the table for the placing of pieces [of bread and meat], it is not a table and it is not a delphica/three-legged table used as a waiter. But the Halakha Is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.

22.he: דְּלֹא חֲזִי לְשֻׁלְחָן, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לֶאֱכֹל עָלָיו:
22.en: for it is not fit as a table, for it is not appropriate to eat upon it.

22.he: שֶׁרָאוּי לֶאֱכֹל עָלָיו כְּמוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי טַבְלָא. וְהוּא שֶׁיַּחְשֹׁב לֶאֱכֹל עָלָיו:
22.en: for it is appropriate to eat upon it like on top of a board. And it is something that he would consider to eat upon.

22.he: דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁרָאוּי לֶאֱכֹל עָלָיו הֲרֵי הוּא מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה:
22.en: for since it is appropriate to eat upon it, it is susceptible to receive defilement.

22.he: דִּינוֹ כְּדִין הַשֻּׁלְחָן, וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ בַּשֻּׁלְחָן כָּךְ נֶחְלְקוּ בַּדְּלֻפְקִי. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
22.en: its law is like that of the table. And just as there was disagreement regarding a table, so there was disagreement regarding the delphica. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yossi.

22.he: דַּף רָחָב וְאָרֹךְ, בְּרֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד תָּקוּעַ מִתַּחְתָּיו דַּף גָּבֹהַּ וְכֵן בְּרֹאשׁוֹ הַשֵּׁנִי, כְּדֵי לְהַגְבִּיהּוֹ מִן הַקַּרְקַע שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רָאוּי לֵישֵׁב עָלָיו:
22.en: a wide and long board/plank, its one end/head/ is fastened with a a high board/plank and similarly its second head/end, in order to left it up from the group that it would be appropriate to sit upon.

22.he: וְלֹא דָמֵי לְשֻׁלְחָן דִּכְשֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שָׁלֹשׁ רַגְלָיו טָמֵא, דְּסַפְסָל שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ שְׁנֵי רָאשָׁיו לֹא חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה, שֶׁהַיּוֹשֵׁב עָלָיו כְּיוֹשֵׁב עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע:
22.en: for it is not similar to a table that if the removed three legs it is impure, for a bench whose two ends/heads were broken is not appropriate for sitting, for a person who sits upon it is like sitting on the ground.

22.dibur: אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ גֹבַהּ טֶפַח טָמֵא.
22.he: שֶׁהַדַּף הָעָב טֶפַח חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה:
22.en: that the board/plank is a handbreadth thick it is appropriate for sitting.

22.he: סַפְסָל לַהֲדוֹם רַגְלָיו שֶׁל אָדָם:
22.en: a bench for the footstool of a person.

22.he: דִּינוֹ כִשְׁרַפְרַף:
22.en: its law is like that of a footstool.

22.he: לְשׁוֹן חָפֵי פוֹתַחַת, כְּמִין שִׁנַּיִם יוֹצְאִים מִכָּל צַד בְּכִסֵּא שֶׁל כַּלָּה, וַעֲשׂוּיִין כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּסְמְכוּ עֲלֵיהֶן:
22.en: it is the language of covering that opens, like a kind of teeth that extend outward from all sides of the chair of the bride, and are made in order to support them.

22.he: דְּאַכַּתִּי חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה:
22.en: for they are still fit for sitting.

22.he: דְּלֹא חֲזִי לְכַלָּה, וְהָוֵי כְנִשְׁבָּר:
22.en: for they are not fit for the bride, for it is like it is broken.

22.he: כְּלוֹמַר, אַף מַלְבֵּן הַכִּסֵּא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ בְלֹא הַכִּסֵּא וּבְלֹא חִפּוּיָו טָמֵא, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁהַכִּסֵּא בְלֹא חִפּוּיָו טָמֵא. מַלְבֵּן, צוּרַת לְבֵנָה מְרֻבַּעַת עוֹשִׂים עַל הַכִּסֵּא וְיוֹשְׁבִים עָלָיו:
22.en: meaning to say, that even the frame of the chair on its own, without the seat and without its cover is impure, all the more so that he chair without its covering is impure. The frame, is the form of square brick they make on the chair and they sit upon it.

22.he: הֵבִיא כִסֵּא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וּקְבָעוֹ בַעֲרֵבָה דֶרֶךְ יְשִׁיבָתוֹ. וַעֲרֵבָה אֵינָהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, דְּחַזְיָא לְלִישָׁה:
22.en: they brought a chair from another place and affixed it in a trough in the manner of his sitting. But the trough is not impure through treading. For it is appropriate for kneading.

22.he: דְּלֹא בָטֵל כִּסֵּא לְגַבֵּי עֲרֵבָה:
22.en: for it did not annul the seat concerning the trough.

22.he: מִמִּדְרָס. דְּבָטֵל כִּסֵּא לְגַבֵּי עֲרֵבָה. אֲבָל כִּסֵּא הֶעָשׂוּי בָּעֲרֵבָה עַצְמָהּ מוֹדוּ בֵית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל דְּטָהוֹר:
22.en: [makes it pure] from [impurity through] treading, for the seat is nullified concerning the trough. But concerning a seat made in the trough itself, the School of Shammai agrees with the School of Hillel that it is pure.

22.he: אַף כִּסֵּא הֶעָשׂוּי בָּעֲרֵבָה עַצְמָהּ טָמֵא מִדְרָס:
22.en: even the sea that is made inside the trough itself is impure through treading.

22.he: שֶׁאֵין הַנְּסָרִים בּוֹלְטִים חוּץ מִן הַכִּסֵּא. שֶׁהַכִּסֵּא עָשׂוּי מֵאַרְבָּעָה עֵצִים וּנְסָרִים קְבוּעִין מִשְּׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹת הַכִּסֵּא עוֹמְדִין גְּבוֹהִים תַּחַת הָעֵצִים מְהֻדָּקִים זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה, וּמִמַּעַל לָעֵצִים לוּחוֹת עֲשׂוּיִין לֵישֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן. וְאִם נִשְׁבְּרוּ הַלּוּחוֹת הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְמוֹשָׁב, יָכוֹל לְהַטּוֹת הַכִּסֵּא לְכָל צַד שֶׁיִּרְצֶה וְלֵישֵׁב עַל אוֹתָן הַנְּסָרִים הַקְּבוּעִים בְּשָׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹת שֶׁל כִּסֵּא, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהֵן בּוֹלְטִים לַחוּץ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַטּוֹתוֹ עַל צִדּוֹ. וְחִפּוּיָו דְּהָכָא לָאו כְּחִפּוּיָו דְּרֵישָׁא שֶׁהֵן כְּמוֹ שִׁנַּיִם בּוֹלְטִים, אֶלָּא לַנְּסָרִים שֶׁמְּחַפִּין הָעֵצִים קָרֵי חִפּוּיָו:
22.en: that the boards/planks do not protrude outside of the chair. That the chair is made from four [pieces of] wood and planks fixed from three directions of the chair stands high under the wood that is fastened with each other, and from above the wood, tablets are made to sit upon them. But if the tablets are broken that are made for sitting, one can tip the chair to each side that one wishes and to sit upon those boards that are affixed from the three sides of the chair, but when they protrude outward, he is not able to tip it on its side. And the covers/seat boards mentioned here are not like the covers/seat boards mentioned in the first part of the Mishnah, for they are like protruding teeth, but rather for the boards that cover the wood are called חפויו/upholstered seat.

22.he: שֶׁנִּטַּל לוּחַ הָאֶמְצָעִי וְנִשְׁאַר לוּחַ מִכָּאן וְלוּחַ מִכָּאן:
22.en: that the middle board/tablet was removed and there remains a board from here and a board from there.

22.he: דַּחֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה:
22.en: for it is appropriate for sitting.

22.he: חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה. וְאִם לֹא, לֹא:
22.en: it would be appropriate for sitting, but if is not, it is not [appropriate for sitting].

22.he: מִלּוּחוֹת הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְמוֹשָׁב:
22.en: from the tablets that are made for sitting.

22.he: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
22.en: But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Akiba.

22.he: שֶׁהוּא חָלוּל קְצָת וְרָאוּי לְקַבֵּל רִמּוֹנִים, טָהוֹר. וְלֹא מְטַמְּאִינַן לֵיהּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל:
22.en: that is slightly hollow and appropriate to receive pomegranates is pure, and we don’t defile it because it has a receptacle.

22.he: דְּעִקָּרוֹ לִישִׁיבָה עֲבִיד וְלֹא לְבֵית קִבּוּל, וְהוֹאִיל וְנִתְבַּטֵּל הָעִקָּר שֶׁבַּעֲבוּרוֹ הָיָה חֲשׁוּב כְּלִי, בָּטְלָה הַטְּפֵלָה, וְלֹא מִטַּמֵּא מִטַּעַם שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל. וְכֵן הֲלָכָה. דְּהָכִי תְנַן לְעֵיל פֶּרֶק הַמְפָרֵק גַּבֵּי מִשְׁפֶּלֶת. וּבְפֶרֶק כָּרִים וּכְסָתוֹת גַּבֵּי חֵמֶת:
22.en: for is made for the primary purpose of sitting and not as a receptacle , for since the primary purpose was nullified, and on whose account it was considered a vessel, the secondary purpose was annulled, but it was not nullified for the reason that it has a receptacle. And this is the Halakha. And this is taught above in the chapter “Who takes apart/loosens” (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 19, Mishnah 10) and in the chapter “Mattresses and Pillows” (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 20, Mishnah 2).

22.he: עֲשׂוּיָה כְמִין אָרוֹן. וּבְשִׁדָּה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מַיְרֵי, שֶׁהִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה:
22.en: made like a kind of ark. And we are speaking of a chest that does not hold forty Se’ah, which is susceptible to receive ritual impurity.

22.he: הַכִּסּוּי שֶׁעָלֶיהָ:
22.en: the covering that is over it.

22.he: שׁוּלֶיהָ:
22.en: its rim.

22.he: וְהַדַּפִּין שֶׁבַּצְּדָדִין נִשְׁאֲרוּ:
22.en: but the planks that are on the sides remained.

22.he: וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:
22.en: And the Halakha is according to the Sages.

22.he: מְסַתֵּת אֲבָנִים. וְהוּא מְתַקֵּן לוֹ מָקוֹם לָשֶׁבֶת בְּקָצֶה הָאֶחָד מֵהָאֶבֶן כְּשֶׁמְּסַתֵּת בַּקָּצֶה הַשֵּׁנִי:
22.en: who cuts/chisels stones. And he prepares for him a place to sit on one end of the stone when he is cutting/chiseling the other end.

22.he: חֲתִיכַת עֵץ עָבָה וּרְחָבָה. וְהָכִי מַשְׁמַע פֵּרוּשׁוֹ בַתּוֹסֶפְתָּא:
22.en: a thick and wide piece of wood, and this is implied in his explanation in the Tosefta (see Tosefta Demai, Chapter 1, Halakha 11 and see also Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra, Chapter 2, Halakha 1).

22.he: צִיְּרוֹ:
22.en: which was painted.

22.he: צְבָעוֹ בְכַרְכֹּם:
22.en: which was colored with crocus/saffron.

22.he: פִּסְּלוֹ בְמַעֲצָד וְהִשְׁוָהוּ בִרְהִיטְנִי, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִרְאִים לוֹ פָנִים יָפִים:
22.en: he invalidated it with an adze and made it smooth with a tool for planning wood, that it should have a nice appearance.

22.he: דְּמוֹשָׁב הוּא:
22.en: for it is for sitting.

22.he: דְּכַחֲתִיכַת עֵץ בְּעָלְמָא חֲשִׁיב:
22.en: for it is considered like a plain piece of wood.

22.he: שֶׁיַּחְקֹק בּוֹ מְקוֹם יְשִׁיבָה:
22.en: until he hollows out a place of sitting.

22.he: מִמִּדְרָס. לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֲשׂוּיִין לִישִׁיבָה וּבָטְלָה דַעְתּוֹ אֵצֶל כָּל אָדָם:
22.en: from impurity through treading/Midras, because they are not made for sitting and knowledge of it was abolished among all people.

22.he: עַל פִּיהֶן, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁמְּסָרְגִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת:
22.en: on their openings, in the manner that they plait the beds.

22.he: דְּאֵין הַתֶּבֶן וְהַמּוֹכִין יְכוֹלִין לִפֹּל, וַחֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה:
22.en: that the straw and the hackled wool/a soft spongy substance won’t be able to fall, and they are appropriate for sitting.

22.he: בֵּית מוֹשָׁב שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל מְכֻסֶּה עוֹר, וְיוֹשְׁבִים עָלָיו בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא:
22.en: place of sitting of iron which is covered with leather, and they sit upon it in the toilet.

22.he: הָעוֹר מִן הַבַּרְזֶל:
22.en: the leather from the iron.

22.he: דְּעוֹר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה, וְהַבַּרְזֶל בְּלֹא עוֹר לֹא חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה, וַחֲזִי לִשְׁאָר תַּשְׁמִישִׁים:
22.en: that the leather by itself is appropriate for sitting, but the iron without the leather is not appropriate for sitting, but it is appropriate for other usages.

22.he: סַל קָטָן עָשׂוּי מֵעֲרָבָה קְלוּפָה, וְאוֹכְלִים עָלָיו לֶחֶם:
22.en: a small basket made from peeled willows, and they eat bread upon it.

22.he: דְּמִפְּנֵי קָטְנוֹ לֹא חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה. וְלֹא לִשְׁאָר תַּשְׁמִישִׁין, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דְפָנוֹת:
22.en: that because of its being small, it is not appropriate for sitting , and neither for the rest of the usages, for it has no walls.

22.he: שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ הֵן:
22.en: they are of marble.

22.he: אִם יָשַׁב הַזָּב עָלָיו טְמֵאִין הָרַגְלַיִם: שֶׁל עֵץ. מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב. אֲבָל הַסַּפְסָל עַצְמוֹ טָהוֹר, דִּכְלֵי אֲבָנִים אֵין לָהֶם טֻמְאָה כְלָל לֹא מִדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה וְלֹא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים:
22.en: if the person with gonorrhea sat upon it, the legs of wood are unclean because of uncleanness through sitting. But the bench itself is ritually pure, for the stone vessels have no defilement at all, neither from the words of the Torah nor from the words of the Scribes.

22.he: דַּהֲוֵי כְאִלּוּ הַסַּפְסָל כֻּלּוֹ מֵאֶבֶן:
22.en: for it is as if the bench is completely made from stone.

22.he: שֶׁפִּסְּלָן וְתִקְנָן בִּרְהִיטְנִי:
22.en: that had become unfit and were repaired with a tool to plane wood/a chisel.

22.he: וְלָאו לִישִׁיבָה עֲבִידֵי, אֲבָל בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹשְׁבִים שָׁם כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִטַּנְּפוּ מִמֵּי הַמֶּרְחֲצָאוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִים. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:
22.en: but they are not made for sitting, but people sit there in order that they not be soiled from the water of bath-houses that come out. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.

22.he: כְּלִי שֶׁמְּשִׂימִין תַּחְתָּיו אֵשׁ וְגָפְרִית כְּדֵי לְעַשֵּׁן הַבְּגָדִים שֶׁעָלָיו:
22.en: a vessel that they place fire and sulfur underneath them in order to fumigate the clothing that is upon it.

22.he: שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל לְקַבֵּל הַבְּגָדִים שֶׁעָלֶיהָ:
22.en: that it has a receptacle to receive the clothing that is upon it.

22.he: מְפֻלֶּשֶׁת מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִים:
22.en: that it is perforated from its two sides.

23.he: פלוט"א בְּלַעַ"ז:
23.en: PLOTA in the foreign language.

23.he: דְּפוּס שֶׁל מִנְעָל. וְכָל אֵלּוּ חִיצוֹנֵיהֶם עוֹר וּמְלֵאִין מִבִּפְנִים שֵׂעָר אוֹ מוֹכִין:
23.en: frame of a shoe. And all of these their outer sections are leather and they filled from the inside with hair or hackled wool/a spongy substance.

23.he: יֵשׁ בְּתוֹךְ הַבָּתִּים שֶׁל עוֹר פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת כְּתוּבוֹת בִּקְלָף:
23.en: there is within the housing of leather [Biblical] portions written on parchment.

23.he: אִם נִטְמָא אַחַת מֵאֵלּוּ בְמֵת וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרַע, וְנָגַע אֶחָד בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן, טָהוֹר, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן חִבּוּר לָהֶן וְאֵין מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן טָמֵא כְמוֹתָן:
23.en: if one of these was defiled through [contact with] a corpse and afterwards was torn, and a person came in contact with what is within them, he is ritually pure, because there isn’t any attachment with what is within them, and there isn’t anything that is within them that is ritually impure like them.

23.he: כְּמוֹ אֻכָּף:
23.en: like אוכף/saddle.

23.he: אִם נִטְמָא הָאֻכָּף בְּמֵת, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַנּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ טָמֵא, כָּךְ הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָמֵא:
23.en: if the saddle was defiled through [contact with] a corpse, just as what touches it is ritually impure, so the person who coms in contact with what is within it is also ritually impure.

23.he: וְעוֹשֵׂהוּ אֶחָד, זֶה שֶׁבִּפְנִים עִם הַחִיצוֹן:
23.en: the covering to the stuffing) – and makes it one, that which is within with the outer part.

23.he: חֲגוֹרָה רְחָבָה שֶׁבָּהּ חוֹבְשִׁים אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה. תַּרְגּוּם וַיַּחֲבֹשׁ אֶת חֲמוֹרוֹ, וְזָרֵז (בראשית כב) וּבְאַשְׁקְלוֹן עוֹשִׂים אוֹתָן שֶׁל עֵץ, וּקְרוּיִין זָרֵיז אַשְׁקְלוֹנִי עַל שֵׁם מְקוֹמָן:
23.en: a wide belt in which harness/saddle the cattle. It is the Aramaic translation of (Genesis 22:3): “And he (i.e., Abraham) saddled his ass,” and he saddled it. And in Ashkelon they make it of wood, and it is called the Ashkelonian saddle on account of their place.

23.he: מַכְתֶּשֶׁת הָעֲשׂוּיָה בְמָדַי. לוֹקְחִים חֲתִיכַת עֵץ גְּדוֹלָה עָבָה וַאֲרֻכָּה, וְחוֹקְקִים כְּמִין מַכְתֶּשֶׁת בְּאֶמְצָעָהּ, וְרוֹכְבִים עָלֶיהָ מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן וְכוֹתְשִׁים. וּלְפִיכָךְ יֵשׁ עָלָיו תּוֹרַת מֶרְכָּב:
23.en: on the protruding handles of which the pounders ride when at work) – a mortar that is made in Median. They take a large, thick, and long piece of wood, and they hollow it out/shape a receptacle in its middle, and ride upon it from here and from there and pound it/crush it. Therefore, it has upon it the law of מרכב/riding upon it.

23.he: תַּרְגּוּם בְּכַר הַגָּמָל, בַּעֲבִיטָא דְגַמְלָא (שם לא):
23.en: It is the Aramaic translation of the camel bearing for the first time, the cushion on the camel’s back (Genesis 31:34): “[Rachel, meanwhile, יhad taken the idols and placed them] In the camel cushion [and sat on them].”

23.he: אֻכָּף שֶׁעַל הַסּוּס בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה טַפֵּיטָן שְׁמוֹ, וְשֶׁל גָּמָל עָבִיט שְׁמוֹ, וְשֶׁל נָאקָה אֻכַּף שְׁמוֹ, כָּל אֶחָד שְׁמוֹ עָלָיו. וְכֻלָּן מֶרְכָּב הֵן, אֶלָּא שֶׁיֶּשׁ מֵהֶן שֶׁפְּעָמִים עֲשׂוּיִין לֵישֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן:
23.en: the saddle that is upon the horse in the language of eh Mishnah it is called טפיטן/horse-cloth, housing, and for a camel, its name is a cushion/עביט, and of a נאקה/camel it is called a saddle, each one has its name upon it. And all of them are for riding, but there are from them that sometimes they are made to sit upon them.

23.he: דְּאֵין טָמֵא מֶרְכָּב אֶלָּא הַמְיֻחָד לִרְכִיבָה בְּפִסּוּק רַגְלַיִם, וְאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לִישִׁיבָה כְלָל:
23.en: but it is not ritually impure through riding other than which is designated for riding through spreading of the feet, but it is not made for sitting at all.

23.he: שָׂדֶה שֶׁשּׂוֹחֲקִים שָׁם הַמְּלָכִים, וּרְגִילִים לָשֶׁבֶת עַל הַטַּפֵּיטָן שֶׁל סוּס לִרְאוֹת בִּשְׂחוֹק הַמֶּלֶךְ, הִלְכָּךְ טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב. קוּנְפּוֹן, שָׂדֶה, בִּלְשׁוֹן לע"ז קנפ"ו. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
23.en: because soldiers and sports stand upon it) – a field that the kings play there, and they regularly sit on the horse-cloth/housing of the horse to see the playing of the king, therefore it is impure through sitting. קונפון is a field, KANPO in the foreign tongue. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yossi.
